tra.summary: BrowserStack Test Reporting & Analytics (TRA, aka Test Observability): ingest, investigate and report on automated test runs. A build groups the test runs of one CI/SDK execution; each run carries status, logs, errors, hooks and AI root-cause analysis. Everything is scoped to a project. Read builds and runs; filter and search them; manage dashboards, custom views and saved reports; configure quality gates, webhooks, notifications, CI triggers and integrations; and read stability, performance, flakiness and unique-error analytics. Tests are REPORTED here, not executed here - execution happens in your runner or another BrowserStack product and is pushed in via the SDK. Access-key auth reaches only the /ext/v1 external API; everything else needs a session or service credential. Destructive capabilities need explicit human approval.

capabilities.name: list_ci_triggers
capabilities.intent: List the CI triggers (Jenkins, GitLab CI or custom webhook definitions) you can see in your group — your own plus any shared — for example to populate a 're-run in CI' picker on a report.
guidance: Not paginated — every trigger visible to you in the group comes back in one array under `triggers`; there is no page, count or per_page parameter.
Visibility is your own triggers plus any with isShared=true, scoped to your group. Another user's private trigger is simply absent, not an error.

No credential values here: each row carries only the booleans hasJenkinsApiToken / hasAuthToken telling you whether a token is stored. To see actual secret or credential values, use resolve_ci_trigger.
Take each trigger's `uuid` — that is the id every other trigger call needs; the integer DB id is not exposed.

capabilities.name: get_ci_trigger

path_params.name: triggerId
path_params.description: The trigger's `uuid`, not an integer id.

capabilities.intent: Fetch one CI trigger's saved configuration by its uuid — the CI tool, webhook URL and which credentials it carries — for an edit or detail view.
guidance: Addressed by the trigger `uuid` (a UUID). A trigger you cannot see (not yours and not shared) returns not-found, indistinguishable from one that truly does not exist.
Returns the configuration only — no plaintext token. hasJenkinsApiToken / hasAuthToken tell you whether credentials are stored; use resolve_ci_trigger to see their values.
The response is the trigger object at the top level (not wrapped in a `triggers` array or a `data` envelope).

capabilities.name: create_ci_trigger
capabilities.intent: Save a new CI trigger for your group: the CI tool, the webhook URL to hit, the credentials to use, and whether other group members can see it — the 'connect your CI' setup step so a build can later be fired from Test Reporting.

body.name: name
body.description: Display name. Must be non-blank and unique within your group; a duplicate raises a duplicate error.

body.name: ciTool
body.description: The CI system. Recognised values: jenkins, gitlab_ci, github_actions, circleci, travis_ci, bitbucket_pipelines, azure_devops, buildkite, teamcity, custom. Not validated against this set — an unrecognised value is stored without error but has no built-in auth/body behaviour when the trigger is later fired.

body.name: webhookUrl
body.description: The URL to call. Must be non-blank. May embed [SECRET] placeholders that are resolved at fire time.

body.name: description
body.description: Optional free-text note.

body.name: jenkinsUsername
body.description: Jenkins basic-auth user (used when ciTool=jenkins).

body.name: jenkinsApiToken
body.description: Jenkins API token. Stored only Base64-obfuscated, not encrypted, and never returned by reads. May itself be a single [SECRET] reference. Reported back only via the hasJenkinsApiToken boolean.

body.name: authToken
body.description: Generic auth token/credential for non-Jenkins tools (GitHub Actions bearer, CircleCI token, GitLab CI trigger token, etc.). Stored Base64-obfuscated, never returned. May be a single [SECRET] reference. Reported back only via the hasAuthToken boolean.

body.name: authUsername
body.description: Username paired with authToken for basic-auth tools (bitbucket_pipelines, azure_devops).

body.name: isShared
body.description: Whether other members of the group can see and fire this trigger. Defaults to false when omitted.

body.name: httpMethod
body.description: Custom-tool only (ciTool=custom): HTTP method to use; defaults to POST at fire time. Ignored for built-in tools.

body.name: requestHeaders
body.description: Custom-tool only: a JSON object of headers encoded as a STRING (not a nested object). Values may contain [SECRET] placeholders. Unparseable JSON is silently dropped (no headers sent). Ignored for built-in tools.

body.name: requestBody
body.description: Custom-tool only: raw request body; [SECRET] placeholders are substituted at fire time. Ignored for built-in tools.

body.name: contentType
body.description: Custom-tool only: Content-Type for the outbound call; defaults to application/json. Ignored for built-in tools.

guidance: name, ciTool and webhookUrl are all required and must be non-blank. A duplicate name within your group is rejected (DUPLICATE_CI_TRIGGER, 400).

The httpMethod / requestHeaders / requestBody / contentType fields take effect only when ciTool=custom; for built-in tools they are ignored. requestHeaders is a JSON object encoded as a string, not a nested JSON object.
jenkinsApiToken and authToken are stored only Base64-obfuscated (not encrypted) and are never read back — the response reports them only as the booleans hasJenkinsApiToken / hasAuthToken.
Reference a secret by putting its [UPPER_SNAKE] name in the URL, headers or body; create the secret first (create_ci_trigger_secret) or the placeholder resolves to empty when the trigger fires.
isShared defaults to false when omitted. The trigger is created enabled.
Blocked with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION in the demo-sandbox environment.
The created trigger is returned at the top level; take its `uuid` for later calls.

capabilities.name: update_ci_trigger

path_params.name: triggerId
path_params.description: The trigger's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Edit an existing CI trigger — rename it, repoint the webhook URL, switch the CI tool or custom request shape, rotate credentials, or toggle sharing.

body.name: name
body.description: Required again (non-blank) — this is a full replace, not a patch.

body.name: ciTool
body.description: Required again. See create_ci_trigger for recognised values.

body.name: webhookUrl
body.description: Required again (non-blank).

body.name: description
body.description: Overwritten with whatever you send — omit it and the stored description is cleared to null.

body.name: jenkinsUsername
body.description: Overwritten unconditionally; omit to clear.

body.name: jenkinsApiToken
body.description: EXCEPTION to the full-replace rule: a blank or omitted value leaves the stored token untouched (so a UI can submit a masked value). Send a new non-blank value to rotate it.

body.name: authToken
body.description: EXCEPTION: blank or omitted leaves the stored token untouched; a non-blank value rotates it.

body.name: authUsername
body.description: Overwritten unconditionally; omit to clear.

body.name: isShared
body.description: EXCEPTION: omitted (null) leaves the current sharing unchanged; send true/false to change it.

body.name: httpMethod
body.description: Custom-tool only; overwritten unconditionally (omit to clear).

body.name: requestHeaders
body.description: Custom-tool only; JSON object as a string; overwritten unconditionally.

body.name: requestBody
body.description: Custom-tool only; overwritten unconditionally.

body.name: contentType
body.description: Custom-tool only; overwritten unconditionally.

guidance: This is effectively a full replace, not a partial patch: name, ciTool and webhookUrl are required again, and description / jenkinsUsername / authUsername / custom-request fields are overwritten with exactly what you send — omit one and it is cleared to null. Read the trigger first and echo back every field you want to keep.

Three fields are the exception and preserve their stored value when you leave them out: a blank/omitted jenkinsApiToken or authToken keeps the existing token (masked-value submit), and an omitted isShared keeps the current sharing.
Owner-only: a group member who can merely see a shared trigger cannot edit it (FORBIDDEN_OPERATION). A trigger you cannot see returns not-found.
A duplicate name/URL is rejected (DUPLICATE_CI_TRIGGER). There is no version history — the previous configuration cannot be restored.
Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: delete_ci_trigger

path_params.name: triggerId
path_params.description: The trigger's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a CI trigger and its stored credentials from the group.
guidance: Owner-only and permanent: the webhook configuration and its stored credentials are gone, with no undo and no version history. A non-owner (even one who can see a shared trigger) is refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION; a trigger you cannot see returns not-found.
Returns {message: "Deleted"} on success.
Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: execute_ci_trigger

path_params.name: triggerId
path_params.description: The trigger's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Fire a saved CI trigger now — resolve its secret placeholders, build the tool-specific request (Jenkins buildWithParameters + basic auth, GitLab CI form body, or a fully custom method/headers/body) and call the customer's CI system — to actually kick off a build or pipeline.
guidance: Side effect outside the product: this makes a real outbound HTTP call to the customer-configured CI URL and starts a build/pipeline. There is no way to un-fire it — treat it as irreversible.

The API's own HTTP status is 200 even when the build was not queued: read the body's `isError` / `statusCode`, which reflect the REMOTE CI system, so a remote 4xx/5xx comes back as HTTP 200 wrapping statusCode>=400 and isError=true.

A disabled trigger is refused (CI_TRIGGER_DISABLED, 400). A URL rejected by the SSRF/security validator returns body statusCode 400 with a generic 'Failed to execute CI trigger' message, and any other internal failure returns body statusCode 500 with that same generic message — not the real cause.

Visible-trigger check only: any group member who can see a shared trigger can fire it, using the OWNER's stored credentials. Secret [NAME] placeholders in the URL (and, for custom tools, headers/body) are resolved at fire time; a missing secret resolves to empty.
Takes no request body. Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: resolve_ci_trigger

path_params.name: triggerId
path_params.description: The trigger's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Preview/debug what a CI trigger would actually send: the resolved webhook URL, the decoded values of the secrets it references, and its stored Jenkins/auth credentials — so a UI can show the effective request before firing it. Returns credential material.
guidance: Credential-disclosure surface: `resolvedSecrets` is a map of every referenced secret name to its DECODED plaintext value, returned to ANY caller who can see the trigger — including a non-owner viewing a shared trigger.
The trigger's own stored jenkinsApiToken and authToken are returned in plaintext ONLY to the trigger's owner; a non-owner sees null for both (but still sees the decoded resolvedSecrets).
Read-only despite being a POST: it changes no state and makes NO outbound call (unlike execute_ci_trigger). Use it to preview the effective request.
resolvedUrl has the webhook URL's [SECRET] placeholders substituted and URL-encoded. Only placeholders in the webhook URL are resolved here — execute additionally resolves custom-tool headers/body.
Takes no request body. Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: list_ci_trigger_secrets
capabilities.intent: List the CI-trigger secrets (named credentials such as a Jenkins API token) you can see in your group — your own plus any shared — each annotated with the triggers that reference it. Secret values are never returned.
guidance: Not paginated — all visible secrets come back in one array under `secrets`; there is no page/count parameter.

Values are write-only: each row is name/description/owner/isShared plus `usedInTriggers` (the NAMES of triggers whose URL, headers or body contain this secret's [NAME]). The stored value is never returned here — only resolve_ci_trigger exposes decoded values.
Visibility is your own secrets plus any with isShared=true, scoped to your group. Take each secret's `uuid` for update/delete.

capabilities.name: create_ci_trigger_secret
capabilities.intent: Store a new named secret (e.g. a Jenkins API token) that CI triggers can then reference by its [NAME] placeholder, optionally shared with the rest of the group.

body.name: name
body.description: The [NAME] token triggers reference. Required and must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]* — start with an uppercase letter, then only uppercase letters, digits and underscores. Unique within your group; a duplicate is rejected.

body.name: value
body.description: The secret value. Required and non-blank. Stored only Base64-obfuscated (not encrypted) and never returned.

body.name: description
body.description: Optional free-text note.

body.name: isShared
body.description: Whether other group members can see and use this secret. Defaults to false when omitted.

guidance: name must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]* (start uppercase, then uppercase letters/digits/underscores) — this is exactly the [NAME] token triggers reference. value is required and must be non-blank.
A duplicate name within your group is rejected (DUPLICATE_CI_SECRET, 400).
The value is stored only Base64-obfuscated, not encrypted, and is never returned — the response is the secret metadata (with an empty usedInTriggers) but no value.
isShared defaults to false. Create the secret before referencing its [NAME] in a trigger, or the placeholder resolves to empty at fire time.
Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: update_ci_trigger_secret

path_params.name: secretId
path_params.description: The secret's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Rename a CI-trigger secret, edit its description or sharing, and rotate its value in place so triggers that reference it by [NAME] keep working.

body.name: name
body.description: Required; must match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*. Renaming does NOT rewrite triggers that referenced the old name.

body.name: value
body.description: Required and non-blank (validated @NotBlank). Because it must be sent non-empty, an update ALWAYS re-sets (rotates) the stored value — there is no way through this call to keep the existing value while editing only name/description/sharing.

body.name: description
body.description: Overwritten with whatever you send.

body.name: isShared
body.description: Omitted (null) leaves sharing unchanged; send true/false to change it.

guidance: Does NOT support a value-preserving edit: `value` is validated @NotBlank, so you must send a non-empty value on every update, and the handler then always re-sets it. Every update effectively rotates the value — you cannot change only the name/description/sharing while leaving the value untouched.
name must still match ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*. Owner-only: you cannot modify another user's secret even if it is shared (FORBIDDEN_OPERATION).

Renaming does NOT rewrite triggers that referenced the old [NAME]; those placeholders silently stop resolving (they expand to empty at fire time). Update the referencing triggers too — list_ci_trigger_secrets shows which triggers use this secret.
A duplicate name is rejected (DUPLICATE_CI_SECRET). Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: delete_ci_trigger_secret

path_params.name: secretId
path_params.description: The secret's `uuid`.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a CI-trigger secret you own, provided no CI trigger still references it.
guidance: Owner-only and permanent — the value cannot be recovered. A secret owned by another user in the group is refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION even if it is shared.
Refused with CI_SECRET_IN_USE (400) if any trigger in the group still contains this secret's [NAME] placeholder; remove those references first. The error message names the secret.
Returns {message: "Deleted"} on success. Blocked in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: get_integration_score

query.name: source
query.description: Pass "INTEGRATIONS" to force a fresh recalculation of the score instead of returning the cached value. Any other value (or omitting it) returns the cached score unless it is stale.

capabilities.intent: Get this org's integration health score and the per-category breakdown (BrowserStack builds, non-BrowserStack builds, quality gate, CI/CD, PM tools, app-log recorder, communication tools, PR checks) behind the 'improve your setup' widget.
guidance: Org-wide value keyed by the caller's group, not per user. Gated by a feature flag: when the integration-score flag is off for the org this returns 403 (feature not accessible), which is a gap, not a zero score.

Classified read by intent, but it is not side-effect free: it lazily creates the org's score row when missing, and recomputes and persists the score and preferences when source=INTEGRATIONS or the cached value is older than the refresh timeout.
`preferences` is null until a score has been calculated at least once; each category object only carries the sub-fields relevant to it plus an optional notApplicable reason.
Call this at least once before trying to edit a category, because the category edit needs the score row this call creates.

capabilities.name: update_integration_score_category

query.name: category
query.description: Which score category the answer applies to. Required; omitting it is a 400 'Category is required'.

query.name: notApplicableReason
query.description: Reason this category is not applicable, removing it from the score. When OTHERS, `otherReason` becomes required.

query.name: otherReason
query.description: Free-text reason. Required only when notApplicableReason=OTHERS; omitting it then is a 400 'OtherReason is required when NotApplicableReason is OTHERS'.

query.name: cannotIntegrate
query.description: Flags that the org cannot integrate its builds. Only valid for categories BStackBuilds or NonBStackBuilds; sending it with any other category is a 400.

capabilities.intent: Record the admin's answer for one integration-score category, e.g. marking it not-applicable with a reason or flagging that the org cannot integrate its BrowserStack / non-BrowserStack builds, which removes that category from the score.
guidance: Restricted to org admins or owners, or a user with the 'Product Admin' product role; other callers get 403.
The score row must already exist: if the org has no score yet this is a 400 'Integration score not found', so read the integration score once first to create it.
The 200 body is a bare JSON boolean (`true`), not an object; there is no message or updated score in the reply, so re-read the score to see the effect.

The write is skipped silently when the submitted values match what is already stored, and it only sets/clears the category's not-applicable reason (and, for the two build categories, the cannot-integrate flag); it does not change any other category.

capabilities.name: get_integration_setup_status

query.name: tool
query.description: Which third-party tool to check. Only tools that map to an integrations-service key are accepted (Jenkins, Jira, Slack, Linear, GitHub Actions, CircleCI, GitLab CI); passing PM_TOOL, AZURE_DEVOPS or an email type errors out.

query.name: as_bot
query.description: Check the group bot's connection instead of the signed-in user's.

capabilities.intent: Tell whether a given third-party tool (Slack / a PM tool such as Jira) is fully connected for this user or the group bot, so a UI can show 'connect' vs 'connected'.
guidance: Not-connected is reported as a 200 with a null body, NOT as {"setup_completed": false}; treat a null/empty 200 as 'not set up'. Only when connected does it return {"setup_completed": true}.
An upstream authorization failure from the integrations service is swallowed and reported as not-connected (false), so a false here can mask a revoked token rather than an unfinished setup.
Always returns not-connected in the demo-sandbox environment regardless of real state.
Selecting SLACK checks the Slack configuration; any other accepted tool checks the configured PM-tool configuration.

capabilities.name: get_integration_access_token

query.name: tool
query.description: SLACK selects the Slack configuration key; any other value (or omitting it) selects the configured PM-tool key.

query.name: group
query.description: true scopes the lookup to the group and requests the bot token instead of the user's own token.

capabilities.intent: Fetch the caller's (or the group bot's) OAuth access token for a third-party tool (Slack, or the configured PM tool such as Jira) from the central integrations service, so a UI can call that integration on their behalf.
guidance: The 200 body is a JSON-encoded STRING, not a JSON object: parse the string, then read access_token / expires_at / success from the parsed value.
This response carries a live OAuth access token; treat it as a secret and do not log it.

On an upstream authorization failure it deliberately returns 200 with the string "{}" (so a frontend auth interceptor does not log the user out); an empty parsed object means not-connected, not an error.
Returns an empty-string 200 body in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: create_user_integration

path_params.name: name
path_params.description: The tool to connect (an IntegrationEnum value, matched case-insensitively). An unknown value is a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND.

body.name: username
body.description: Account username for the integration (e.g. a Jira account). Stored as-is.

body.name: authToken
body.description: The integration's auth token / API key. Effectively required: a null token causes a 500. It is base64-encoded (NOT encrypted) before being stored.

capabilities.intent: Connect a third-party tool for the signed-in user by storing the username and auth token for that integration, e.g. a Jira account or a CI token.
guidance: Fails with 400 'Integration <name> already exists' when the user already has that integration; use the update capability to change an existing connection rather than re-creating it.
The body is read flat ({username, authToken}); unknown keys are ignored silently.
The token is only base64-encoded at rest, not encrypted; reading the integration back returns it decoded to plaintext.
Per-user scope: this connects the tool only for the signed-in user, not for the whole group.
The 200 body is just {message:"Stored information successfully!"}; it does not echo the stored username or token.

capabilities.name: update_user_integration

path_params.name: name
path_params.description: The already-connected tool to update (an IntegrationEnum value, matched case-insensitively). Unknown value, or a tool the user has not connected, is a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND.

body.name: username
body.description: Replacement username for the integration.

body.name: authToken
body.description: Replacement auth token. Effectively required: a null token causes a 500. Re-encoded to base64 before storage, replacing the previous token.

capabilities.intent: Update the stored username / auth token for an integration the signed-in user has already connected, e.g. after rotating a CI token.
guidance: Only updates an existing connection: if the user has no row for this tool it is a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND, not an upsert. Use the create capability for a first-time connection.
The whole value is overwritten with the new {username, authToken}; there is no partial merge, so send both fields.
Per-user scope; does not affect other users in the group.
The 200 body is just {message:"Updated information successfully!"} and does not echo the new values.

capabilities.name: delete_user_integration

path_params.name: name
path_params.description: The tool to disconnect (an IntegrationEnum value, matched case-insensitively). Unknown value, or a tool the user has not connected, is a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.intent: Disconnect a third-party integration for the signed-in user (Jira, Slack, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, Linear, GitHub Actions, CircleCI, GitLab CI, ...), deleting the stored username and auth token.
guidance: The stored credential is deleted outright, not soft-deleted; there is no undo and it must be re-entered to reconnect.
Per-user, not per-group: it removes only the signed-in user's connection.
Both an unknown tool name and a tool the user has not connected come back as the same 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND.
The 200 body is just {message:"Deleted information successfully!"}.

capabilities.name: get_user_integration

path_params.name: name
path_params.description: The tool whose stored connection to read (an IntegrationEnum value, matched case-insensitively). Unknown value is a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.intent: Read the signed-in user's stored connection details for one third-party integration (the username and auth token) to show or prefill the integration settings form.
guidance: The returned authToken is the stored token base64-DECODED to plaintext, so this response contains a live secret; treat it as sensitive and do not log it.
When the user has no such integration the body is an empty 200 (null), not a 404; a 404 INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND means the tool name itself is unrecognised.
Per-user: it returns only the signed-in user's own credential.

capabilities.name: get_email_preferences_with_projects
capabilities.intent: Read the signed-in user's legacy email-notification settings: per email type, whether they are subscribed and which projects the type applies to. Superseded by the rule-count and detail reads for new callers.
guidance: Always operates on the authenticated user; there are no parameters.

This is the legacy shape: a map keyed by the raw email-type name, each value {isSubscribed, projects:[projectId,...]}. Only DAILY_SUMMARY_EMAIL and BUILD_FINISH_EMAIL carry a non-empty project list; other types return an empty projects array.

Differs from the rule-count read, which keys by notification-type name (DAILY_SUMMARY, BUILD_INSIGHTS, ...) and returns ruleCount instead of a project list. Do not assume the two responses share keys or shape.
Reads the user's preference row, lazily creating it if missing.

capabilities.name: get_email_preferences_with_rule_counts
capabilities.intent: Read the signed-in user's email-notification settings in the newer shape: per notification type, whether they are subscribed plus how many notification rules they have configured for it.
guidance: Always operates on the authenticated user; there are no parameters.

Map keyed by NOTIFICATION-type name (DAILY_SUMMARY, BUILD_INSIGHTS, ALERTS, WEEKLY_SUMMARY, TEST_FAILURE), each value {isSubscribed, ruleCount}. The comment-email type has no notification-type mapping, so it appears under the raw key COMMENT_EMAIL when present.
This returns a per-type ruleCount instead of the legacy project list; to get which projects and rules are enabled, use the per-project detail read.
ruleCount is 0 for a type with no configured rules; a type the user has no row for is simply absent from the map. Lazily creates the user's preference row if missing.

capabilities.name: list_users_email_subscriptions

query.name: userIds
query.description: Comma-separated list of numeric user ids to look up. A non-numeric entry is a 400 'Please specify proper user ids'.

capabilities.intent: Bulk lookup of several users' email subscription flags at once, e.g. to show which teammates are subscribed to which notification types.
guidance: Every requested user must belong to the caller's group; a single outsider fails the WHOLE call with 400 'User: <id> does not belong to this group'.
An empty result set (no such users) is a 400 'No user found', not an empty 200.

Response is a map keyed by numeric user id, each value a map of notification-type name (DAILY_SUMMARY, BUILD_INSIGHTS, ALERTS, WEEKLY_SUMMARY, TEST_FAILURE) to a subscribed boolean; the comment-email type is not included here.
Side effect: it lazily creates a missing preference row for each requested user id before returning.

capabilities.name: get_email_preference_rules_by_type

query.name: dailySummary
query.description: Include DAILY_SUMMARY rules. At least one of the four type flags should be true, or the response is the empty skeleton.

query.name: buildInsights
query.description: Include BUILD_INSIGHTS rules.

query.name: alerts
query.description: Include ALERTS rules.

query.name: testFailure
query.description: Include TEST_FAILURE rules.

query.name: legacy
query.description: Selects the legacy notification set instead of the current one.

capabilities.intent: Read the per-project detail behind the user's email settings: for the requested notification types, which projects and which notification rules are enabled, with project names resolved. This is the source of the rule ids the rule-toggle write needs.
guidance: If none of the four type flags is true it returns the empty-skeleton map (all four keys present with empty lists), not an error.

The response ALWAYS has exactly the four keys DAILY_SUMMARY, BUILD_INSIGHTS, ALERTS and TEST_FAILURE; the requested types are filled, the rest stay empty. Each entry lists per-project preferences with a projectName and an `items` array of individual rules.
Only EMAIL-notifier rules are considered; other notifier channels are not reflected here.
Take each rule's integer `id` from `items[]` (and the entry `id`): those are the ids the bulk rule-toggle write consumes.
A project whose name cannot be resolved is dropped from the result, so a missing project usually means an unresolvable project name rather than no rule.

capabilities.name: set_email_preferences_with_projects

body.name: payload
body.description: Map keyed by email-type name (e.g. DAILY_SUMMARY_EMAIL, BUILD_FINISH_EMAIL, COMMENT_EMAIL); each value is a per-type preference. Required: a null payload is a 400 'payload is required'.

fields.name: isSubscribed
fields.description: Whether the user is subscribed to this email type.

fields.name: projects
fields.description: Integer project ids this email type applies to. Project ids not listed are turned off for the type; ignored for COMMENT_EMAIL.

capabilities.intent: Save the signed-in user's legacy email-notification settings: subscribe/unsubscribe per email type and choose which projects each type applies to.
guidance: This is the legacy save; new callers should prefer the subscription-toggle, rule-toggle or per-project preference writes.
The 200 body is the plain string "Updated", not a JSON object.

Only DAILY_SUMMARY_EMAIL, BUILD_FINISH_EMAIL and COMMENT_EMAIL keys are acted on; a key that is not a known project-attribute email type is skipped silently. For non-comment types the `projects` list REPLACES the enabled-project set (unlisted projects are disabled).
No-op returning 200 "Updated" in the demo-sandbox environment.

capabilities.name: set_email_subscription_toggles

body.name: payload
body.description: Map keyed by notification-type name (DAILY_SUMMARY, BUILD_INSIGHTS, ALERTS, WEEKLY_SUMMARY, TEST_FAILURE) or COMMENT_EMAIL; each value is a toggle item. Required: a null payload is a 400 'payload is required'.

fields.name: isSubscribed
fields.description: The master on/off for this type. This is the ONLY field read by this route.

capabilities.name: list_recent_runs

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised (URL-safe) name.

query.description: Zero-based page index. Each page returns a fixed 5 builds; there is no page-size param.

query.name: source
query.description: Zero or more ProductSource values to restrict which product's runs are listed; repeat the param for a set.

capabilities.intent: List a project's most recent builds - one entry per build with its summary (name, number, status, counts) - the run picker / recent-runs list on the Testing Trends page.
guidance: SIDE EFFECT despite being a GET: this marks the project as subscribed for the calling user - a persisted user-preference write. Do not call it merely to peek at recent runs if you must avoid changing the user's subscriptions; there is no read-only variant on this route.

Takes NO date range; results are just the latest builds. Fixed page of 5 builds via the zero-based `pageNumber`; stop when `pagingParams.hasNext` is false. Here the response key is `pagingParams` (PLURAL) - unlike the leaderboards' singular `pagingParam`.
`data` is an array of full build summaries (not trend series), and `currentQGOverrideStatus` is the project's quality-gate override flag.

capabilities.name: get_group_access
capabilities.intent: Check what the caller's group is allowed to do in Test Observability / TRA — the central plan/permission (CPM) access record used to gate UI entry points and feature availability.
guidance: Takes no parameters — the group id is read from the authenticated session, so you always get the caller's own group's access, never another group's.

This is a pass-through: it relays the raw JSON from the upstream BrowserStack CPM access API unchanged, so the response shape is owned upstream, not by TRA, and can change without notice. Do not hard-code its fields.
Scoped to product test_observability specifically; it does not describe access to other BrowserStack products.

capabilities.name: list_group_teams
capabilities.intent: List the BrowserStack teams in the caller's group so team-based pickers and filters (assigning a report, scoping a dashboard to a team) can be populated.
guidance: Returns a BARE JSON array of {id, name} — not an object with a `teams` key. Each id is the BrowserStack team id.

Fails soft: any error while resolving the user/group is swallowed and an empty array is returned (never a 5xx). An empty array can therefore mean team access is disabled for the group, NOT that the group has no teams — do not conclude 'no teams' from it.
The list is also empty when team access is not enabled for the caller's user/group even though teams exist.
In demo-sandbox environments this returns canned dummy teams instead of real data.

capabilities.name: list_group_users
capabilities.intent: List every user in the caller's group in one shot to populate people pickers — @mention lists, 'run by' / owner filters, report recipients — when you want the whole roster rather than a searched page.
guidance: Returns a BARE JSON array of users, each {id, email, full_name} — not a wrapped object, and NOT the {data, pagingParams} envelope the searchable variant returns.
No pagination, search or filtering — it returns the group's entire user list every call. If you need to search, filter by product access, or page, use the searchable group-users capability instead.

Public-link aware: if a public-link token header ('Public-Link-Token' or the observability public-link header) is present and non-empty, EVERY user's email is blanked to an empty string before responding, so shared public reports get names but not addresses.
In demo-sandbox environments it short-circuits to a canned dummy user list.
If the backing rails call fails it surfaces as a raw 500 RuntimeException, not a structured error body.

capabilities.name: search_group_users
capabilities.intent: Search, filter and page through the caller's group's users — for large groups where you need to find a specific person, narrow to those with a given product's access, or fetch the roster a page at a time for owner/assignee pickers.

query.name: search
query.description: Optional substring to match users by (name/email); forwarded to the backend as-is. Omit to list without filtering.

query.name: productAccessFilter
query.description: Optional — narrows the list to users who have access to the named product. Forwarded to the backend uninterpreted, so the accepted value set is defined upstream.

query.name: perPage
query.description: Page size. Defaults to 100 when omitted. The upper bound is enforced by the upstream rails service, not here.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Cursor for the next page — pass back the `searchAfter` value from the previous response's `pagingParams`. Omit for the first page. This is a cursor, not a page number/offset.

guidance: Returns a WRAPPED object {data: [ {id, email, full_name} ], pagingParams: {hasNext, searchAfter}} — unlike the flat list variant, which returns a bare array. Read the users from `data`, not the top level.
Cursor pagination, not offset: keep calling with `searchAfter` set to the previous response's `pagingParams.searchAfter` while `pagingParams.hasNext` is true. There is no page-number parameter.
`pagingParams` is only present when the backend returned it; on the last/only page it may be absent — treat a missing `pagingParams` as 'no more pages'.
Public-link aware: if a public-link token header is present, every user's email is blanked to an empty string before responding.
In demo-sandbox environments it short-circuits to a canned dummy user list (a bare array, without the pagingParams envelope).
If the backing rails call fails it throws a raw RuntimeException surfaced as 500.

capabilities.name: list_sub_group_users
capabilities.intent: List only the users inside the caller's own sub-group (team / child org) rather than the whole group — for sharing or assignment that must stay scoped to the caller's sub-group.
guidance: Returns a BARE JSON array of users, each {id, email, full_name}. No pagination, search or filtering.

The sub-group is resolved from the caller's own user details (their subGroupId) — you cannot target another sub-group. If the caller has no sub-group, the backend is queried with a null sub-group and typically returns an empty list.
Emails are NOT blanked for public-link callers here, unlike the group-users listing — this route is not public-link aware.

Exposed unchanged at both /api/v1/users/getSubGroupUsers and /api/v2/users/getSubGroupUsers: the v2 route runs the exact same code (no pagination or search was added), so there is one capability for both.
In demo-sandbox environments it short-circuits to a canned dummy user list.
If the backing rails call fails it surfaces as a raw 500 RuntimeException.

capabilities.name: invite_users_by_email
capabilities.intent: Invite teammates to the group by email from inside TRA — sends the BrowserStack group invite plus a TRA-branded invite email carrying your message, and reports per-address success/failure.

body.name: newUsers
body.description: Email addresses of people not yet in the group. MUST be present (non-null) even if empty — the validator requires both `newUsers` and `existingUsers` to be non-null; omitting either fails validation. Each address is regex-validated; an invalid one fails the request.

body.name: existingUsers
body.description: Email addresses of people already in the group. MUST be present (non-null) even if empty. `newUsers` and `existingUsers` are merged and invited together; the split is a UI hint, not two different flows. At least one address across the two lists is required.

body.name: message
body.description: Personal message included in the invite email. Must be non-null (an empty/absent message fails validation). It is HTML/JS-escaped and Jsoup-sanitised (basic whitelist), so most markup you send is stripped.

guidance: Both `newUsers` AND `existingUsers` must be present as arrays even if one is empty, plus a non-null `message` and at least one address total — otherwise you get 400 'Need atleast one email and message for inviting new user'. Sending only `newUsers` (with `existingUsers` omitted) fails this way.

Partial success is reported as HTTP 400: the body's `message` names how many addresses could not be invited, but the others WERE invited — a 400 does not mean nothing happened. Read `message` rather than treating the status as all-or-nothing.
Addresses that were 'already invited' or 'already present' are treated as success, not failure.
A caller lacking invite rights upstream gets 400 (not 403) with 'You do not have permission to invite users...', and `invite_api_data` comes back null.
Requires an end-user session with the USER role. Side effect is external: invite emails are actually sent, so this cannot be undone by re-calling.
An unexpected backend error is flattened to 500 with a generic '...could not be invited' message.

capabilities.name: get_invite_link
capabilities.intent: Get the group's shareable 'copy invite link' so a user can invite teammates without typing email addresses.
guidance: Returns {invite_link: "<url>"}. The link is read off the caller's rails user record; if it comes back empty you get a 500 with a PLAIN STRING body (not JSON), so guard against a non-JSON error body.
Requires the USER role. If the backend refuses with 403 it is mapped to a 403 'You do not have access to generate invite link'.

The upstream status code is recovered by regex-scraping the exception message, so an unexpected error-message shape can itself cause a failure — treat any non-200 as 'link unavailable, retry/escalate' rather than parsing it.

capabilities.name: delete_user
capabilities.intent: Offboard a user from Test Observability (identity-sync callback): mark them deleted, blacklist their JWTs, unsubscribe them from all email integrations, and delete their private views.

body.name: user-id
body.description: BrowserStack user id (as a string) of the user to offboard. Sent as a JSON:API attribute under the primary `data` resource. The resource `type` is 'data-requests'. Any `data.id` you send is ignored — the handler overwrites it with a server-generated UUID — so the target is carried solely by this attribute.

guidance: IRREVERSIBLE: the user's private views are hard-deleted (not soft-deleted) and their active sessions are invalidated immediately by blacklisting their JWTs. There is no restore.

Service-to-service ONLY — the whole controller requires the SERVICE role (ObsService X-Service-API-Key or the configured service Basic client). It cannot be called from an end-user session or with a customer username + access key.
Body must be a JSON:API document; the target user is the `user-id` attribute under `data`, not a top-level field. A malformed JSON:API payload fails during conversion.
Returns {success: true} on completion; the delete work runs regardless of whether the user existed (a non-matching id simply updates zero rows).

capabilities.name: expire_user_sessions
capabilities.intent: Force-expire a user's Test Observability sessions (identity-service callback) — writes a token cut-off timestamp so any JWT issued before now is rejected. Used on logout-everywhere, password change or deactivation.

body.name: id
body.description: BrowserStack user id whose sessions to expire. Read from `data.id` DIRECTLY (a plain nested object, NOT a JSON:API attribute) — note this differs from the offboarding call, which reads a JSON:API `data.attributes.user-id`. If `data.id` is missing the request silently no-ops, writing a cut-off under a null key and still returning success.

guidance: Service-to-service ONLY — the controller requires the SERVICE role; not callable from a user session or a username + access key.
The cut-off is a Redis key with a TTL of the JWT timeout + 60s, so its effect is temporary: it stops pre-existing tokens for that window and then expires on its own.
Omitting `data.id` does NOT error — it silently no-ops (cut-off written under a null user key) and returns {success: true}. Verify you sent the id; a 200 does not prove a real user was targeted.
The id here goes at `data.id`, unlike the offboarding call which takes `data.attributes.user-id` — do not carry one shape into the other.

capabilities.name: sync_user
capabilities.intent: Push a user's profile and team membership into Test Observability (identity-sync callback) so subsequent requests resolve the user from cache without a round trip.

body.name: id
body.description: BrowserStack user id. JSON:API primary-resource id; the resource `type` is 'browserstack-users'.

body.name: email
body.description: User's email. A specific '...gdpr_forget@browserstack.com' form marks the record as GDPR-deleted.

body.name: user-product-accesses
body.description: List of product slugs the user has access to (e.g. test_observability, test_management, automate, app_automate, automate_turboscale, low_code_automation). When present, the individual per-product access booleans are DERIVED from this list and any legacy per-product boolean fields you also send are ignored.

fields.name: product_slug
fields.description: One product identifier string per array element.

body.name: team
body.description: JSON:API relationship carrying the user's BrowserStack team membership (resource type 'browserstack-teams').

guidance: Service-to-service ONLY — the controller requires the SERVICE role; not a user-facing endpoint.
Body must be a JSON:API document for a 'browserstack-users' resource (id + attributes + optional team/organization relationships). A malformed JSON:API payload fails during conversion.

This only writes a cache entry: the synced user is stored in Redis under a 1-hour TTL and returns {success: true}. It does not create or persist a user record in a database — the entry simply expires.
Prefer `user-product-accesses` (the newer list form) over the legacy per-product boolean attributes; when the list is present the booleans are derived from it and the legacy fields are dropped.

capabilities.name: list_project_webhooks

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project name or identifier; resolved to a TestHub project id before the lookup.

capabilities.intent: List the webhook rules configured on a project — use this to see each rule's name, target URL, event type and enabled state, and to get the UUID you need to read, edit, toggle or delete one.
guidance: No permission is required to list — any caller who can address the project sees its rules, unlike the create/edit/delete routes which need the webhook settings permission.

Each row is a summary only: name, uuid, url, enabled, eventType, projectSelection and projectMapping. The headers, request body and stored auth are NOT here — call get_project_webhook with the uuid for the full definition.
This is the project-scoped list; it does not return group-scoped rules. Use list_group_webhooks for those.
Not paginated — the whole set comes back in one response with no page/info envelope.

capabilities.name: get_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Required by the route but IGNORED by the lookup — the rule is found by uuid within the caller's group only, so any resolvable project name works. It does not scope or authorise the rule.

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID, from list_project_webhooks.

capabilities.intent: Fetch the full definition of one webhook rule — its event rules, target URL/method/headers/body, stored auth and re-trigger settings — e.g. to populate an edit form before updating it.
guidance: The rule is looked up by uuid scoped to the caller's group — the {projectName} in the path is not used, so passing the wrong project still returns the rule.
A uuid not present in the caller's group comes back as a not-found error (WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND), the same signal as a truly missing rule.
This response, unlike the list, includes the stored payload.auth configuration.

capabilities.name: create_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project name/identifier the rule is created under; resolved to a TestHub project id.

body.name: name
body.description: Rule name. Must be unique within the project — a duplicate returns DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK_RULE. Stored as a NOT NULL column, so an empty/absent name fails on save.

body.name: eventType
body.description: The event that fires the rule.

body.name: enabled
body.description: IGNORED on create — a new project rule is always saved enabled=true regardless of what you send. Use toggle_project_webhook afterwards to disable it.

body.name: payload
body.description: The outbound request definition. Stored NOT NULL. url is validated for SSRF and private/untrusted hosts are rejected.

fields.name: url
fields.description: Target URL. Validated — private/unresolvable/untrusted hosts are rejected.

fields.name: method
fields.description: HTTP method for the outbound call. Only POST or PUT.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Payload template mode (wire values are lowercase).

fields.name: auth
fields.description: Target auth. fields: type (noAuth|basicAuth|bearerToken), username, password, token. username and password are required when an auth object is present.

fields.name: headers
fields.description: Custom request headers, each an object {id, key, value}.

fields.name: params
fields.description: Query params, each an object {id, key, value}.

fields.name: body
fields.description: Raw request body sent to the target (arbitrary JSON).

body.name: eventRules
body.description: Condition rules that further filter the event. Each item is {id, lhs:{value}, rhs:{value:[...]}, operator}. operator is one of `is` or `matches_wildcard`. Omit for an unconditional rule.

body.name: reTrigger
body.description: Optional second payload sent on re-trigger; same shape as payload.

body.name: reTriggerEnabled
body.description: Whether re-trigger is active. Stored NOT NULL — send it (true/false).

capabilities.intent: Create a webhook rule on a project so an external system is notified when a chosen build/test event occurs — you define the event, optional match conditions, and the target URL/method/headers/body/auth.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission (modify_project_settings on PROJECT_SETTING_WEBHOOK); listing/reading does not, so being able to see rules does not mean you can create one.
Refused in the demo-sandbox environment (CANNOT_CREATE_WEBHOOK).
The `enabled` flag you send is ignored — the rule is always created enabled. Disable it with toggle_project_webhook afterwards if needed.
The success body carries only {success, uuid}; it does NOT echo the rule back. Take the uuid to address the rule later, or call get_project_webhook to read the stored form.
The target url is validated (SSRF/private-host protection) — an unreachable or private host is rejected at create time, not silently stored.
A duplicate name in the same project is rejected (DUPLICATE_WEBHOOK_RULE); names are unique per project.
projectSelection/projectMappingChanges are group-surface concepts — a project rule is scoped to this one project, so leave them out here.

capabilities.name: update_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Required by the route; the rule is located by uuid within the caller's group.

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID, from list_project_webhooks.

body.name: name
body.description: Rule name (unique per project).

body.name: payload
body.description: Full outbound request definition — same shape as create (url, method, type, auth{type,username,password,token}, headers[], params[], body). This is a full replacement, not a patch.

body.name: eventRules
body.description: Condition rules; same shape as create. Full replacement of the rule's conditions.

body.name: reTrigger
body.description: Re-trigger payload; same shape as payload.

body.name: reTriggerEnabled
body.description: Whether re-trigger is active.

body.name: enabled
body.description: Enabled state. Prefer toggle_project_webhook for a pure enable/disable.

capabilities.intent: Edit an existing project webhook rule — change its name, trigger conditions, target URL/method/headers/body, auth or re-trigger configuration.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission; refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_UPDATE_WEBHOOK).
Full replacement of the fields sent — send the COMPLETE payload definition, not a partial patch; omitted sub-fields of payload are not merged with the stored ones.
There is NO undo and no version history — the previous URL, headers, auth and conditions are gone once this returns. Read the rule first (get_project_webhook) if you need to preserve any of them.
The success body is just {success:true}; it does not return the updated rule. Re-read with get_project_webhook to confirm the stored form.
The url is re-validated on update, but a url left unchanged from what is already stored is grandfathered through even if it would now fail validation.

capabilities.name: toggle_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Required by the route but NOT used to locate or authorise the rule — the lookup is by uuid within the caller's group only.

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID.

body.name: enabled
body.description: true to resume the rule, false to pause it.

capabilities.intent: Pause or resume a webhook rule without editing or deleting it — the enable/disable switch. Use this instead of delete when you only want to stop it firing temporarily.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission; refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_UPDATE_WEBHOOK).
The rule is found by uuid scoped to the caller's group — {projectName} is ignored — and a uuid not in the group returns WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND.
Success returns a fixed {message:"Updated"} — it does not echo back the new enabled state; re-read the rule to confirm.
This is fully reversible — toggle again to restore the previous state.

capabilities.name: delete_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Required by the route; the delete is scoped by the caller's group id.

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a webhook rule from a project so it stops firing.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission; refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_DELETE_WEBHOOK).
Permanent — the rule definition (URL, headers, auth, conditions) is NOT recoverable. If you only want to stop it firing, use toggle_project_webhook to disable it instead.
Deletion is scoped by the caller's group id; the {projectName} path value does not restrict which rule is removed.
Success returns a fixed {message:"Deleted"}.

capabilities.name: test_project_webhook

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Required by the route but not used for the call itself.

body.name: url
body.description: Target URL to fire the one-off request at. Sent through an SSRF-protected HTTP client.

body.name: method
body.description: HTTP method for the test request.

body.name: auth
body.description: Target auth {type(noAuth|basicAuth|bearerToken), username, password, token}.

body.name: headers
body.description: Request headers, each {id, key, value}.

body.name: params
body.description: Query params, each {id, key, value}.

body.name: body
body.description: Raw request body sent to the target.

capabilities.intent: Fire a one-off test request at a webhook payload's target URL and return the target's status code and response body — use this to verify the endpoint, headers and auth before saving a rule.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission. Stores NOTHING in the product — but it DOES make a real outbound HTTP call to the caller-supplied URL, so side effects land on the target system. Do not treat it as read-only.

It NEVER returns a non-200 for a failed target: any failure comes back as HTTP 200 with {isError:true, statusCode:500, response:<message>}. Inspect the body's `isError`, not the HTTP status, to decide if the test passed.
statusCode/response in the body reflect the TARGET's reply (or the failure message), not this API's outcome.
The URL goes through SSRF protections (private/untrusted hosts blocked), the same as create/update.

capabilities.name: list_group_webhooks
capabilities.intent: List the group's webhook rules for the Settings > Webhooks screen — name, event type, enabled state and linked projects — searchable by name and filterable by type/status/projects.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number. OMITTING page deliberately returns the LEGACY UNPAGINATED response (all rules, no `info` block) for pre-pagination clients — so the response shape depends on whether page was sent. Send page to get the paginated shape.

query.name: pageSize
query.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 20; values above 100 are clamped to 100.

query.name: query
query.description: Name substring search.

query.name: type
query.description: Event-type filter (comma-separated event types).

query.name: status
query.description: Enabled/disabled filter (e.g. `enabled`/`disabled`). A value that is neither is treated as no status filter.

query.name: projectIds
query.description: Comma-separated project ids to filter by. A request-size bound only — unrelated to the 30-project storage cap per rule.

guidance: No @PreAuthorize, but a feature-entitlement check runs before EVERY handler on this surface: Test Management callers need the group-webhooks feature, other (TRA) callers need the webhooks feature, else FEATURE_INACCESSIBLE. Today the TRA feature is granted on all plans, so it blocks no one, but it is not the same gate as the write permission.
Response shape is conditional on `page`: WITH page you get {webhooks, info:{page,pageSize,count,prev,next}}; WITHOUT page you get just {webhooks} and no info. Do not assume `info` is present.
Rows are summaries (name, uuid, url, enabled, eventType, projectSelection, projectMapping) — fetch a single rule for headers/body/auth.
Visibility is bucketed by the X-CAD-Product-Name header (product scoping, not authorization), so which rules appear depends on the product context of the request.
This lists group-scoped rules only; project-scoped rules come from list_project_webhooks.

capabilities.name: get_group_webhook

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID, from list_group_webhooks.

capabilities.intent: Load one group webhook rule for the edit drawer — its name, event type, enabled flag, payload/re-trigger configuration and the resolved list of projects it is mapped to.
guidance: Subject to the same controller-wide feature-entitlement check as the group list; the rule must exist in the caller's group and product-visibility bucket, else WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND.

projectMapping (info + projects) is hydrated from TestHub. A rule with no mapping rows falls back to the legacy single project_id on the rule row, so a rule may show one project via projectId rather than the projects list.
Includes the stored payload.auth, unlike the list summary.

capabilities.name: create_group_webhook

body.name: name
body.description: Rule name. Stored NOT NULL.

body.name: enabled
body.description: Enabled state persisted for the new rule (stored NOT NULL).

body.name: payload
body.description: Outbound request definition — same shape as the project create (url, method[POST|PUT], type[default|custom|reuse], auth{type,username,password,token}, headers[]{key,value}, params[]{key,value}, body). url is SSRF-validated.

body.name: eventRules
body.description: Condition rules, each {id, lhs, rhs, operator(is|matches_wildcard)}.

body.name: reTrigger
body.description: Optional re-trigger payload; same shape as payload.

body.name: reTriggerEnabled
body.description: Whether re-trigger is active. Stored NOT NULL.

body.name: projectSelection
body.description: Which projects the rule applies to. OMITTING it defaults to `specific` for a group-level create (NOT the entity's own `current` default). `all` is rejected for non-Test-Management callers (WEBHOOK_ALL_PROJECTS_NOT_ALLOWED).

body.name: projectMappingChanges
body.description: Which projects to link. { addedProjects:[projectId], deletedProjects:[projectId] }. On create, addedProjects is the set to link.

body.name: source
body.description: Product source of the rule; defaults to `TO` when omitted.

capabilities.intent: Create a group-level webhook rule that can span multiple projects — you define the event, the target URL/method/headers/body/auth, an optional re-trigger payload and which projects it applies to.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission AND passes the controller-wide feature-entitlement check.
Refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_CREATE_WEBHOOK).

An omitted projectSelection defaults to `specific` here — the opposite of the stored default `current` — because a group create has no 'project it was created under'. Set it explicitly if you want a different scope.
`all` (all projects) is refused unless the caller is a Test Management caller; other callers get WEBHOOK_ALL_PROJECTS_NOT_ALLOWED.
A rule links AT MOST 30 projects — more than 30 in projectMappingChanges.addedProjects is rejected by the cap.
Success returns only {success, uuid}; it does not echo the rule. Take the uuid; read it back with get_group_webhook.
Link projects via projectMappingChanges.addedProjects (project ids), not a bare projectId — that legacy field is for single-project (project-scoped) rules.

capabilities.name: update_group_webhook

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID.

body.name: payload
body.description: Full outbound request definition — same shape as create. Full replacement, not a patch.

body.name: eventRules
body.description: Condition rules; full replacement.

body.name: reTrigger
body.description: Re-trigger payload; same shape as payload.

body.name: projectSelection
body.description: OMITTING it falls back to the rule's STORED selection (NOT the create default) — deliberately, to avoid orphaning project mappings and silently making the rule stop matching on a 200. Entering `all` is refused for non-Test-Management callers unless the rule is already `all`.

body.name: projectMappingChanges
body.description: Project link changes to apply. { addedProjects:[projectId], deletedProjects:[projectId] }.

capabilities.intent: Save edits to an existing group webhook rule — name, event type, target payload, re-trigger payload and project mapping.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission and the feature-entitlement check; the rule must be in the caller's group and product bucket, else WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND. Refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_UPDATE_WEBHOOK).

Full replacement of the fields sent — send the COMPLETE payload; there is NO undo and no version history, so the prior URL/headers/auth/conditions are lost once this returns. Read the rule first if you need them.

An OMITTED projectSelection falls back to the rule's CURRENTLY STORED value, not `current`/`specific` — this prevents silently narrowing a rule and orphaning its project mappings. To change scope, send projectSelection explicitly.
Change project links via projectMappingChanges.addedProjects/deletedProjects; the 30-project cap still applies to the resulting set.
Success is just {success:true}; re-read with get_group_webhook to confirm.

capabilities.name: toggle_group_webhook

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID.

body.name: enabled
body.description: true to enable the rule, false to disable it.

capabilities.intent: Enable or disable a group webhook rule without editing or deleting it — the on/off switch in the webhooks list.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission and the feature-entitlement check; rule must be in the caller's group/bucket. Refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_UPDATE_WEBHOOK).
Success returns a fixed {message:"Updated"} — it does not echo the new state; re-read to confirm.
Fully reversible — toggle again to restore.

capabilities.name: delete_group_webhook

path_params.name: webhookId
path_params.description: The rule's UUID.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a group webhook rule and its project mappings so it stops firing.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission and the feature-entitlement check; the rule must belong to the caller's group and product bucket. Refused in demo-sandbox (CANNOT_DELETE_WEBHOOK).
Permanent — removes the rule AND its project mappings, and none of it is recoverable. Use toggle_group_webhook to disable instead if you only want to pause it.
Success returns a fixed {message:"Deleted"}.

capabilities.name: test_group_webhook

body.name: url
body.description: Target URL to fire the one-off request at. Sent through an SSRF-protected HTTP client.

body.name: auth
body.description: Target auth {type(noAuth|basicAuth|bearerToken), username, password, token}.

body.name: headers
body.description: Request headers, each {id, key, value}.

body.name: params
body.description: Query params, each {id, key, value}.

body.name: body
body.description: Raw request body sent to the target.

capabilities.intent: Fire the user's configured webhook request (URL, method, headers, params, auth, body) once against the real target and return its status and response body — the 'Test webhook' button, to verify the endpoint before saving.
guidance: Requires the webhook settings permission and the feature-entitlement check. Stores nothing, but makes a REAL outbound HTTP call to the caller-supplied URL — side effects land on the target system, so it is not read-only.
NEVER returns a non-200 for a failed target: failures come back as HTTP 200 with {isError:true, statusCode:500, response:<message>}. Check the body's `isError`, not the HTTP status.
statusCode/response reflect the TARGET's reply, not this API's outcome. The URL goes through SSRF protections.

capabilities.name: list_group_webhook_projects
capabilities.intent: List the group's TCM/TO projects for the webhook editor's project picker — a paginated, searchable, sortable list that marks the projects already linked to a given webhook.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number (required). Page size is fixed at 30 and is NOT caller-controllable — there is no perPage/pageSize parameter here.

query.name: sortBy
query.description: Sort token for the project list.

query.name: webhookId
query.description: When supplied, each returned project's `isSelected` flags whether it is already linked to this rule; the rule must exist in the caller's group and product bucket.

query.name: search
query.description: Project name substring filter.

guidance: Subject to the controller-wide feature-entitlement check. When webhookId is passed, the rule must be in the caller's group/bucket or it is not found.
Page size is HARDCODED to 30 and the product source is HARDCODED to `TCM,TO` — neither can be changed by the caller; there is no perPage parameter. Walk pages via info.next.
Each project carries `isSelected`, true when it is already linked to the webhookId you passed — that is how the picker pre-checks linked projects.
Response is nested under projectMapping:{info, projects}; info here is the project-picker PaginationInfo (totalProjectsCount/linkedProjectsCount), distinct from the rule-list info block.

capabilities.name: get_ai_session_token
capabilities.intent: Bootstrap AI features for the current session — get a short-lived AI-service token plus the tenant's enabled AI features, opt-in-consent flag and test-failure-analysis enablement. Call this before showing any AI affordance.

body.name: is_pipeline_request
body.description: When true AND the group has AI test-failure-analysis disabled, the call short-circuits with an empty jwt_token, an empty enabled_features array and ai_opt_in_consent=false (the aiTFA block is still populated). Omit it (or send false) for interactive UI calls.

guidance: The whole body is optional — an empty POST is valid and is the common case.
This is a read: it mints a token but changes no product state, and many other AI endpoints call it internally, so treat it as a hot, side-effect-free bootstrap.

A null response from the upstream AI service is treated as consent declined, not an error: you get 200 with enabled_features=[] and ai_opt_in_consent=false. Read those fields, do not infer from the status code.

ai_opt_in_consent is the group-level opt-in; ai_enabled is the separate per-user override and is null when the user has no explicit override (only an explicit false disables). Check both before enabling an AI action for a user.
In a demo-sandbox environment a canned token ("demo-token") with consent true is returned regardless of real flags.

capabilities.name: get_rca_context_attachment_download_url

query.name: s3Key
query.description: The stored key of the attachment to download. Must start with confirmed-data/{groupId}/{buildId}/{testRunId}/ for this test run or it is rejected as not belonging to the run; a key containing '..' is rejected. Use a key returned by the RCA-context presign / conversation, not one you construct.

guidance: Returns { downloadUrl } — a short-lived presigned GET URL, NOT the file bytes. Fetch the URL yourself; it expires.
Tenant-scoped by construction: the key must live under this test run's confirmed-data prefix, so you cannot use it to read another run's attachment even within your group.
The test run and its build are re-resolved for the caller's group, so a foreign testRunId 404s rather than leaking.

capabilities.name: presign_build_chat_upload
capabilities.intent: Mint a presigned S3 POST for a file the user attaches in the build-level RCA chat composer, before the chat turn itself exists. Returns the upload URL, form fields, s3Key and expiry.

body.name: buildUuid
body.description: The build's uuid. It travels in the BODY, not the path — this presign route is not nested under the build. The build is resolved for the caller's group (a foreign build errors) and must pass build-level RCA eligibility.

body.name: fileName
body.description: Original file name. Non-blank.

body.name: contentType
body.description: MIME content type of the file. Non-blank; validated here.

guidance: Mints credentials only — nothing is persisted in the product here. POST the file to uploadUrl with formFields (a standard S3 browser POST), then quote the returned s3Key when the chat turn is submitted.
The object lands under an unconfirmed-build-chat prefix and is only promoted to confirmed when the turn is actually submitted; an upload never referenced is discarded.
A per-user pending-upload cap is enforced: over the limit the call is refused with UPLOAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
All three body fields are required and must be non-blank; buildUuid in particular is easy to omit because it is not in the path.

capabilities.name: presign_rca_context_upload
capabilities.intent: Mint a presigned S3 POST so the user can attach a file (log, screenshot, note) as extra context before re-running the agentic AI RCA for a failed test. Returns the upload URL, form fields and the s3Key to quote back on retrigger.

body.name: fileName
body.description: Original file name. Non-blank.

body.name: contentType
body.description: MIME content type of the file. Non-blank.

guidance: Mints credentials only — no product row is written. POST the file to uploadUrl with formFields, then pass the returned s3Key in the retrigger call's attachments to actually use it.
Only agentic (is_agentic) RCAs accept context — a non-agentic RCA is a 400. The build must also be eligible for the newer RCA generation.
The test run and build are resolved for the caller's group (foreign ids 404), and test runs older than the allowed age are rejected.
Caps apply: a per-test-run file cap and a per-user pending-upload cap, the latter refused with UPLOAD_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
The object lands under an unconfirmed-uploads prefix and is promoted only when the retrigger references its key.

capabilities.name: retrigger_rca_analysis
capabilities.intent: 'Improve analysis' — re-run the agentic AI RCA for a failed test with a user instruction and up to 3 previously presigned attachments, creating a new conversation turn. Returns the new message id (and trial quota used) so you can poll for the refreshed analysis.

body.name: instruction
body.description: Free-text instruction for the improved analysis. Max 5000 characters.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Up to 3 previously presigned attachments to include as context. Each item references a key returned by the RCA-context presign call. More than 3 is rejected.

fields.name: s3Key
fields.description: The key returned by the RCA-context presign call. Non-blank, max 512 chars.

fields.name: fileName
fields.description: Non-blank, max 200 chars.

fields.name: contentType
fields.description: Non-blank, max 100 chars.

fields.name: description
fields.description: Optional note about the attachment. Max 500 chars.

body.name: usePreferences
body.description: Whether saved code-fix / analysis preferences should be applied to this run.

body.name: webhook_url
body.description: Optional Atlas agent-callback URL. When present it rides the retrigger's metadata and the finished RCA is delivered to it. Max 2048 chars. Wire name is webhook_url.

guidance: Asynchronous: the response carries only messageId (and trialQuota.used for trial users) — the analysis itself arrives later when the AI service calls back. Poll the RCA conversation / that message id for the refreshed result.
trialQuota is present only for test-level trial users (their usage counter is incremented on success); it is omitted otherwise, so do not treat its absence as an error.
Attachments must first be presigned and uploaded via the RCA-context presign call — pass those returned s3Keys here; at most 3.
Only agentic RCAs on RCA-v2-eligible builds are accepted, the test run must be within the allowed age, and a run owned by the MCP-driven agent is refused.
There is no undo for a retrigger — it appends a new conversation turn; approve or discard the resulting turn separately.

capabilities.name: submit_ai_workflow_callback
capabilities.intent: Notify the product that an embedded Atlas AI workflow reached a terminal state, so it relays a browser nudge to the user; the browser then reads the actual result from Atlas. This is the Atlas platform's callback endpoint.

body.name: job_id
body.description: Atlas job id. Non-blank, max 64 chars, restricted to [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] (whitespace/control chars rejected). Wire name job_id.

body.name: status
body.description: Terminal status, e.g. succeeded | fallback | failed. NOT pinned to a closed set — an unknown status relays through rather than being rejected. Non-blank, max 32 chars, same [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] alphabet.

body.name: workflow
body.description: Workflow identifier. Non-blank, max 64 chars, same [A-Za-z0-9_.:-] alphabet.

body.name: product
body.description: Atlas product slug, e.g. tra. Optional, max 32 chars, same alphabet (empty string allowed).

body.name: client_ref
body.description: Caller-supplied correlation text echoed back from the initiate call. Opaque, never routed on or logged; only length-bounded (max 128 chars). Wire name client_ref.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded. Carries a Retry-After header; the bucket is hourly.

503.description: The nudge could not be relayed (Pusher failure). This is the only status the caller should retry.

guidance: Notification relay only — nothing from the payload is persisted; a success returns { status: "ok" }.

Auth is the caller's OWN per-user bearer token, NOT a shared service secret: any authenticated user of the group can reach it (it uses hasRole('USER'), unlike the SERVICE-fenced build-RCA webhooks). Do not expect to call it with a service key.

Per-user/per-group hourly rate limit: over budget returns 429 with Retry-After. Because the bucket is hourly, a caller that hits it typically exhausts retries — the browser's own read of Atlas is the recovery path.
503 (relay failed) is the ONLY status worth retrying; a 400 (unreadable/invalid envelope) or 429 should not be retried blindly.
The body is capped at 8 KiB and parsed leniently: unknown keys are ignored, but a malformed or oversized body is a quiet 400.
status is relayed verbatim and is not validated against a fixed set, so a new terminal status will pass through.

capabilities.name: create_code_fix_preference
capabilities.intent: Save AI code-fix guidance for a project + build name — a free-text instruction and/or a previously uploaded context file — which the AI code-fix feature then uses when suggesting fixes.

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Internal project id; re-resolved against the caller's group.

body.name: buildName
body.description: Build name the guidance applies to. Non-blank. Preferences are keyed by (group, project, buildName) — one row per build name.

body.name: instruction
body.description: Free-text code-fix guidance. Max 5000 characters. At least one of instruction / fileAttachments must be supplied.

body.name: fileAttachments
body.description: Context files to attach, each referencing an s3Key from the code-fix presign call. At most 1 file. At least one of instruction / fileAttachments must be supplied.

fields.name: s3Key
fields.description: Key returned by the code-fix presign call. Non-blank, max 512 chars.

fields.name: fileName
fields.description: Non-blank, max 200 chars.

fields.name: contentType
fields.description: Non-blank, max 100 chars.

guidance: Returns 201. One preference per (project, buildName): a second create for the same build name fails with CODE_FIX_PREFERENCES_ALREADY_EXIST — use the update call to change it instead.
At least one of instruction or fileAttachments is required; a body with neither is rejected. fileAttachments takes at most 1 file.
Plan-gated (403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED without the AI TFA plan) AND requires the calling user to have AI enabled individually.
Attachments must first be uploaded via the code-fix presign call; on save they are moved from the unconfirmed to the confirmed S3 prefix, and rolled back if the DB write fails.
This is recoverable in the sense that it can be re-created, but overwriting the guidance replaces the prior instruction/files — there is no revision history.

capabilities.name: delete_code_fix_preference
capabilities.intent: Remove the stored AI code-fix guidance (instruction + attached context files) for a project/build, so the AI fix feature falls back to no custom guidance.

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Internal project id; re-resolved against the caller's group.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The preference id, as returned by the get / create call.

guidance: Returns 204 No Content. Deletes the DB row AND its uploaded S3 attachments — the instruction text and files cannot be recovered.
Plan-gated (403 without the AI TFA plan). Unlike create/update it does NOT require the per-user AI-enabled check.
Get the preference id from the get-preference (or create) call; deleting by build name is not supported — you delete by numeric id.

capabilities.name: get_code_fix_preference
capabilities.intent: Fetch the saved AI code-fix guidance for one project + build name — the free-text instruction and the list of attached context files (with download URLs) the AI fix feature feeds to the model.

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Internal project id; re-resolved against the caller's group (anti-IDOR).

query.name: buildName
query.description: Build name whose guidance to fetch. Required. Preferences are keyed per build name, so this selects exactly one row.

204.description: No preference exists for that project + buildName. Empty body — NOT a 404.

guidance: Returns 204 No Content (empty body) when no preference exists for that project + buildName — do NOT expect a 404. Treat 204 as 'no guidance saved'.
