Plan-gated: 403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED if the group's plan does not include AI TFA.
Each returned file attachment carries a downloadUrl (a presigned GET, present only when resolvable); fetch that URL for the bytes.
buildName is required — there is no list-all-preferences variant on this route; you read one build name at a time.

capabilities.name: presign_code_fix_preference_upload
capabilities.intent: Step 1 of attaching a context file to AI code-fix guidance: mint a short-lived S3 presigned POST (URL + form fields + s3Key) so the browser can upload the file directly to S3, before referencing that key in create/update.

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Internal project id; re-resolved against the caller's group.

body.name: buildName
body.description: Build name the upload is scoped to. Non-blank.

body.name: fileName
body.description: Original file name. Non-blank.

body.name: contentType
body.description: MIME content type. Non-blank; file type/content-type is validated here.

guidance: Persists nothing itself — it returns an upload credential scoped to an unconfirmed S3 key under the caller's group/project, with a size cap and expiry. POST the file to uploadUrl with formFields, then reference the returned s3Key in create/update.
The upload is only kept if a later create/update references that s3Key; otherwise it is discarded.
Plan-gated (403 without AI TFA plan) AND requires the calling user to have AI enabled individually.
All three body fields are required and non-blank.

capabilities.name: get_build_accessibility_meta
capabilities.intent: Get the build-level accessibility summary header — whether auto-scan was enabled, the severity breakdown (critical/serious/moderate/minor) and the total issue count — for the strip above a build's per-test accessibility listing.

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: Build UUID. Can be silently overridden by the `run` query param — see guidance.

query.name: run
query.description: Optional test-run ids (bound from `A11yFilterParams.run`). If supplied, the FIRST entry is treated as a test-run id and the build UUID is resolved from it, OVERRIDING the path `buildId`. Send this empty/absent to honour the path build.

query.name: status
query.description: Accessibility status filter (bound from A11yFilterParams). Not used to compute the meta totals on this route.

query.name: searchQuery
query.description: Search token (bound from A11yFilterParams). Not used to compute the meta totals on this route.

guidance: This is the web/Automate accessibility shape. For App-Automate builds that have App Accessibility enabled for the group, the request is proxied to the App Accessibility service and returns a DIFFERENT body — do not assume the fields below when the build is an app build.
The `run` query param silently overrides the path `buildId`: if you pass a run id, the meta is for the build that run belongs to, not the build in the path.

The build must have finished (status FINISHED or TIMEOUT) and carry accessibility data; otherwise you get a classified accessibility error (build-not-completed / build-not-found / results-not-found), not an empty 200.
`autoEnabledBuild` and `autoEnabled` are the same value duplicated. `severityBreakdown` only carries the severities that were present, and `totalIssue` is their sum.
`reportUrl` is a deep link into the Accessibility dashboard, not an API endpoint you can call for the raw report.
The central-auth JWT (cookie or Bearer) is extracted and forwarded to the App-Accessibility proxy on the app path; a missing token there surfaces as an accessibility-service auth error.

capabilities.name: close_build
capabilities.intent: Manually close a build that is still open (e.g. a CI run that never reported completion) — marks it closed and kicks off a final quality-gate evaluation.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

body.name: close
body.description: Ignored: the handler forces `close=true` regardless of what you send. A body is still required because the endpoint declares one — send `{}`.

body.name: reCalculateQG
body.description: Ignored on this route. Unknown keys are also ignored (the body tolerates unknown properties).

guidance: Closing a build CANNOT be undone through the API — there is no reopen operation. Confirm with the user before calling.
Requires the TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_EDIT permission on the build's project; without it the call is refused with an access-denied error.
The request body is effectively ignored (the close flag is forced on); do not expect `reCalculateQG` or any other field to change behaviour. Send an empty object.
The quality-gate evaluation is asynchronous — the response is only the acknowledgement `{message:"Build Closed successfully"}`; re-read the build's quality gate afterwards to see the result.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) if the build is locked by plan fencing; build-not-found if the UUID is unknown or in another group.
Shares its backend with the recalculate-quality-gate action, distinguished only by the forced close flag.

capabilities.name: list_similar_test_runs
capabilities.intent: For the auto-analyser / unique-errors view: given a failed test run (or a set of error-cluster ids) in a build, list the other test runs with a similar failure so you can judge blast radius and treat the cluster as one issue.

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

query.name: mode
query.description: Scope of the similarity search. Required — a missing/invalid value is a 400.

query.name: testRunId
query.description: Numeric test-run id to find similars for. Optional, but at least one of `testRunId` or `clusterIds` must be present.

query.name: clusterIds
query.description: Error-cluster ids to find similars for. Optional, but at least one of `testRunId` or `clusterIds` must be present.

guidance: Send EITHER `testRunId` OR `clusterIds` (or both) — if neither is provided the call is a 400 ("Either clusterIds or TestRunId is required").
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is locked by plan fencing; this is a plan-fenced analyser feature.

`current` describes the reference run and `similar` the matched runs; each carries the run uuid plus project/build normalised names and build number so you can deep-link. `message` may explain why the list is empty.
Available on public-link-token auth (public dashboards), unlike most write routes.

capabilities.name: get_build_always_failing_stats
capabilities.intent: Get the 'always failing' tile for a build — how many of the build's tests have been failing consistently (out of the total), plus the tile's comment count — for the build insights page.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text filter over the build's tests (part of the standard build filter set). The whole FilterParamsV2 filter set is accepted here; it narrows which tests the metric counts.

query.name: status
query.description: Test status filter (standard build filter set).

query.name: folders
query.description: Folder-path filter (standard build filter set).

query.name: testTags
query.description: Tag filter (standard build filter set).

query.name: customParams
query.description: Any extra query params not bound to a named FilterParamsV2 field are collected into a customParams map and forwarded. Unknown keys are not rejected.

guidance: `count` is the always-failing test count and `meta` typically carries the total it is out of; `commentCount` is the number of comments on this tile.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.

One of a family of near-identical build tiles (flaky, new-failure, muted, defect, stability) that share this shape and differ only in the metric computed — pick the endpoint for the metric you want rather than re-filtering this one.
This is the standard build filter set: the same query params work across the tiles.

capabilities.name: get_build_authoring_report_url
capabilities.intent: Get a presigned S3 URL (plus expiry) for a build's Authoring Agent report — the artefact produced when tests were auto-authored during the run.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: Returns a presigned URL, NOT the report content — the caller must follow `presignedUrl` itself to fetch the file, and it expires at `expiresAt` (ISO-8601). This API cannot stream the report bytes.
Check first: the build summary read advertises `showAuthoringReport`; call this only when that is true, otherwise expect a report-not-found error.
Internal-only — deliberately not exposed on the external API surface.
On demo-sandbox environments this returns canned data without touching S3.

capabilities.name: get_build_ai_failure_summary
capabilities.intent: Get the AI-generated narrative of why a build failed — a summary paragraph plus the top failure themes (name, description, affected test count, failure %) and the top affected workflows.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The NUMERIC internal build id — NOT the UUID used by most other build routes. A UUID here will not resolve.

guidance: Takes the numeric build id, so it will NOT accept the UUID the sibling build endpoints use.
Fails soft: any upstream error or missing theme data returns 200 with `status: "NOT_AVAILABLE"`, `summary: null` and empty theme/workflow lists — check `status`, do not treat it as an error.
`topFailureThemes` and `topAffectedWorkflows` are each capped at 5 items.
Ownership-checked: if the build's group does not match the caller it reads as build-not-found.

capabilities.name: get_build_alerts
capabilities.intent: Get the alerts raised for a build (which configured alert rules fired, e.g. failure-rate or duration thresholds) and whether any alerts are configured for the project — for the alert banner/chips on the build page.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: `data` is the list of fired alerts (each with text, level, a CTA and a filter query); `alertsConfigured` says whether the project has any alert rules at all — an empty `data` with `alertsConfigured:false` means nothing is set up, not that the build is healthy.
Returns an empty/neutral alerts object while the build is still PENDING (alerts are evaluated after it finishes).
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.

capabilities.name: get_build_attempt_run_stats
capabilities.intent: Break a build's test results down per re-run attempt — pass/fail/skipped/unknown and workflow-status counts for attempt 1, 2, 3… (including manual runs) — so you can see how results changed across retries.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: `attempts` is one entry per attempt (label, attemptNumber, totalAttempts and status counts); `summary` is the aggregate across attempts.
The project's hooks visibility is resolved first and changes which test-run documents are counted — the same build can report different totals depending on hooks visibility.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.

capabilities.name: get_build_history
capabilities.intent: Get the trend of the recent builds of the same build name leading up to this one (per-build pass/fail counts, keys, lock state) so the build page can show how this build compares with previous runs.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text filter (standard build filter set). The whole FilterParamsV2 filter set is accepted and narrows what the trend counts.

query.name: status
query.description: Test status filter (standard build filter set).

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params not bound to a named FilterParamsV2 field are collected into a customParams map and forwarded; unknown keys are not rejected.

guidance: The window is hard-coded to the ~10 most recent builds of the same build name — there is no page size or count parameter to widen it.
`data` is a per-status series and `keys` the build labels/order along the x-axis; builds locked by plan fencing are flagged within the mapping.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the CURRENT build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.

capabilities.name: get_build_id_from_build_coordinates
capabilities.intent: Resolve a human-readable build coordinate (project name + build name + build serial number, i.e. what appears in a build URL) into the internal build id/UUID, so deep links and CI references can be turned into an API-usable handle.

query.name: projectNormalisedName
query.description: Project normalised name as it appears in the dashboard URL.

query.name: buildNormalisedName
query.description: Build normalised name as it appears in the dashboard URL.

query.name: buildSerialId
query.description: Build serial number (the #N shown in the UI).

guidance: All three query params are required.
When no build matches you get a bare HTTP 404 with an EMPTY body (not a structured error object) — handle the status code, there is nothing to parse.
The lookup is scoped to the caller's group, so a build in another group reads as not-found.
Returns just `{buildId}` (the resolved UUID); use `get_build_coordinates_from_uuid` for the inverse.

404.description: No build matched the coordinates. Empty response body.

capabilities.name: get_build_coordinates_from_uuid
capabilities.intent: The inverse of the coordinate lookup: given a build UUID, get the URL-safe coordinates for it (project & build normalised names, serial id, project id/name, finished/created timestamps) so a caller holding only a UUID can construct the build's dashboard URL.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: The normalised names are URI-encoded with spaces turned into '+', so use them verbatim when building a URL — do not re-encode.
If the build's group does not match the caller the call is refused with a forbidden-operation error.
An unknown UUID returns a build-not-found error (note: an older description claimed an empty JSON object here; the current handler throws not-found — do not rely on an empty-object sentinel).
`toProjectId` is the Observability project id and `thProjectId` the TestHub project id — they are different id spaces.

capabilities.name: get_build_optimization_data
capabilities.intent: Power the Smart Test Selection / test-orchestration widget on a build: get the test-orchestration configuration, whether a builder configuration exists, and whether the test-selection model for that project+build name is still in learning mode.

query.name: uuid
query.description: Build UUID. OPTIONAL — if omitted, only the orchestration-configuration lookup runs (the model-availability part is skipped).

guidance: `uuid` is a query param, not a path segment, and is optional — omitting it still returns orchestration data.

`isLearningModeEnabled` comes from a live call to the TCS service; when TCS fails the error is swallowed and the field is left UNSET — and because the DTO omits nulls, the key can simply be ABSENT from the response. Absence means 'unknown', not 'false'.
On demo-sandbox environments the seeded 'Regression #376' build returns canned data.
Fields that are null are omitted from the body (JsonInclude NON_NULL), so treat missing keys as unset rather than false.

capabilities.name: get_build_rerun_stats
capabilities.intent: Get the flat re-run summary for a build — a list of re-run legs with per-leg pass/fail/skipped/unknown counts and totals — for the re-run section of the build page.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: This is the flat/legacy shape, computed straight from the DB by build id + group id; `retryData` is a flat list of legs with no split-build grouping and there is no aggregate `summary`.
For split or parent/child builds, or when you need the aggregate summary, use `get_split_build_rerun_stats` instead — its response shape is different and NOT a drop-in swap.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.
Hooks visibility for the project is resolved first and affects which runs are counted.

capabilities.name: get_split_build_rerun_stats
capabilities.intent: Get the split-build-aware re-run summary for a build — re-run legs grouped (with per-split breakdowns) plus an overall aggregate summary — resolved against the whole build and the Observability project id so split/parent-child builds are handled correctly.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: Use this for split or parent/child builds and project-scoped configuration — it resolves against the whole build object and the Observability project id.

The response shape differs from `get_build_rerun_stats`: `retryData` is a list of GROUPS (each with `splits` and its own `summary` and build metadata) and there is a top-level aggregate `summary`. It is NOT a drop-in swap for the flat version.
403 (plan-feature-not-allowed) when the build is plan-locked; build-not-found for an unknown UUID.
Hooks visibility for the project is resolved first and affects which runs are counted.

capabilities.name: get_build_test_filters

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: The build's UUID. If it is a leg of a split build, the parent is resolved automatically and the filter set is aggregated over the parent plus every child leg.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text search echoed back into the resolved `applied` block; part of the currently-applied test filter, not a facet type-ahead.

query.name: status
query.description: Currently-applied test status values, echoed back resolved. All the FilterParamsV2 test-listing fields are accepted here (status, priority, caseType, automationStatus, testTags, folders, owner, assignee, deviceList, osList, browserList, failureCategories, dateRange, isFlaky, isNewFailure, ...) and are returned normalised under `applied`.

query.name: priority
query.description: Applied priority ids. When any of priority / caseType / automationStatus is present the response rewrites their labels in `applied` to match the static catalogue, so read labels from the response rather than assuming them.

query.name: lastExecutedBy
query.description: Test-management user ids; max 500 entries (enforced server-side).

capabilities.intent: Get the filter panel for a build's TEST listing — the currently applied test filters resolved with labels, the static catalogue of every selectable test filter, hooks visibility, and which filters are pro-only for this workspace.
guidance: This is the filter set for the TESTS inside one build, not for the build listing — use get_build_list_filters / get_build_sidebar_filters for the builds-list facets.

`applied` is your own query echoed back in resolved form (ids turned into user/label objects); `staticFilters` is the full catalogue of selectable values keyed by filter name. Read available option values from `staticFilters`, not from `applied`.

`proFilters` lists the filter keys locked behind a paid plan; it is NON-EMPTY only for a freemium workspace (then it names keys like isFlaky, isNewFailure, isAlwaysFailing, hasPerformanceAnomaly, isMuted) and empty otherwise. Treat a key that appears here as disabled, not missing.
`hooksVisibility` is one of all / failed / beforeFailed / none and tells you how before/after hook tests are surfaced for this project.
For a split build you may pass any leg's UUID; the parent is resolved and the static filters are unioned across all legs, so the result is the same whichever leg you name.

capabilities.name: get_build_list_filters

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised-name slug. Resolved within the caller's group first, so a project in another group (or an unknown slug) returns 404.

query.name: uniqueBuildNames
query.description: Applied build-name selection, echoed back resolved. Any of the GetBuildFilterRqV2 build-list fields may be supplied as query params.

query.name: users
query.description: Applied build-owner user ids (integers), echoed back as resolved user objects (id + name).

query.name: teams
query.description: Applied team ids (integers), echoed back as resolved team objects.

query.name: frameworks
query.description: Raw framework values — branded SDK names and pass-through values like 'appium'/'selenium-4'. Sent as strings (not an enum), matched case-insensitively; use the exact value the static catalogue offers.

query.name: statuses
query.description: Applied build display-status values.

query.name: buildTags
query.description: Applied build-tag values (build-level tags).

query.name: branches
query.description: Applied git branch values.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond longs [start, end] — a size other than 2 is rejected.

query.name: tags
query.description: Test-execution tag names (distinct from buildTags); max 500 entries, and gated by a per-group flag — ignored downstream when the flag is off.

query.name: state
query.description: Build state scope; defaults to `active` when omitted.

capabilities.intent: Populate the build-listing filter bar for a project in one call — the static catalogue of selectable build filters (statuses, frameworks, build types, product sources, creation types) plus the caller's currently applied filter echoed back resolved.
guidance: `staticFilters` carries the option lists: statusList, frameworkList, types, sources, creationType — each a list of {id, value, label} option objects. `applied` is your query resolved (user/team ids to names, date range, tags, branches).
This is the PER-PROJECT filter bar (scoped by the path project) — it returns the catalogue for that project. For a cross-project, filter-narrowed facet list use the sidebar capabilities instead.

On a demo-sandbox tenant this short-circuits before any project lookup and returns a hardcoded framework/static list, so the option set there is the global master list rather than what the project actually contains.
An unknown or foreign project slug is a 404 — the project is resolved inside the caller's group.

capabilities.name: list_build_branch_filter_options

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: Project normalised-name slug, resolved within the caller's group; unknown/foreign slug returns 404.

query.name: q
query.description: Case-insensitive search prefix for the branch name. Optional — omit to get the leading matches.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Branch' filter on a project's build listing — git branch names seen in the project's builds, as {id, value, label} option objects.
guidance: Per-project, prefix-search only — it does not narrow by any other currently-applied filter. For branches present under a full applied filter across a project set, use list_sidebar_branch_filter_options.
Each option's `id`/`value` IS the branch string; send that value straight back as the branch filter selection.

capabilities.name: list_build_tag_filter_options

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: Project normalised-name slug, resolved within the caller's group; unknown/foreign slug returns 404.

query.name: q
query.description: Case-insensitive search prefix for the tag value. Optional.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Build tag' filter on a project's build listing — matching build-tag values as {id, value, label} option objects.
guidance: Per-project, prefix-search only — no other applied filter narrows the result. This handler always does a real project lookup (there is no demo-sandbox short-circuit here).
These are build-level tags. For test-execution tags, or for a tag list narrowed by an applied cross-project filter, use the sidebar tag facet.

capabilities.name: list_build_team_filter_options

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: Project normalised-name slug, resolved within the caller's group; unknown/foreign slug returns 404.

query.name: q
query.description: Case-insensitive search prefix for the team name. Optional.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Team' filter on a project's build listing — BrowserStack teams that have builds in the project, as {id, value, label} option objects.
guidance: Each option's `id` is the numeric team id (as a string) and `value`/`label` are the team name — send the id back as the team filter selection, not the name.
Per-project only; it is not narrowed by any other applied filter.

capabilities.name: list_build_user_filter_options

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: Project normalised-name slug, resolved within the caller's group; unknown/foreign slug returns 404.

query.name: q
query.description: Case-insensitive search prefix for the user name. Optional.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'User' (build owner) filter on a project's build listing — matching users as {id, value, label} option objects.
guidance: Each option's `id` is the numeric user id (as a string) and `value`/`label` are the user's name — send the id back as the user/owner filter selection.
Per-project only; it is not narrowed by any other applied filter.

capabilities.name: get_build_sidebar_filters

body.name: projects
body.description: Integer project ids the filter spans. When omitted the server falls back to a default project set for the group, so send it explicitly to scope the view.

body.name: query
body.description: Free-text search over the applied selection; echoed back in the resolved `applied` block.

body.name: users
body.description: Applied build-owner user ids (integers), returned resolved to {id, name}.

body.name: teams
body.description: Applied team ids (integers), returned resolved to team objects.

body.name: statuses
body.description: Applied build display-status values.

body.name: buildTags
body.description: Applied build-tag values.

body.name: branches
body.description: Applied git branch values.

body.name: frameworks
body.description: Raw framework values (branded SDK names and pass-through values like 'appium'/'selenium-4'); strings, matched case-insensitively.

body.name: dateRange
body.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond longs [start, end]; a size other than 2 is rejected.

body.name: assignees
body.description: Assignee tokens, each matching ^(\$none|[0-9]+)$ — the literal '$none' selects unassigned, otherwise a numeric user id. A value that does not match the pattern is a 400.

body.name: tags
body.description: Test-execution tag names; max 500 entries, gated by a per-group flag (ignored when off).

body.name: state
body.description: Build state scope; defaults to `active`.

capabilities.intent: Hydrate the build-listing sidebar filter panel across a set of projects — the caller's applied selection resolved into display objects (user/team ids to names, date range, tags, branches, statuses, build names) alongside the static option catalogue.
guidance: POST but purely read — the body is only a filter payload and nothing is written.

`applied` (a SidebarFilter: the resolved build filter plus the `projects` it was scoped to) echoes your selection resolved; `staticFilters` is the option catalogue (statusList, frameworkList, types, sources, creationType).

This is the GROUP-WIDE variant: the static framework list is the hardcoded master list, NOT the frameworks actually present in the selected projects. If you need the frameworks that really occur, treat frameworkList here as the full menu, not a presence list.
Scope with `projects`; if you leave it out you get the group's default project set rather than an error.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_branch_filter_options

body.name: projects
body.description: Integer project ids to search across. Omitted → the group's default project set.

body.name: query
body.description: Case-insensitive search text for the branch name. Optional.

body.name: statuses
body.description: Part of the currently-applied build filter that narrows which builds are considered; the full GetBuildFilterRqV2 build-list field set is accepted (users, teams, buildTags, frameworks, dateRange, state, ...).

body.name: dateRange
body.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond longs [start, end]; size other than 2 is rejected.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Branch' facet of the build-list sidebar — git branch names present in the builds matching the rest of the currently applied filter, optionally narrowed by a search string.
guidance: POST but read-only — the body is a filter, no state change.
Unlike the per-project branch list, this narrows to branches that actually occur under the whole applied filter across `projects`, and returns BARE STRINGS in `data` (not {id,value,label} objects).
Values come from an Elasticsearch terms aggregation capped at 100, so the list is a suggestion set, not a complete enumeration — narrow with `query` rather than expecting every branch back.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_build_name_filter_options

body.name: projects
body.description: Integer project ids to search across. Omitted → the group's default project set.

body.name: query
body.description: Case-insensitive search text for the build name. Optional.

body.name: statuses
body.description: Part of the applied build filter that narrows which builds are considered; the full build-list field set (users, teams, buildTags, branches, frameworks, dateRange, state, ...) is accepted.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Build name' facet of the build-list sidebar — the distinct build names present under the current filter/projects, optionally matched against a search string.
guidance: POST but read-only — body is a filter payload only.
Returns BARE STRINGS in `data`. Distinct from the shipped list_build_names capability, which is a different (paged) listing — this one is the sidebar facet's aggregation.
ES terms aggregation capped at 100 distinct names, so results are bounded, not exhaustive — use `query` to find a specific name.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_run_group_filter_options

body.name: projects
body.description: Integer project ids whose run groups to list. Omitted → the group's default project set.

body.name: query
body.description: Case-insensitive name search for the run group. Optional.

capabilities.intent: Type-ahead options for the 'Run group' (build group) facet of the build-list sidebar — the first 100 run groups of the selected projects, name-searchable.
guidance: POST but read-only. ONLY `projects` and `query` are read from the body — every other build-filter field is ignored here, so do not expect statuses/tags/dateRange to narrow the result.

Pagination is hardcoded to page 1, page size 100 and CANNOT be driven from the request: you always get at most the first 100 run groups. `info` reports paging but there is no way to fetch page 2 through this endpoint — use the per-project build-groups listing if you need to page.
`data` items are full build-group objects (id, name, description, projectId, createdBy, isClosed, timestamps, ...), not bare strings, unlike the other sidebar facets.
This facet is not available on a public dashboard link (no public-link-token auth); it needs an authenticated session or service key.

capabilities.name: list_dashboards
capabilities.intent: List the custom dashboards visible to the caller (their own plus group-shared ones) for the dashboard switcher and dashboards landing page — the source of the UUID ids the read/update/clone/delete calls need.

query.name: source
query.description: Product source to list. Defaults to TO (Test Observability). TCM (Test Management) dashboards are hidden unless this is TCM, or the group has GCD enabled.

guidance: Requires the Custom Dashboard feature entitlement; without it the call is refused (feature-inaccessible), which is not the same as an empty dashboard set.

Scheduled reports are excluded here — use list_reports for those. Visibility follows the group's enterprise-data-access (UDAC) setting and sub-group membership, not a simple owner check, so two users in one group can see different sets.
Returns each dashboard's full definition under `data[]` (widgets included), not just id/name — there is no pagination on this route.

capabilities.name: get_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Fetch one custom dashboard's definition — name, visibility level, saved global filters and full widget configuration — to render or edit the dashboard.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID (from list_dashboards).

query.name: source
query.description: Product source the dashboard belongs to. Defaults to TO.

guidance: The lookup is permission-filtered to rows the caller owns or that are group-visible, so a dashboard that exists but is not visible to the caller reads as not-found.
Returns the dashboard definition only; each widget's data is fetched separately per widget.

capabilities.name: create_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Create a new custom dashboard with its widget layout, global filters and visibility level (private vs shared with the group).

query.name: source
query.description: Product source the new dashboard belongs to. Defaults to TO.

body.name: name
body.description: Dashboard name, 1-100 characters. Checked for uniqueness within the group.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level: 1 or 2 (private vs group-shared). Values outside 1-2 are rejected.

body.name: type
body.description: Dashboard type; use `Dashboard` for an ordinary custom dashboard. Free string validated to 4-100 chars, but only the listed enum names are meaningful.

body.name: desc
body.description: Optional description. Max 100 characters (the validation message misstates the limit as 200).

body.name: filters
body.description: Global dashboard filters applied to every widget. See fields for the several keys whose wire name differs from the obvious one.

fields.name: projects
fields.description: TRA project ids (Long).

fields.name: buildName
fields.description: Build-name filter. The wire key is `buildName` (singular), NOT `buildNames`.

fields.name: branches
fields.description: Branch filter. The wire key is `branches`, NOT `branchList`.

fields.name: tcmTestPlanIds
fields.description: Test-plan ids (Long). Wire key `tcmTestPlanIds`; the legacy name `testPlanIds` is accepted as an alias for old persisted blobs.

fields.name: tags
fields.description: Test-execution tag names.

fields.name: buildTags
fields.description: Build tag names.

fields.name: folders
fields.description: Folder filter.

fields.name: users
fields.description: User ids (Long).

fields.name: teams
fields.description: Team ids (Long).

fields.name: dateRange
fields.description: Date-range filter.

fields.name: match
fields.description: Per-field AND/OR match mode map (e.g. match.tags).

body.name: widgets
body.description: Widget definitions, at the BODY ROOT (there is no `data` wrapper on the request — the inventory's `data.widgets` is wrong). Each widget's config is validated for render-safety before saving.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Client widget id, max 100 chars.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Widget title, 1-100 chars.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Widget type enum (e.g. TEST_CASE_TREND, FAILURE_RATE_BY_FOLDERS).

fields.name: config
fields.description: Widget configuration (chart/display/filter/segments options). Validated for render-safety.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: Grid layout (position/size) of the widget.

fields.name: globalFilters
fields.description: Per-widget filter overrides; wire key `globalFilters` (maps to the widget's dashboardFilters).

guidance: Widgets and filters sit at the body ROOT (`widgets`, `filters`), not under a `data` object. Widget configs are validated for render-safety; a config that would crash at render is rejected up front.
Names are unique within the group — a duplicate name is rejected.
Unlike the public-API create, this internal route does NOT normalize widget configs (e.g. it does not strip an incompatible treemap visualization override) — send a clean config.

capabilities.name: update_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Save edits to an existing dashboard — rename it, change its visibility level, or persist a new widget layout / filter set.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID to update.

body.name: name
body.description: New name, 1-100 chars.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level 1 or 2.

body.name: type
body.description: Dashboard type.

body.name: filters
body.description: Replacement global filters (same shape as create; note buildName / branches / tcmTestPlanIds wire names).

body.name: widgets
body.description: Replacement widget set at the body root (no `data` wrapper). This is a FULL replace of the layout, not a merge.

guidance: This is a FULL replace, not a patch — the whole widget/filter set you send overwrites what was stored. Omitted collections are treated as the new value, so read the dashboard first and send back everything you want to keep.
There is NO undo: dashboards keep no version history, so an overwritten layout/name/filters cannot be restored.
In demo-sandbox environments updating the default dashboard (07c9f7be-0cd7-4669-8d3d-a1adff0b2aec) is rejected with 400, and that error body's shape differs from a success body.
Unlike the public-API update, this route does NOT backfill omitted name/type/level from the stored dashboard — a null name here can trip the edit path; send the fields explicitly.

capabilities.name: delete_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a custom dashboard and its widget layout.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID to delete.

guidance: Not recoverable — the dashboard and its widget layout are gone for good; there is no bin or version history.
The delete SQL is additionally scoped to rows the caller owns or is permitted to manage, so a dashboard the caller cannot manage comes back as DASHBOARD_NOT_FOUND (404) rather than deleting.
In demo-sandbox environments deleting the seeded default dashboard (07c9f7be-0cd7-4669-8d3d-a1adff0b2aec) is rejected with 400.
Success body is the JSON object {"success": true} (rendered as a string).

capabilities.name: clone_dashboard
capabilities.intent: Duplicate an existing dashboard under a new name/visibility, copying the source dashboard's widgets and filters verbatim — the 'Duplicate dashboard' action.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: SOURCE dashboard UUID to copy from.

body.name: name
body.description: Name for the new copy, 1-100 chars, must be unique in the group.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level 1 or 2 for the copy.

guidance: Only `name` and `level` are read from the body — widgets and filters are always copied from the SOURCE dashboard, so any widgets you send are ignored.
The source dashboard's widget config is validated for render-safety before the clone is written, so a broken source can fail the clone.
The clone is owned by the caller regardless of who owned the source.

capabilities.name: list_widget_custom_field_filters
capabilities.intent: List the Test Management custom fields usable as extra filters on a test-case widget, so the widget-config panel can offer them.

path_params.name: widgetType
path_params.description: Widget type. ONLY these four are valid; any other widget type returns a 400 (BAD_REQUEST_ERROR).

query.name: page
query.description: Page number. Presence of ANY of page/per_page/search switches the response to the paginated shape (see guidance).

query.name: per_page
query.description: Page size. Passed through to Test Management's custom-fields API unchanged — no ceiling is enforced by this service.

query.name: search
query.description: Substring filter over custom-field names.

guidance: TWO response shapes from one route: omit all of page/per_page/search and you get a bare JSON ARRAY of {id, label, type, fieldType}; pass any one of them and you get the paginated object {data:[...], info:{...}} instead.
Only the four listed widget types are accepted; anything else is a 400, not an empty list.
This is a pass-through to Test Management's custom-fields API; `per_page` is forwarded without clamping, so a page ceiling cannot be assumed.

capabilities.name: resolve_dashboard_filter_names
capabilities.intent: Batch-resolve project ids and user ids to their display names, so a saved dashboard's stored filter ids can be rendered as readable chips.

body.name: projectIds
body.description: TRA project ids (Long) to resolve to names. Required key, but may be an empty array. Converted to Test Management project ids before lookup.

body.name: userIds
body.description: User ids (Long) to resolve to names. Required key, but may be an empty array.

guidance: POST but read-only — it changes nothing, it only looks names up.
Both `projectIds` and `userIds` are required keys (may be empty arrays); omitting either fails validation.

Returns {projects, users}, each a list of {id, name}. Project names come from the project repository (ids are mapped to Test Management project ids first); user names come from the user-details service.

capabilities.name: search_unique_errors
capabilities.intent: Autocomplete over unique error signatures — given a partial error string, return the top matching unique errors so a user can pick one while configuring an error-focused dashboard widget.

query.name: q
query.description: Partial error string to search for. Matched against the errors search index.

guidance: The body is a top-level JSON ARRAY of {errorClusterId, error} — there is no wrapper object.
The result count is hardcoded to 10 and cannot be paged or raised; refine `q` to narrow rather than expecting more rows.
Backed by an Elasticsearch aggregation over the errors index; `errorClusterId` is the stable id of the unique-error cluster.

capabilities.name: list_reports
capabilities.intent: Power the Reports listing page: a paginated, searchable, sortable list of saved dashboards/reports across Test Observability and Test Management, each with owner, linked projects, type and schedule frequency, plus 'my reports' and total counts.

query.name: projectIds
query.description: TRA project ids to filter by. UDAC project filtering is applied on top; if UDAC blocks every project the page comes back empty.

query.name: source
query.description: Product source. An INVALID value does not 4xx — it returns HTTP 200 with an `error` string and empty data.

query.name: type
query.description: Report/dashboard type filter.

query.name: userId
query.description: Filter to a specific owner's reports.

query.name: frequency
query.description: Schedule frequency filter.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number (1-based).

query.name: size
query.description: Page size. Clamped server-side to the range 1-100.

query.name: sortBy
query.description: Sort column. Defaults to modifiedAt.

query.name: sortOrder
query.description: Sort direction. Defaults to desc.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Free-text search. The query-parameter name is literally `q[query]`.

guidance: An invalid `source` returns HTTP 200 with a top-level `error` string and empty `data` — check `error`, not the status code.
TRA report types (Build Comparison, Tabular Test Runs) are hidden unless the group has the Custom Dashboard entitlement AND the TM-TO-reports rollout flag is on; other TM reports stay visible.
`size` is clamped to a maximum of 100 (and a minimum of 1); asking for more returns at most 100 rows.
The search parameter is spelled `q[query]`, not `q` or `query`.
`my_report_count` / `total_report_count` are separate top-level counts; pagination cursors are under `info` (page/next/prev/count/page_size).

capabilities.name: list_dashboards_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Public-API listing of the custom dashboards visible to the caller's group (used by the Atlas AI dashboard builder and API clients) to discover dashboard ids/names/widgets before reading or cloning one.

query.name: source
query.description: Product source to list. Defaults to TO.

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.
Same underlying service as the internal listing: scheduled-report dashboards are excluded and each row carries the full definition (widgets included); there is no pagination.

capabilities.name: get_dashboard_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Fetch one dashboard's full definition (name, type, level and the widget list with each widget's config) via the public API, so a client can render or edit it.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID (from list_dashboards_via_public_api).

query.name: source
query.description: Product source. Defaults to TO.

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.
Resolves the id as a dashboard (not a scheduled report).

capabilities.name: create_dashboard_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Create a new custom dashboard with its widget layout via the public API, so a client (or the AI dashboard builder) can provision a dashboard programmatically instead of building it in the UI.

query.name: source
query.description: Product source for the new dashboard. Defaults to TO.

body.name: name
body.description: Dashboard name, 1-100 chars, unique in the group.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level 1 or 2.

body.name: type
body.description: Dashboard type; use `Dashboard` for an ordinary dashboard.

body.name: desc
body.description: Optional description, max 100 chars.

body.name: filters
body.description: Global filters (same shape as the internal create; note buildName / branches / tcmTestPlanIds wire names).

body.name: widgets
body.description: Widget definitions at the body root. Each widget is {id, name, type, config, layout, globalFilters}. See guidance for the treemap normalization this surface applies.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Client widget id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Widget title.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Widget type enum.

fields.name: config
fields.description: Widget config; validated for render-safety before persist.

fields.name: layout
fields.description: Grid layout.

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.
This surface silently DROPS a `visualization` override on a treemap widget (FAILURE_RATE_BY_FOLDERS) rather than rejecting it — don't rely on that override being honoured.
It also runs render-safety validation up front, so a widget config that would 5xx at render is rejected here. The internal create does neither of these.

capabilities.name: update_dashboard_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Update an existing dashboard's name/type/level and replace its widget set via the public API.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID to update.

body.name: name
body.description: New name, 1-100 chars. May be omitted — it is backfilled from the stored dashboard (see guidance).

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level 1 or 2. Backfilled from the stored dashboard if omitted.

body.name: type
body.description: Dashboard type. Backfilled from the stored dashboard if omitted.

body.name: widgets
body.description: Replacement widget set at the body root. Same treemap-visualization stripping and render-safety validation as create.

body.name: filters
body.description: Replacement global filters (same shape as create).

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.

Unlike the internal PUT this TOLERATES a partial body: omitted name/type/level are backfilled from the stored dashboard (an extra read) so a null is not mistaken for a change. The widget set, however, still fully replaces the stored one — there is no undo.
Same normalization as create: a treemap `visualization` override is silently dropped and widget configs are validated up front.
In demo-sandbox environments updating the default dashboard is rejected with 400.

capabilities.name: delete_dashboard_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a custom dashboard and its widgets via the public API.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Dashboard UUID to delete.

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.
Not recoverable — the dashboard and its widgets are gone for good; delete is scoped to rows the caller owns/manages (else DASHBOARD_NOT_FOUND).
In demo-sandbox environments the shared default dashboard is guarded and the call 400s.
The success body is the JSON object {"success": true} returned as a plain string, not a structured JSON response.

capabilities.name: clone_dashboard_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Copy an existing dashboard (its persisted widgets) into a new dashboard via the public API — typically to fork a template dashboard under a new name/level.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: SOURCE dashboard UUID to copy from.

body.name: name
body.description: Name for the copy, 1-100 chars, unique in the group.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility level 1 or 2 for the copy.

body.name: type
body.description: Dashboard type for the copy.

guidance: Public API surface — authenticate with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic.
The widgets in the request body are IGNORED — the clone copies the SOURCE dashboard's stored widgets; only name/type/level are taken from the body.
Render-safety validation runs against the resolved source dashboard (inside the service), not the request body, so a broken source can fail the clone.

capabilities.name: get_project_automation_coverage_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Get one project's automation-coverage figures - total test cases, automated count and coverage percent over all time - to chart automation progress from outside the UI.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Exact project display NAME (not the normalised slug and not the id), matched within the caller's group. Blank or missing is a 400; a name that does not resolve in the group is a 404.

guidance: Public REST API route - callable with a username + access key as well as service credentials; scoping is by the authenticated group only, with no project-level permission check on this route.
Lookup is by EXACT project name, case- and space-sensitive, within your group. The normalised slug used elsewhere and the numeric id are both rejected here - use the display name.
This reuses the Automation Coverage dashboard widget over an all-time window, so it is an aggregation query, not a cheap key lookup - expect it to be slower than a plain read.
Fields are serialised only when non-null (NON_NULL). `calculated_at` is when this figure was computed, not a project timestamp; treat it as the freshness of the number.

capabilities.name: list_projects_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: List the calling account's Test Observability projects (public REST API) - the entry point for scripted/CI consumers that then drill into a project's builds.

query.name: next_page
query.description: Opaque base64 cursor from the previous response's pagination.next_page (it encodes an offset). Omit for the first page. A malformed value is a 400 'Incorrect pagination params'.

guidance: Requires a service-account credential carrying the PROJECT_VIEW permission; a session/user credential without it is refused.
Fixed page size of 10; there is no page-size parameter. Paginate only with the returned base64 next_page cursor, not a numeric page.

pagination.has_next is computed as 'this page was non-empty', so the last full page still reports has_next=true and you get one extra EMPTY page. Stop when projects comes back empty, not when has_next turns false.
There is no total count in the response. Each row carries the project's id, name and a ready-made observability_url into its builds page.

capabilities.name: list_home_unique_builds
capabilities.intent: List the Home page's latest runs grouped by unique build name - one row per build pipeline with its most recent run's status and counts - optionally narrowed to 'my builds' and quick filters.

query.name: pageNumber
query.description: Zero-based offset page (page size 10). Offset pagination is capped: has_next stays true only while offset <= 99, i.e. roughly the first ten pages. For deeper paging use the afterKey cursor instead.

query.name: afterKey
query.description: Elasticsearch search_after cursor for cursor pagination. Prefer this over pageNumber for walking past the offset cap; carry forward pagingParams.afterKey from the previous response.

query.name: myBuilds
query.description: Restrict to builds owned by the calling user.

query.name: applyQuickFilters
query.description: Turn the per-request quick filters below ON. When false (default) the endpoint applies only the user's persisted Home filters and ignores the quick-filter params.

query.name: statuses
query.description: Quick-filter build statuses. Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true; invalid values are skipped rather than 400ing.

query.name: users
query.description: Quick-filter user ids. Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true.

query.name: frameworks
query.description: Quick-filter framework values. Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true.

query.name: buildTags
query.description: Quick-filter build tags. Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true.

query.name: projects
query.description: Quick-filter project ids. Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true.

query.name: isRealDevice
query.description: Quick-filter device type (string, not boolean, so a stale value degrades instead of erroring). Only applied when applyQuickFilters=true.

guidance: The user's saved Home filters (build tags, projects, users, teams, unique build names, statuses) are merged into the query server-side even when applyQuickFilters is off - results are always scoped by the caller's persisted personalisation and sub-group.

Two pagination schemes coexist: offset (pageNumber, capped at offset<=99) and cursor (afterKey). Use afterKey to page beyond the offset cap; pagingParams.hasNext is 'this page was full AND under the offset cap'.
Quick-filter params are inert unless applyQuickFilters=true. Bad/stale quick-filter values are silently dropped (mapSkippingInvalid), never 400.
Heavy on large groups (emits per-stage timing telemetry); each row is a BuildSummary for the latest run of that unique build name.

capabilities.name: list_home_recent_views
capabilities.intent: Get the user's last few visited items (dashboards, builds, views) for the Home page 'Recently viewed' strip.
guidance: Read from a per-user Redis sorted set, capped at the 5 most recent entries; there are no parameters and no pagination.
Entries are written as a side effect of the user opening a dashboard - this endpoint never writes. A fresh user gets an empty data array.
Unparseable stored entries are silently skipped, so the list can be shorter than 5 even when 5 were recorded. Response is {"data": [ ... ]}; each item has type, link, id, name.

capabilities.name: get_home_takeaways
capabilities.intent: Get the Home page 'key takeaways' cards with the aggregate time-saved metric - stability, pass-rate, always-failing/flaky/new-failure counts and a single time-savings percentage, versus the previous 7-day window.
guidance: This is the older takeaways variant. It returns the aggregate `timeSavingsData` object (timeSavings %, testToVerify, uniqueErrors, flakiness, alwaysFailing, autoTagged) and leaves the v2 `timeSavingV2Metric` field absent. For the shape the current Home page uses, pick get_home_takeaways_with_noise_breakdown instead.
Scoped implicitly by the caller's saved Home filters, sub-group and visible projects; no parameters.

Cached in Redis per USER id for ~1 hour, so a filter change is not reflected until the cache expires. All metrics compare the current 7 days to the prior 7 days (each TakeAwayMetric carries value and prev).

capabilities.name: get_home_takeaways_with_noise_breakdown
capabilities.intent: Get the Home page 'key takeaways' cards with the failure-noise breakdown - the same stability/pass-rate story plus per-category (flaky, always-failing, auto-analyzed, unique-error) failure counts and their percentage reductions.
guidance: This is the variant the current Home page uses. It returns the `timeSavingV2Metric` object (totalFailures plus flakyFailing/alwaysFailing/autoAnalyzedFailure/uniqueErrors, each a count + reduction%) and explicitly sets the legacy `timeSavingsData` to null - do not expect a single time-savings percentage here.
Same takeAwayData block (stability, unique executions, new failures, always-failing, flakiness, failures; each value vs prev 7-day) as the older variant.
Cached in Redis per (filter-hash + CAD product + sub-group), so the cache is SHARED across users with identical filters - unlike the per-user cache of the older variant. TTL ~1 hour.
When there are zero failures in the window, timeSavingV2Metric collapses to just {totalFailures: 0} with the per-category objects omitted.

capabilities.name: claim_extended_free_trial
capabilities.intent: Claim the 30-day extended (reverse) free trial for the caller's group and get the refreshed plan details back.
guidance: Requires an authenticated USER role. No request body or parameters - it acts on the caller's group.

Idempotent-ish: if the group already requested or acquired the trial, it silently returns current plan details WITHOUT calling payments again, so a 200 here does not prove a trial was newly granted - check canClaimFreeTrial/isOnFreeTrial in the response.

Side effects outside the product: calls the BrowserStack payments service, marks the trial in Redis and seeds a free-trial test-execution quota. The Redis group-cache override it writes is expected to be replaced by the next group sync.
The response is the same plan-details object returned inside the app-bootstrap call's planDetails, not a trial receipt.

capabilities.name: get_user_access_details
capabilities.intent: App bootstrap call: get everything the frontend needs on first paint - user identity, group, plan/access, the computed RBAC permission map, T&C and get-started flags, usage banner and the user's build-view preferences.
guidance: Pass the X-CAD-Product HEADER to select the calling product; AA/AUT/ATS drive the QIG T&C A/B branch that decides hasAcceptedTnC and showGetStartedModal. Other products take the legacy whitelist/blacklist branch.
Requires an authenticated session (obs-token / central-auth cookie in practice); identity is derived from the JWT.
Heavy: fans out to Rails user/group details (Redis-cached), the usage service and the user-filters repo.

In the demo-sandbox environment userDetails.userId and userDetails.groupId are nulled out. When globalRBAC is on, legacy permission keys are added into accessDetails for backward compatibility alongside the new permissions map.

capabilities.name: meter_feature_usage
capabilities.intent: Meter a quota-limited feature: increment the caller's usage counter when they use a re-run or download a report, so free-plan limits can be enforced.

query.name: feature
query.description: A known Features name. Only RERUN and DOWNLOAD_REPORT actually increment usage; other recognised names are accepted as no-ops. An UNKNOWN name returns 404 with an empty body.

200.description: Metered (or accepted as a no-op / super-user short-circuit). Empty body.

guidance: Fire-and-forget: a success is an empty 200 with NO counter in the body - re-read plan details (planDetails.features.<name>.used) to see the new count.
Super users are short-circuited with 200 and no metering; public-link guests are skipped inside FeatureService so a guest never burns the link owner's quota.
The `values` list is the set that actually meters; passing another KNOWN Features name is a silent 200 no-op, while an UNKNOWN name is a 404 (empty body), not a 400.
This only increments a counter (recoverable state), so it is a write, not destructive - but there is no decrement endpoint here to undo an over-count.

capabilities.name: whitelist_group_for_observability
capabilities.intent: Self-serve opt-in: add the caller's group to the Test Observability whitelist (and remove it from the blacklist), which flips T&C / product access on for the org.
guidance: This is a GET that MUTATES state (Redis whitelist/blacklist set membership) - it is a write despite the verb, and takes no parameters. Any authenticated session can whitelist its own group; there is no role check.

A 403 here does NOT mean forbidden - it means the group was ALREADY whitelisted (the set-add reported no change). Both 200 and 403 carry the same {"success": bool} body; read success, and treat 403+success=false as 'already enabled', not an error.
The change is recoverable (a set membership) but there is no companion 'remove from whitelist' capability in this batch.

capabilities.name: create_project
capabilities.intent: Provision the Test Observability mirror of a TestHub project (creating the user row on first sight) and return the new observability project id.

body.name: user
body.description: The acting/owning user to attach the project to; the user row is created if this id is unseen.

fields.name: id
fields.description: BrowserStack user id; becomes the project owner and is created if it does not exist.

fields.name: groupId
fields.description: The user's group id; scopes the project.

fields.name: username
fields.description: Used only when creating the user row.

fields.name: fullName
fields.description: Used only when creating the user row.

body.name: project
body.description: The TestHub project to mirror. Idempotency is keyed on thProjectId.

fields.name: thProjectId
fields.description: TestHub project id. If a mirror already exists for it, that existing project_id is returned instead of a new one.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Project display name for the new mirror.

guidance: Service-to-service ONLY: authenticated by X-Service-API-Key (@ObsServiceAuthRequired). A customer username + access key CANNOT call this even though the path prefix would otherwise permit a session - this is not a customer-facing 'new project' API.
Idempotent on thProjectId: an existing mirror for the same TestHub project id is returned rather than duplicated.
The response body is a raw JSON STRING like {"project_id": 123}, not a typed object - parse it as JSON text.
First creation seeds the project (quality-profile mappings, issue types, default attributes) and, when UDAC is enabled, clears the group's cached project-id list.

capabilities.name: delete_project

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Numeric id of the project to delete. Interpreted per the `source` query param (see below).

query.name: source
query.description: Selects how projectId is read. TO (default) = an observability project id. TCM = the id is a TCM project id, resolved to its mirrored observability project before deleting. Passing a TCM id WITHOUT source=TCM deletes the wrong (or a nonexistent) project.

guidance: IRREVERSIBLE. Delegates to TestHub, which cascades the delete to everything under the project (builds, runs, results). There is no restore.

The projectId is bound with the `source` param: with source=TCM the supplied id is treated as a TCM project id and resolved to the TO project first. Match source to the id family or you will delete a different project.
Blocked with 400 in demo-sandbox environments ('Cannot delete default project').
On success returns {"message": "Project with ID: '<id>' is successfully deleted."} and clears the group's deleted-projects Redis cache. A TestHub-side failure surfaces as the upstream error message.

capabilities.name: list_project_builds_by_group
capabilities.intent: List a project's builds rolled up by build group (consolidated re-runs/shards shown as one row), with the full v2 build-listing filter set.

path_params.name: normalisedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (URL-safe slug), not its numeric id.

query.name: buildNameIds
query.description: Filter by build name ids.

query.name: uniqueBuildNames
query.description: Filter by unique build names.

query.name: users
query.description: Filter by user ids (numeric).

query.name: assignees
query.description: Assignee ids; each must match ^(\$none|[0-9]+)$ ($none = unassigned).

query.name: teams
query.description: Filter by team ids.

query.name: buildGroupIds
query.description: Filter by build group ids.

query.name: frameworks
query.description: Raw framework values (branded enum names and pass-through values like 'appium'); matched case-insensitively.

query.name: statuses
query.description: Build display statuses.

query.name: sources
query.description: Product sources.

query.name: types
query.description: Build types.

query.name: buildTags
query.description: Filter by build tags.

query.name: tags
query.description: Test-execution tag names (max 500); AND/OR selected via `match`.

query.name: branches
query.description: Filter by branch names.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Exactly two epoch-millis longs [from, to] (size must be 2).

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text build search.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: ES search_after cursor; must match ^[0-9a-zA-Z]{40}$ (a 40-char id).

query.name: state
query.description: Build state; defaults to active.

query.name: isArchived
query.description: Restrict to archived builds.

query.name: selfHealed
query.description: Only self-healed builds.

query.name: aiAuthored
query.description: Only AI-authored builds.

query.name: isRealDevice
query.description: Device-type multi-select (true=real, false=virtual); empty/both = no filter.

guidance: Sibling of the ungrouped v2 build listing: this one consolidates re-runs/shards into build groups (see buildGroupAggResult). Filters are the same rich v2 set, passed as query params (there is no request body).
Cursor-paginated via searchAfter (carry pagingParams.searchAfter forward); pagingParams.hasNext signals more pages. Page size is the server default and was not verifiable from the controller.
Side effect: reading this marks the project as SUBSCRIBED for the caller (a user-preference write) - a benign, recoverable effect, but it is not a pure read.
Unlike the ungrouped v2 listing, this route does NOT apply the group's custom-retention window, so it can surface builds older than that window.

capabilities.name: list_alert_types
capabilities.intent: List the catalogue of alert types an account can subscribe to (id, type, description) — the source of the alertTypeId the older create-project-alert call needs.
guidance: Reference/lookup data only — the same list for every account, with no group or user scoping and no parameters.
The response is a BARE JSON array, not an object wrapper: iterate the top-level array directly.
Take each row's integer `id`: that is the value `create_project_alert_by_integer_id` expects as `alertTypeId`. The newer `create_project_alert` instead takes a string `alertType`.

capabilities.name: get_global_settings
capabilities.intent: Read the account-wide list of build sources/types hidden from this product's views, so the UI can show which build kinds are excluded group-wide.
guidance: Takes no parameters — the product/visibility bucket and group are resolved from the session.
The excluded build types are at `data.excluded_sources` (snake_case), NOT `data.excludedSources`.

This is a pass-through to an upstream settings service; on ANY upstream error it logs and returns an empty settings object rather than failing. So an empty `excluded_sources` can mean either 'nothing is excluded' or 'the upstream read failed' — you cannot tell which from this response.

capabilities.name: update_global_settings
capabilities.intent: Hide or unhide whole classes of builds account-wide by adding to / removing from the group's build-type include and exclude lists.
guidance: ADMIN or OWNER only (IAAM role check) — any other role gets 403, even one that can edit project settings.
Diff-style patch: the server reads the current lists, applies your `add`/`remove` as a set union/difference, and writes the merged result back. Reversible by removing what you added.
The whole payload sits under a top-level `build` object; the list-ops are at `build.build_type.include.{add,remove}` and `build.build_type.exclude.{add,remove}`.
A `product` key in the body is IGNORED — the server overwrites it from the session, so you cannot target another product by setting it.
This is a read-modify-write with no version check, so a concurrent patch can silently drop the other writer's change. Returns {success:true} whether or not anything actually changed.

body.name: build
body.description: Wrapper for the whole payload. Contains `build_type`, which holds an `include` and an `exclude` list-op, each a {add:[], remove:[]}.

fields.name: build_type
fields.description: Holds `include` and `exclude`, each a {add:[], remove:[]} of build-type/source names.

body.name: include_add
body.description: Build-type/source names to ADD to the include list (a set union with the current list).

body.name: include_remove
body.description: Build-type/source names to REMOVE from the include list.

body.name: exclude_add
body.description: Build-type/source names to ADD to the exclude list — i.e. hide these build kinds account-wide.

body.name: exclude_remove
body.description: Build-type/source names to REMOVE from the exclude list — i.e. unhide them.

capabilities.name: get_user_preferences
capabilities.intent: Read the signed-in user's cross-project UI preferences — build-details tab order and default tab, and the default test view for running vs completed builds — so the UI opens where the user left it.
guidance: Send the `X-CAD-Product` header to select the product context (AUT / TO / TM / AA …); it drives how the response is rewritten.

The response is rewritten per product and may NOT match what was stored: the accessibility tab is stripped for products that do not support it (and the default falls back to insights), and a sessions tab is injected for Automate / App Automate.
`defaultTabForRunningBuilds` is null on rows written before OB-10619 and should be read as 'sessions'.
Everything is under a top-level `data` key.

headers.name: X-CAD-Product
headers.description: Product context selector (AUT / TO / TM / AA …). Determines which tabs are added/stripped in the response.

capabilities.name: save_user_preferences
capabilities.intent: Save the signed-in user's build-details tab preferences (order + default tab) and default test views for running/completed builds.
guidance: Send the `X-CAD-Product` header — it scopes which product's preferences are written.
This is a FULL REPLACE of the user's preference row, not a merge; omitted fields are cleared. Reversible only by saving again — there is no prior-value history.

The server MUTATES what you send: a missing 'sessions' or 'accessibility' tab is appended when the product supports it, so the stored value can differ from your payload. Re-read to see the effective preference.
Returns {success:true}.

headers.name: X-CAD-Product
headers.description: Product context selector (AUT / TO / TM / AA …) the preferences are saved under.

body.name: buildDetailsTabPreferences
body.description: Ordered tabs for the build-details page. Order in the array IS the tab order.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Tab id (e.g. insights, sessions, accessibility).

fields.name: isDefault
fields.description: Whether this tab is the default the build-details page opens on.

body.name: testViewForRunningBuilds
body.description: Default test view shown for running builds.

body.name: testViewForCompletedBuilds
body.description: Default test view shown for completed builds.

body.name: defaultTabForRunningBuilds
body.description: Tab id a running build opens on. Legacy rows store null, which the read side interprets as 'sessions'.

capabilities.name: create_project_alert_by_integer_id
capabilities.intent: Create a project alert on the older surface: a named threshold/condition rule set plus its notification routing (email/Slack), optionally scoped to specific build names. Returns the new alert id.
guidance: `{projectId}` here is the NUMERIC observability project id, not the normalized name. To create an alert by the project's normalized name use `create_project_alert`.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_ALERTS permission on the project — 403 otherwise.
`name` is required; an empty name is a 400.

Build-name scoping is the field `buildName` (SINGULAR) on this surface — the newer `create_project_alert` takes `buildNames` (plural). The rule set is `alertRules`, a flat set of rules each carrying its own `level`; the alert type is set by the integer `alertTypeId` (see list_alert_types).
`notificationRules` is keyed by notifier type (SLACK / EMAIL), each mapping to lists of notifier resources.
Returns 201 CREATED with the new alert's integer `id`.

path_params.description: Numeric observability project id.

body.name: name
body.description: Alert name. Required and must be non-empty (@NotEmpty).

body.name: alertTypeId
body.description: Which alert type this alert is; the integer id from list_alert_types.

body.name: alertRules
body.description: Set of threshold/condition rules. Duplicate rules (same level+value) are de-duplicated.

fields.name: level
fields.description: Severity/level label for this rule.

fields.name: value
fields.description: Threshold value. Required, sent as a string.

fields.name: condition
fields.description: Comparison/condition. Required.

body.name: notificationRules
body.description: Notification routing: a map keyed by notifier type (SLACK / EMAIL), each value a map of channel-key → list of notifier resources {notifierId, name, workspaceId, id, allAlerts, userId, groupId, enabled}.

body.name: buildName
body.description: Build names this alert is scoped to. NOTE the SINGULAR key `buildName` on this older surface (the newer surface uses `buildNames`).

capabilities.name: create_failure_category_sub_type_by_integer_id
capabilities.intent: Create a custom failure-category sub-type for a project (a project-specific flavour of a built-in category) with its own long name, short name and colour, so testers can categorise failures more precisely.
guidance: `{projectId}` is the NUMERIC observability project id. To create by normalized name (and with the newer `category`/`name` body) use `create_failure_category_sub_type`.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission — 403 otherwise.
All four fields are required. `shortName` is max 4 characters, `longName` max 64, and `color` must match a hex colour (#RGB or #RRGGBB).
`typeRef` names the PARENT built-in issue type this sub-type hangs under.
Returns 201 with {id, locator}. The string `locator` is how `update_failure_category_sub_types_by_integer_id` later identifies this sub-type.

capabilities.name: get_project_settings_by_integer_id
capabilities.intent: Load the project settings page payload: the project's custom failure-category sub-types (grouped by parent issue type) and its configured alerts (grouped by alert type).
guidance: Ungated read — there is no permission check; it is scoped to the caller's group.
`{projectId}` here is the NUMERIC observability project id — unlike the /notifications/* siblings on the same base path, which treat the path segment as the project's normalized name.
`subTypes` is a map keyed by parent issue type → list of sub-types; each sub-type carries the string `locator` used to update or delete it, plus `abbreviation` (short name) and `color`.
`alerts` is a map keyed by alert type → list of alert objects (same shape create/update take, with the alert's integer `id`).

path_params.name: projectId

guidance: The alert to update is taken from the body's `id`, NOT from the path. Omitting `id` does not target by path — supply it in the body.
`{projectId}` is the NUMERIC project id; requires the PROJECT_SETTING_ALERTS permission.
Responds 201 CREATED (not 200) on a successful update — a quirk of the handler; do not read the non-200 status as a failure.
Same body shape as create: `name` required, rule set in `alertRules` (flat, each with its own `level`), build scoping via `buildName` (SINGULAR).

body.name: buildName

guidance: `{projectId}` is the NUMERIC project id; requires the PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission.
The body's top-level key is `ids`, but despite the name it is a NON-EMPTY list of full sub-type OBJECTS, not a list of bare ids. An empty list is rejected.
Each item must carry its string `locator` (which sub-type to update) and `typeRef`, plus longName / shortName / color. shortName max 4, longName max 64, color must be hex.
Returns 200 with a `message`. Reversible only by updating again.

capabilities.intent: Create a project alert by the project's normalized name: a named rule set (e.g. failure-rate thresholds per severity level, optionally scoped to specific build names) plus its Slack/email notification mappings.

Build scoping is `buildNames` (PLURAL) here; the alert type is the string `alertType` (not the older integer `alertTypeId`).
`name` is required. Returns 201 with {success, id} — note `id` is a STRING on this surface.

guidance: Path takes the project's NORMALIZED NAME. To create by numeric project id (with the older `typeRef`/`longName`/`shortName` body) use `create_failure_category_sub_type_by_integer_id`.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission (legacy 'modify_project_settings'), checked in-handler — 403 otherwise.
Body uses `category` (the parent failure category) + `name` — NOT the older surface's `typeRef`/`longName`/`shortName`. `name` max 64.
`color` is optional and defaults to #56Cb9D; when supplied it must match a hex colour.
Returns 201 with {success, id}.

capabilities.name: list_alert_notifiers
capabilities.intent: List the notification targets available to a project (its configured Slack channels / email notifiers) so the alert editor can offer them as choices.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check. Path takes the project's normalized name.

The response is a BARE JSON array of notifiers. Only ENABLED, non-conditional notifiers that are NOT already bound to an alert are returned — it is the pool of targets you can attach to a new alert, not the alert's current routing.
Each notifier has an integer `id`, a `type` (SLACK / EMAIL) and a `value` blob (JSON) holding the channel / email detail.
Served by the notification-mapping service, so its shape differs from the alert objects returned elsewhere.

capabilities.name: get_auto_analyser_settings
capabilities.intent: Read a project's automatic failure-analysis configuration (whether AI/auto categorisation of failures is on) for the Settings tab.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check. Path takes the project's normalized name.
Returns an UNTYPED settings object: a flat map of setting-key → value. The keys are not fixed by this contract — read them dynamically rather than assuming a field set.
Every expected key is always present: an attribute with no stored value is returned with its default filled in.
Values come back as STRINGS even for boolean-like flags.
