capabilities.intent: Read a project's auto-close policy — whether stale open test runs are closed automatically, after how many days, and when the policy was enabled.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check (unlike the auto-close preview-count sibling, which needs the write permission).
When no policy is set the response is {enabled:false} with `thresholdDays` and `enabledAt` absent — a missing policy reads as disabled, not as a 404.
`enabledAt` is epoch SECONDS and anchors the 7-day grace window.
`projectsConfigured` is only populated on a WRITE; it is null/absent on this read.

capabilities.name: approve_test_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id. The run is resolved for the caller's group first, so a foreign id is not readable.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The conversation turn's messageId (UUID), from a conversation list or a create reply.

capabilities.intent: Accept one AI RCA answer as a test's official root cause: mark that conversation turn approved and promote its analysis onto the test run's stored RCA so the Test Details page shows it.
guidance: No request body. Session-authenticated (central-auth / obs-token / speedboat); this is the web Improve-Analysis action, not a public-API call — the public mirror is approve_test_rca_conversation_turn_via_public_api.
Overwrites the test run's existing stored RCA with this turn's content. There is no versioning and no undo — the previous analysis is gone.

Only a COMPLETED turn with no prior decision can be approved: a still-running turn returns 409 RCA_CONVERSATION_NOT_COMPLETED, and an already approved/discarded turn returns RCA_CONVERSATION_ALREADY_RESOLVED.
Refused with 403 FORBIDDEN_OPERATION when the run's RCA is owned by the MCP-powered agent (is_mcp_driven), and with 403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when AI-TFA is blocked for the plan.

Side effects beyond the turn: it marks the run web-owned (which then locks out the MCP chat flow) and fires a best-effort Release Readiness report re-generation for the build because the RCA content changed.
Success is a flat {"status":"approved"} — it does not echo the promoted RCA; read the test RCA separately to see the new content.

capabilities.name: discard_test_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id, group-scoped before the lookup.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The conversation turn's messageId (UUID).

capabilities.intent: Reject one AI RCA answer: flag that conversation turn as discarded so the panel stops offering it, while the test run keeps its previous stored RCA.
guidance: No request body. Session-authenticated web action; the public mirror is discard_test_rca_conversation_turn_via_public_api.
Touches only the turn's own metadata (records user_approval=discarded). The test run's stored RCA is untouched, unlike approve.

Same preconditions as approve: the turn must be COMPLETED (else 409 RCA_CONVERSATION_NOT_COMPLETED) and must have no prior decision (else RCA_CONVERSATION_ALREADY_RESOLVED). Unlike approve there is no MCP-ownership guard.
403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when AI-TFA is blocked for the plan.
Success is a flat {"status":"discarded"}.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id, group-scoped before the lookup.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The conversation turn's messageId (UUID).

capabilities.intent: Fetch one turn of a test's AI RCA conversation by message id — the polling read the panel uses to watch a PENDING turn become COMPLETED or FAILED after a retry.
guidance: Poll this after retry_test_rca_conversation_turn (or a retrigger) until state is no longer PENDING. state is one of PENDING, WORKFLOW_PENDING, COMPLETED, FAILED.

This is the test-run turn shape: threadId, threadTitle and userAction are always null here (those carry values only in the build-level chat). The answer is assistantMessage; metadata is sanitised to at most thinking_data and user_approval.
404 RCA_CONVERSATION_NOT_FOUND if the messageId does not belong to that test run.

capabilities.name: list_test_rca_conversation_turns

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id, resolved for the caller's group so foreign runs cannot be read.

capabilities.intent: Load the whole AI RCA chat thread for a failed test — every turn in creation order with its user instruction, assistant answer, state and approval status — to render the Improve-Analysis panel.
guidance: Returns a bare JSON array of turns (no envelope, no pagination), ordered oldest-first by creation time.
Each element is the test-run turn shape: threadId, threadTitle and userAction are null; the approval decision, when made, is in metadata.user_approval (accepted or discarded).
There is no query filtering here; it always returns the full history for the run.

capabilities.name: retry_test_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id; group-scoped, and its build must pass the RCA-v2 eligibility check.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The failed/timed-out turn's messageId (UUID). The same row is reused.

capabilities.intent: Retry a conversation turn that failed or timed out: re-send the same instruction and attachments to the AI service and reset the turn to PENDING, keeping the same message id so the panel keeps polling it.
guidance: No request body. Asynchronous — 200 means the retry was accepted, not answered; poll get_test_rca_conversation_turn on the same messageId until state leaves PENDING.
Creates NO new turn (unlike a retrigger): the existing row is reset in place and its messageId is returned unchanged.

Unlike approve/discard this is NOT gated on the AI-TFA feature block; it runs validateRcaV2Eligibility instead (group scope, test-run age check, build RCA-v2 eligibility). Returns 400 if the caller's username/access key cannot be resolved server-side.
The response carries only messageId here; the trialQuota field of the shared shape is populated only by the retrigger flow, not by retry.

capabilities.name: complete_build_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID the turn belongs to.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The turn (UUID) being completed or narrated.

body.name: success
body.description: Whether the agent's run for this turn succeeded. Read on the terminal (non-THINKING) path.

body.name: assistant_message
body.description: The finished answer payload for the turn (arbitrary JSON). Present on the terminal completion post.

body.name: thinking_data
body.description: Intermediate narration payload. On a THINKING post this is what gets relayed to the client; on the terminal post it is the persisted thinking trail.

body.name: agent_summary
body.description: Optional agent-produced summary of the turn (arbitrary JSON).

body.name: new_checkpointer_s3_uri
body.description: Optional S3 URI of the agent's updated checkpointer state.

body.name: failure_reason
body.description: Failure detail when success is false.

body.name: state
body.description: Set to "THINKING" for intermediate narration posts (relayed to the client, no DB write). Absent/null for the terminal completion post, which flips the turn to COMPLETED/FAILED via the pipeline.

capabilities.intent: Internal service webhook: the build RCA agent posts a turn's finished answer here (terminal), or intermediate THINKING narration pointers while it works.
guidance: Service-to-service ONLY — @PreAuthorize hasRole('SERVICE'); authenticate with the rca-agent service API key (X-Service-API-Key). A normal user token is rejected. Not customer-facing; an agent should not call this to drive a conversation.

Two paths keyed by state: state="THINKING" is relayed straight to the client with no DB write; any other/absent state is the terminal completion, which publishes one event per messageId (idempotent by construction) and lets the pipeline update the row — obs-api itself does not write the row on the terminal path.
Field names are snake_case on the wire (assistant_message, thinking_data, agent_summary, new_checkpointer_s3_uri, failure_reason). Unknown fields are ignored.
Always returns {"status":"ok"}, regardless of path.

capabilities.name: create_build_rca_thread

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID to open the thread on. The thread is scoped to (build, current user).

capabilities.intent: Create an empty build-level RCA chat thread for the current user — backs the 'New chat' button, giving the composer a thread to post into before any message exists.
guidance: No request body. Mostly optional: create_build_rca_conversation_turn lazy-creates a thread when threadId is omitted, so call this only when you need an empty thread up front.
Enforces the per-user active-thread cap (default 10) and returns 400 when the cap is hit — reuse or clean up existing threads instead of retrying.
Plan-tier / AI-TFA fencing applies (403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when the group is not entitled).
The new thread's title is null until the first user message sets it; carry the returned id as threadId on the first turn.

capabilities.name: create_build_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID the chat is on; verified to belong to the caller's group.

body.name: userMessage
body.description: Typed question. Provide this and/or userAction — at least one non-empty is required, else 400. Max 5000 chars.

body.name: userAction
body.description: Structured workflow-card action instead of (or alongside) a typed message — e.g. save_preferences, retrigger, trigger_test_rca. At least one of userMessage/userAction must be present.

body.name: threadId
body.description: Target thread, owned by the caller. When omitted the service lazy-creates a thread and enforces the per-user thread cap (so an omitted threadId can fail with 400 when the cap is hit). A foreign threadId returns 404.

body.name: unconfirmedS3Keys
body.description: Up to 3 S3 keys under unconfirmed-build-chat/ for this turn's attachments. Each key's {groupId} segment must match the caller's group; on submit they are moved to confirmed-build-chat/. More than 3 is rejected.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: One unconfirmed-build-chat S3 key.

body.name: idempotencyKey
body.description: Client-generated key for workflow-card submits: a duplicate submit with the same key on the same thread returns 200 with the existing row instead of inserting a duplicate. User-message turns typically omit it.

body.name: tabContext
body.description: Typed 'where the user is' envelope, forwarded to the agent. STRICT shape — unknown top-level keys are rejected (400). Nullable.

fields.name: snapshot
fields.description: Free-form per-tab snapshot; overall serialised tabContext size is bounded server-side.

capabilities.intent: Submit a new turn in the build-level RCA chat: a typed question, a workflow-card action (save_preferences / retrigger / trigger_test_rca), or both, optionally with attachments; persists the turn as PENDING and kicks off the async agent.
guidance: Asynchronous: 200 means the turn was accepted, not answered. Poll get_build_rca_conversation_turn on the returned messageId (or listen on the push channel) until state leaves PENDING/WORKFLOW_PENDING.

Body fields are flat at the top level (no wrapper). At least one of userMessage or userAction must be non-empty — sending neither is a 400. Unknown top-level body keys are ignored, EXCEPT inside tabContext where they are rejected.
There is no separate regenerate endpoint — to redo a turn, re-POST the same userMessage; you get a new messageId and a new row.
Omitting threadId lazy-creates a thread and can therefore fail on the per-user thread cap (default 10). Attachments beyond 3, or a key not owned by the caller's group, fail the request.
The response is the created turn (build shape): it always carries the resolved threadId (important on lazy-create) and threadTitle, plus the PENDING state.
This is the session-auth build chat; there is no public-API mirror for build-level turns (the public chat surface is submit_test_rca_chat_turn, which is test-run scoped).

capabilities.name: get_build_rca_conversation_turn

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID the turn belongs to.

path_params.name: messageId
path_params.description: The turn's messageId (UUID). The lookup is filtered by the caller's user id.

capabilities.intent: Fetch a single build-RCA turn by message id, with its current state and the assistant's answer once ready — the polling read used after create_build_rca_conversation_turn returns a PENDING row.
guidance: IDOR-safe: the lookup filters on the caller's own user id, so guessing another user's messageId does not leak it.
A missing or foreign row comes back as 400 BAD_REQUEST_ERROR ("Conversation not found: ..."), NOT a 404 — do not treat a 400 here as malformed input.
Build turn shape: threadId, threadTitle and userAction are populated (unlike the test-run turn). Poll until state leaves PENDING/WORKFLOW_PENDING.

capabilities.name: list_build_rca_conversation_turns

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID.

query.name: threadId
query.description: REQUIRED — the thread whose turns to load. The legacy 'all rows for this user' variant was removed, so a call without threadId is a 400. A foreign threadId returns 404.

query.name: cursor
query.description: ISO-8601 instant. Pass the previous page's nextCursor to fetch the page immediately older. Omit for the newest page. An unparseable value is a 400.

query.name: limit
query.description: Page size. Clamped server-side to [1,200]; a value < 1 falls back to 50 rather than erroring.

capabilities.intent: Load a page of one build-level RCA chat thread's turns for the current user — the user's message/action plus the agent's answer — to render the AI RCA panel on a build.
guidance: threadId is MANDATORY as a query param; without it you get a 400.
Scoped to the calling user's own turns on that thread. Turns come back oldest-first within the page.

Cursor pagination: read nextCursor from the response and pass it back as cursor for the next (older) page; nextCursor is null at the end of history. Do not assume the default 50 is the ceiling — request up to 200 per page.
Each turn is the build shape (threadId/threadTitle/userAction populated).

capabilities.name: list_build_rca_threads

path_params.name: buildUUID

capabilities.intent: List the caller's own RCA chat threads on a build (id, title, timestamps), most recently active first — the thread switcher in the build AI panel.
guidance: Returns a bare JSON array of thread objects (no envelope, no pagination). Scoped to (build, current user) — you never see other users' threads.
Empty array when the user has no threads yet; a thread's title is null until its first user message sets it.
Plan-tier / AI-TFA fencing applies (403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when the group is not entitled).

capabilities.name: report_build_rca_workflow_event

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID in the path — NOT used to look the row up; the row is found by trackingId.

body.name: trackingId
body.description: Stable id of the originating workflow run (minted by obs-api on the user_action submit and echoed back). This — not buildUUID — is how the row is located. Required (400 if blank).

body.name: newState
body.description: New workflow state. complete / completed / failed are terminal and fire the narration kickoff; other values are currently a no-op on obs-api's side. Required (400 if blank).

body.name: workflowType
body.description: Workflow kind.

body.name: errorReason
body.description: Failure detail when newState is failed.

body.name: resultPayload
body.description: Free-form result for narration. For retrigger typically { "new_message_id_in_test_rca": "..." }; for trigger_test_rca the new test-RCA's identifier.

capabilities.intent: Internal service webhook: the workflow runner (TFA retrigger / trigger_test_rca pipeline) reports a workflow state change here, so the build chat can narrate the outcome on terminal states.
guidance: Service-to-service ONLY — @PreAuthorize hasRole('SERVICE'); requires the service API key (X-Service-API-Key). A normal user token is rejected. Not customer-facing.
Idempotent and always 200 — even when no row matches trackingId — so duplicate deliveries are harmless. Non-terminal states are currently a no-op.
The row is located by trackingId, not by the buildUUID in the path.
Response is {status, narration_kickoff_fired}; narration_kickoff_fired reports whether a terminal state actually triggered the narration kickoff.

Overwrites the test run's stored RCA with no undo. Only a COMPLETED turn with no prior decision can be approved; refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION when the run's RCA is owned by the MCP agent (is_mcp_driven).

Only flips the turn's user_approval metadata to discarded; the conversation row is kept and the stored RCA is untouched.

path_params.name: test_run_id

capabilities.intent: Public-API: return the full RCA conversation history for a test run — each user instruction and the AI's answer with its status and approval state — so an agent can render or resume the Improve-Analysis thread.
guidance: Public API — username + access key auth. External mirror of list_test_rca_conversation_turns.
Returns a bare JSON array of turns (no envelope, no pagination), ordered oldest-first.
Each element is the test-run turn shape: threadId, threadTitle and userAction are null; approval decision, when made, is in metadata.user_approval.

capabilities.name: submit_test_rca_chat_turn

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id; the run is group-scoped, age-checked and eligibility-fenced before the turn is accepted.

body.name: message
body.description: The user's question for this turn. Required, non-blank, max 5000 chars.

body.name: clientContext
body.description: Optional free-form context — accepts a JSON object OR a string. Forwarded to the agent unchanged; size-capped server-side.

body.name: threadId
body.description: Optional conversation thread id to continue (opaque string, max 255 chars). NOT a UUID like the build-chat threadId.

capabilities.intent: Public-API: submit one conversational turn to the RCA chat agent for a test run (a question plus optional context/thread id) and get back a turn id to poll for the answer.
guidance: Public API — username + access key auth. Asynchronous: obs-api mints a turnId, seeds a 'working' result, and hands the work off; poll get_test_rca_chat_turn_status with the returned turnId. The response is an acknowledgement (turnId, threadId, status), NOT the answer.
The FIRST turn claims the test run for the MCP agent flow (creating a PENDING RCA row). It is refused if the web Improve-Analysis flow already owns the run.

Fail-fast plan fence (403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED) before any run resolution, then the full spine: group IDOR scope, test-run age, build, AI consent/feature fence, credential resolution. Returns 400 if the caller's credentials cannot be resolved.
This turnId is an opaque Redis result key, a different id space from the messageId used by the approve/discard/list conversation endpoints — do not cross them.
There is no separate regenerate — submit another turn to ask again.

capabilities.name: get_test_rca_chat_turn_status

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id, group-scoped before the read and bound to the turn (a turn whose stored test_run_id differs reads as not_found).

path_params.name: turnId
path_params.description: The opaque turn id returned by submit_test_rca_chat_turn (a Redis result key, not a UUID messageId).

capabilities.intent: Public-API: poll the outcome of a previously submitted RCA chat turn, returning its lifecycle status plus the structured answer, metadata or error once the agent finishes.
guidance: Public API — username + access key auth. status is the lifecycle poll state: "working" (still running), "completed" (answer ready in turn), or "not_found".

Results live in Redis with a TTL: a turn is retrievable only while its result key survives. A missing/expired key, OR a turn whose stored test_run_id does not match the path testRunId, both return status "not_found" — a leaked turn id alone cannot read another group's turn.

When completed, the answer is the structured object in `turn` (an LLM-enforced TurnResponse: turn.status + confidence + a per-status sub-object such as needs_info/blocked, or the stitched rca for RESOLVED). Read turn.status; confidence and message_id live inside `turn`, not as siblings.

query.name: teams

query.name: failureCategories
query.description: Failure-category filter values.

query.name: isFlaky

query.name: isNewFailure

query.name: isAlwaysFailing
query.description: Tri-state always-failing filter; omit to not filter.
