query.name: browserList
query.description: Browser filter values.

query.name: deviceList
query.description: Device filter values.

query.name: isMuted
query.description: Muted-test visibility (ALL / MUTED / UNMUTED identifiers also accepted, case-insensitively).

query.name: hooksVisibility
query.description: Hooks visibility scope.

query.name: isAutomationLatest
query.description: When true, failure counts are sourced from the recorded status keyword (SDK-recorded automation status). When not true AND the account has the new build listing flag on, counts instead come from workflow status, which can change the numbers for the same window.

capabilities.intent: Get the Suite Health page chart data in one call: time-bucketed failures-over-executions, average duration, and average failure-rate series for the project's tests over a window, filtered by the full Suite Health filter set.
guidance: Response is a top-level map of three charts — `failureChart`, `durationChart`, `failureRateChart` — each an SPChart with a `data` map of named series (arrays of {x,t,y,pointRange} points) and an `insights` summary. There is no `data` envelope wrapper.
Series keys inside `data`: failureChart carries `totalExecutions` and `totalFailures`; durationChart carries `averageDuration`; failureRateChart carries `averageFailureRates`.
Archived builds are excluded from every counter.

The same query can return DIFFERENT failure numbers depending on account config: with the new build listing flag on and `isAutomationLatest` not true, failures are counted from workflow status rather than the raw status keyword. Set `isAutomationLatest=true` to force the raw-status counts.

The failure series can come back with fewer buckets than the executions series when a slice has zero matches; the failure-rate series is computed by aligning on the `x` timestamp, so do not assume the two arrays are index-aligned.

capabilities.name: get_test_base_info

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (URL slug).

path_params.name: stabilityHash
path_params.description: The test's stability hash, discovered from the Suite Health test listing.

query.name: isMuted
query.description: REQUIRED muted-test visibility. Accepts all / true (muted only) / false (unmuted only); ALL / MUTED / UNMUTED also accepted, case-insensitively. An unrecognised value is a 400. There is no default.

query.name: lowerBound
query.description: Window start as an epoch-millisecond long. Optional on this route (there is no dateRange array here).

query.name: upperBound
query.description: Window end as an epoch-millisecond long. Optional.

query.name: buildName
query.description: Single build name to scope to (wrapped into a one-element list server-side); this route takes at most one, not a list.

capabilities.intent: Get the identifying header info for one test in the Test Health detail view — its name and the environment (OS/browser/device) combinations it ran on — for the selected window.
guidance: Response is a flat object `{name, combinations}` with NO data wrapper. `name` is the test's display name (empty string when the hash matches nothing in the window, still 200), and `combinations` is the list of OS/browser/device environments it ran on.
`isMuted` is required here even though it is optional on the listing; omit it and the request fails.
Narrower filter set than the test listing: no browser/os/device/tag filters, and only a single `buildName`.
Any internal error is rethrown as a bare RuntimeException and surfaces as a plain 500 (no structured error body), so treat a 500 as opaque rather than parsing it.

capabilities.name: get_test_environment_breakdown

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (URL slug).

path_params.name: stabilityHash
path_params.description: The test's stability hash, discovered from the Suite Health test listing.

query.name: isMuted
query.description: REQUIRED muted-test visibility. Accepts all / true / false; ALL / MUTED / UNMUTED also accepted, case-insensitively. An unrecognised value is a 400. There is no default.

query.name: lowerBound
query.description: Window start as an epoch-millisecond long. Optional.

query.name: upperBound
query.description: Window end as an epoch-millisecond long. Optional.

query.name: buildName
query.description: Single build name to scope to (wrapped into a one-element list server-side); at most one, not a list.

query.name: isFlaky
query.description: Tri-state flakiness filter; omit to not filter.

query.name: orderKey
query.description: Sort key for the returned rows. Unrecognised/absent falls back to reliability.

query.name: orderValue
query.description: Sort direction. Unrecognised/absent falls back to descending.

capabilities.intent: Break one test's results down by environment (OS / browser / device) over the window, so you can see whether its instability is platform-specific.
guidance: The body is a BARE JSON ARRAY of environment rows (no object wrapper, no `data` key). Each row: `id` (browser-platform key), `reliability` (fail %), `duration` (avg), `os`/`browser`/`browserDevice` (formatted platform objects), and `totalFailures` {failed,total}.
Uses the older explicit-argument service overload, so it accepts only a SINGLE `buildName` and a much smaller filter set than the test listing (no os/browser/device/tag filters).
`isMuted` is required; omit it and the request fails.

Rows are sorted server-side (default reliability, descending) and platform rows that carry no displayable browser or device are dropped, so the array may be shorter than the number of distinct environments.
Any internal error is rethrown as a bare RuntimeException and surfaces as a plain 500 with no structured body.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_app_logs
capabilities.intent: Get a test run's application (app-under-test / SDK) log lines, parsed and flattened for display — use this for the app-logs tab when you want normalised rows rather than raw Loki JSON.

query.name: testRunUuid
query.description: The test run's UUID (not its integer id and not the TR-NNN identifier). A missing or foreign UUID collapses into an empty 500 with no body.

200.description: Parsed app logs. `status` is 'success', or 'failure' with an empty `logs` list (still HTTP 200) when Loki reports a non-success status.

guidance: Returns ONLY abnormal (error-level) app-log lines — the Loki query hard-codes an abnormal filter — capped at 5000 lines and bounded to the run's own start/finish window (±5s). A passing run with no error logs legitimately comes back with an empty `logs` list.

Two failure shapes, neither is an ordinary HTTP error: when Loki answers non-success you get HTTP 200 with `status:"failure"` and `logs:[]`; when anything throws you get a bare HTTP 500 with no body. Check `status`, and do not read an empty 500 as a specific cause — a missing/foreign run and a Loki outage look identical.
Each log line is split on a ' cSep=S ' separator and only the text after it is kept; a line that lacks the separator is returned raw and unsplit.
For the untouched Loki payload use the raw variant instead; this one is the parsed, UI-normalised form.
`level` on each line falls back to 'unknown' when Loki did not tag the stream with a level.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_app_logs_raw
capabilities.intent: Get a test run's application logs as Loki's raw, unparsed JSON response — use this only when you need the native Loki shape; for displayable rows use the parsed app-logs capability instead.

query.name: testRunUuid
query.description: The test run's UUID (not its integer id and not the TR-NNN identifier).

200.description: Loki's native query_range JSON body, relayed verbatim as an opaque JSON document (top-level `status` and `data.result[]` streams). This is NOT an app model — the shape is Loki's, not the service's.

schema.description: Opaque pass-through of Loki's /query_range response. Typically `{status, data:{resultType, result:[{stream, values:[[epochNano, line]]}]}}`, but treat it as an untyped Loki document.

guidance: Pure pass-through of Loki's body — the same abnormal-only filter, 5000-line cap and run-time-window bounding as the parsed variant apply, but nothing is normalised. Log lines still carry the ' cSep=S ' separator and their level pattern; you must split them yourself.
The handler swallows every exception into a bare HTTP 500 with no body, so a missing or foreign testRunUuid is indistinguishable from a Loki outage.
Prefer the parsed app-logs capability unless you specifically need Loki's native envelope; this one returns a JSON string, not the service's AppLogResponse.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_hooks
capabilities.intent: Public API: list the before/after setup and teardown hook executions relevant to a test run, so a failure can be attributed to a hook rather than the test body.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

200.description: A MAP keyed by hook test-run id (numeric string keys), each value a TestDetailResponse for that hook. An empty object means no hooks matched.

schema.description: Keyed by matched hook run id.

guidance: Public /ext/v1 API — authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.
The result is a MAP keyed by hook test-run id, not a list; iterate the values.

Matching is heuristic, not a stored parent/child link: hooks are matched on the SAME build id + filename + OS + browser + device, latest only. A hook that ran in a differently-configured session will not appear here even though it belongs to the same build.
At most 100 hook runs are returned (the underlying search is size-capped); there is no paging to fetch more.
An unknown test_run_id returns TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND (404). A run with no matching hooks returns an empty object with 200.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_log_bundle
capabilities.intent: Public API: get the full log bundle for a test run — BrowserStack session logs (console/network/selenium/appium/video), SDK logs, hook-run logs, failure and step logs — as URLs plus the test start/finish timestamps and framework.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

200.description: Log URLs and metadata. `browserstackLogs` is a SessionLogs object of per-type log URLs; `sdkLogs` and `hookRunLogs` are lists of URL strings; `failureLogs` and `stepLogs` are inline log-entry objects.

guidance: Public /ext/v1 API — authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.

Returns log URLs to fetch separately, NOT log content. The caller downloads each artefact from the URLs in `browserstackLogs`, `sdkLogs` and `hookRunLogs`; only `failureLogs` and `stepLogs` are inline.
The logs are always the TRIMMED variant — the trim flag is hard-coded true on this route, so there is no way to ask for the untrimmed logs here.
Plan-locked / retention-expired builds are rejected with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED (403).
Several log sources are fetched concurrently, so latency tracks the slowest source; expect a slow response for large sessions.

capabilities.name: get_session_network_log_url
capabilities.intent: Get the URL of a session's HAR network log for the Test Details network tab — returns a link to the HAR file plus its fetch status, not the parsed entries.

path_params.name: sessionId
path_params.description: The session's HASHED id (not a numeric id).

200.description: The network-log URL envelope. `networkLogs` is the HAR file URL, `status_code` is the upstream fetch status, `message` any upstream message.

guidance: Despite the name, this returns the HAR file URL in `networkLogs`, NOT the parsed HAR entries — the handler requests the unparsed form. Fetch the HAR yourself from that URL; it can be large.
On the demo-sandbox environment it short-circuits to an empty HAR (`{log:{entries:[]}, responseOrigin:"demo"}`) before any lookup.
An unknown sessionId returns SESSION_NOT_FOUND. Note the id here is the session's hashed id, the same id the sibling session log-URLs capability takes.

capabilities.name: get_session_log_urls
capabilities.intent: Get the set of log artefact URLs for a session (raw/text, selenium/appium, console, device, network) so the Test Details logs tab can lazily load whichever tab the user opens.

path_params.name: sessionId
path_params.description: The session's HASHED id (not a numeric id).

200.description: Session log URLs. `browserstackLogs` is a SessionLogs object of per-type log URLs; `failureLogs` is present only when the session was manually marked with a reason.

guidance: Returns URLs, not log content — the UI fetches each artefact from the URLs inside `browserstackLogs`.

Log-fetch failures are SWALLOWED: if the upstream log fetch throws, the response comes back with an empty `browserstackLogs` (SessionLogs) and 200 rather than an error. An empty logs object is not proof there were no logs.
Locked (plan-restricted) builds are refused with 403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED; an unknown session is SESSION_NOT_FOUND.
`failureLogs` is populated only when the session was manually marked failed with a reason; otherwise it is empty.
The demo-sandbox environment returns an empty envelope (null framework, empty SessionLogs, empty failureLogs) without any lookup.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_auto_unmute_config
capabilities.intent: Get the auto-unmute rule attached to a muted test — unmute type, expiry, unmute-after-N-runs, the condition's status and who muted it — so the test-detail page can show when and why the test comes off mute.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

200.description: A dynamic map describing the auto-unmute rule. Common keys are `isMuted`, `unmuteStatus`, `mutedByBtcerId`, plus the parsed unmute-config-history fields; the exact keys vary with the unmute workflow state. An empty map means no auto-unmute rule is attached.

schema.description: Dynamic auto-unmute config map; keys depend on unmute workflow state. Empty object = no rule.

guidance: An empty JSON object means the test has NO auto-unmute rule — not an error.

The shape is not fixed: the config is read from the run's own unmute-config history, or from the run that muted it (`mutedByBtcerId`), or from shared test-properties meta, depending on the unmute workflow state. Do not assume a stable set of keys.
An unknown testRunId returns TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND (404).
Errors while parsing the stored config are swallowed — you may get a partial or empty map with 200 rather than a failure.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_behaviour
capabilities.intent: Get the BDD/behaviour payload stored on a test run (the Gherkin feature/scenario structure in the run's meta) that backs the Behaviour tab for Cucumber-style frameworks.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

200.description: The run's meta JSON (the Gherkin/behaviour structure) as an opaque object, or an empty object `{}` when the run has no meta.

schema.description: Opaque BDD/behaviour meta object stored on the run. Empty object when no meta is present.

guidance: Returns the run's raw meta object; only meaningful for BDD (Cucumber-style) builds. A run with no meta returns an empty object `{}` with HTTP 200, not a 404.
A MISSING test run does not give a typed error — the handler checks lock status before the null check, so a bad id throws a NullPointerException (HTTP 500), not TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND.
Locked (retention-expired) runs are rejected with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION.
The Behaviour tab is only offered for BDD builds; for a non-BDD run this payload is not useful even when present.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_capabilities
capabilities.intent: Get the desired/actual Selenium-Appium capabilities the BrowserStack session for this test run was started with — the Capabilities tab on the test-detail page.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

200.description: An opaque capabilities object whose top-level key depends on the platform: `sessionParams` for BrowserStack sessions, `inputCapabilities` for Local-Grid/SauceLabs/LambdaTest, or `outputCapabilities` as a fallback when the BrowserStack fetch fails. Empty for runs with no session.

schema.description: Opaque capabilities object; top-level key varies by test platform (sessionParams / inputCapabilities / outputCapabilities).

guidance: The response shape depends on where the run executed: a BrowserStack session returns the live `sessionParams`; Local-Grid/SauceLabs/LambdaTest runs return `inputCapabilities`; if the BrowserStack lookup fails the handler falls back to a stored `outputCapabilities` shape. Do not hard-code one key.
Pulled from the run's BrowserStack integration record, so it is empty for runs that never had a BrowserStack session.
Bad ids give TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND / BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404); retention-locked builds give FORBIDDEN_OPERATION (403).
On the demo-sandbox environment canned capabilities are returned instead of the real session's.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_merged_logs
capabilities.intent: Get a single merged, time-ordered log stream for a test run — BrowserStack session logs, SDK logs, hook-run logs, failure and step logs combined into one list, with content merged server-side — for the Logs tab.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: The test run's integer id.

query.name: trim
query.description: When true, restrict the merged logs to the test's own time window. Defaults to false (full session).

200.description: A top-level JSON ARRAY of merged, time-ordered log entries (GenericLog objects). Content is downloaded and merged server-side, so entries carry inline `content`, not just URLs.

guidance: This form downloads and MERGES every log source server-side and returns the content inline as one time-ordered array, so it is slow for long sessions. A sibling capability returns log URLs instead (content fetched client-side) — prefer that one for large sessions.
The body is a bare JSON array of log entries, not an object wrapper — iterate it directly.
`trim=true` narrows the stream to the test's own time window; the default (false) includes the whole session.
Bad ids give TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND / BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404); locked builds give FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED (403).
On the demo-sandbox environment canned logs are returned, chosen by the test's name.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_details

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric test run id.

capabilities.intent: Get the full detail of one test run — its metadata plus the captured test code and the code of the before/after hooks that ran around it, i.e. everything needed to understand what the test did.
guidance: This is the heaviest of the detail reads: it assembles the run, its captured code, its meta and the related hook code from several sources, so prefer a lighter read when you only need status or metadata.
testCode (and each entry of hooksCode) can have null code/language when no code was captured for that run — the row is still returned; do not treat a null code as an error.
A run that does not belong to the caller's group, or does not exist, comes back as TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND — the same answer for 'wrong group' and 'no such run'.

testMetadata here is the internal test-meta object and is shaped differently from the flatter meta returned by the baseline/similar-error map reads; read its keys from this response rather than assuming they match.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_baseline

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the (typically failing) run whose baseline you want.

capabilities.intent: Find a failing run's baseline — the most recent passing run of the same test in the last 30 days — returned with full test detail, so you can diff a failure against the last known-good execution.
guidance: Returns a MAP keyed by test run id, not a single object. Priority 1 is the newest passing run with the same test hash (one entry); if there is none it falls back to the newest passing run per device/os/browser combination (several entries). An EMPTY map means no baseline was found, not an error.
The look-back window is hardcoded to 30 days before this run's start time — an older last-good run will not appear, so an empty result does not prove the test has never passed.
Each map value is the same shape as the similar-error read: { testCode, testMetadata } (no hooksCode on this route). Read the passing run's numeric id from the map key.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_build_insights

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric test run id; its parent build is resolved from it.

capabilities.intent: Get the build-level insights that surround a failing run — the parent build's failure/flakiness summary, failure categorisation and top-errors analysis, plus this run's own file/module failure context — so a failure can be reasoned about in context.
guidance: The run's parent build is resolved first; a run whose build cannot be found returns BUILD_NOT_FOUND (distinct from TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND when the run itself is missing).

topErrorsAnalysis.status is one of ANALYSIS_PENDING / ANALYSIS_COMPLETE / ANALYSIS_NOT_STARTED — when not COMPLETE, uniqueErrors may be empty or partial, so check the status before treating the error list as final.

failureContext (file and parentModule failure rates) is the per-run slice; the rest of the payload is aggregated across the whole build. A build-scoped variant that omits this per-run context exists internally but is not this capability.

capabilities.name: list_test_runs_sharing_error

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric id of the failing run whose error cluster you are matching against. Excluded from the returned set.

path_params.name: clusterId
path_params.description: Unique-error cluster id. It sits in the PATH but is bound onto the filter object's clusterId property by Spring's URI-template data binding — you do NOT also pass it as a query param.

query.name: projectId
query.description: Project the error breakdown is scoped to. Required — omitting it is a binding error, not an empty result.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to] scoping the error search. Bound onto the filter but NOT validated at request binding on this route (no @Valid), so a call without it will not 400 here yet may return nothing — supply it to get a meaningful window.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true, search the error across all builds rather than only the run's own build.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Elasticsearch search_after cursor echoed back from a previous page to continue paging the affected-runs scan.

capabilities.intent: List the other test runs that failed with the same unique-error cluster as this run — the 'tests affected by this error' list, each returned with full test detail.
guidance: Returns a MAP keyed by test run id (each value is { testCode, testMetadata }); the querying run itself is always excluded, and an EMPTY map means no other run shares the cluster.
projectId is a REQUIRED query param; the cluster is taken from the {clusterId} path segment via data binding, so do not duplicate it as a query param.

The affected-run scan also accepts the wider GetSPError filter set (test tags, statuses, devices/os/browsers, folders, users, etc.) as query params bound onto the filter object — use them to narrow which affected runs come back.

capabilities.name: list_build_test_runs

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID (not a numeric id). The listing is scoped to this build.

query.name: next_page
query.description: Opaque base64 pagination cursor. Echo back the pagination.nextPage from the previous response verbatim; do not construct it. Stop when pagination.hasNext is false.

query.name: sort
query.description: Sort column.

query.name: order
query.description: Sort direction. Required alongside sort — the two are read together.

query.name: test_statuses
query.description: Filter by status strings (e.g. passed, failed, skipped).

query.name: re_runs
query.description: Filter by re-run numbers (list of integers).

query.name: is_flaky
query.description: Smart-tag filter. On a freemium or source-fenced build this (and is_always_failing / is_new_failure / has_performance_anomaly) is REFUSED with a plan-restriction 403, not silently ignored.

query.name: is_always_failing
query.description: Smart-tag filter; plan-gated as above.

query.name: is_new_failure
query.description: Smart-tag filter; plan-gated as above.

query.name: has_performance_anomaly
query.description: Smart-tag filter; plan-gated as above.

query.name: hooks_visibility
query.description: Which hooks to include in the tree. Defaults to failed.

query.name: is_muted
query.description: Muted-tests visibility: all, true (only muted), false (only unmuted). Also accepts ALL/MUTED/UNMUTED. An unrecognised value is rejected.

capabilities.intent: List a build's test runs as the UI suite/folder tree, with the full filter set (status, flaky, muted, re-runs, tags, failure category, device/os/browser, folders, performance anomaly, new/always-failing), sorted and cursor-paginated, with deep-link URLs back to the BrowserStack UI.
guidance: The response is a NESTED hierarchy (suites/folders/tests), each node carrying an external deep-link URL — it is not a flat array. For a flat list use the flat build listing instead.

Plan- and source-aware: on a freemium or source-fenced build the analysis keys are stripped from every node, and using any smart-tag filter (is_flaky / is_always_failing / is_new_failure / has_performance_anomaly) is refused with a 403 telling you to upgrade — so gate those filters on plan.
Service-account callers are additionally checked for the TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_VIEW permission on the build's project; lacking it is a 403.

Pagination is an opaque base64 next_page token; pass pagination.nextPage back unchanged and stop when pagination.hasNext is false. The response envelope also differs by an account flag: newer accounts get workflowStatusAggregate + isManuallyOverridden, older ones get statusAggregate — read whichever is present.

capabilities.name: list_test_run_attachment_urls

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric test run id.

query.name: type
query.description: Which artefact kind to page. Required, case-insensitive; any other value is rejected with 'Invalid type parameter. Allowed values: ATTACHMENT or SCREENSHOT'.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Page size. Must be 1..100; outside that range is a 400 ('pageSize must be between 1 and 100').

query.name: cursor
query.description: Opaque continuation token from the previous response's pagination.nextCursor. Omit on the first page.

capabilities.intent: Page through one test run's attachments or screenshots as downloadable presigned URLs, so they can be fetched externally.
guidance: Gated by an account feature flag (external attachment download). When off, the call is a 400 'Downloading attachments is disabled for this account' regardless of the run — this is a feature gap, not a missing run.
The urls are PRESIGNED S3 URLs that expire ~2 hours after issue — download promptly; re-call to get fresh URLs rather than caching them.

When the run has zero of the requested type you get 200 with an empty urls list and pagination.totalCount 0 (not a 404). Continue paging while pagination.hasMore is true, passing pagination.nextCursor back as cursor.

capabilities.name: list_build_test_runs_with_attachments

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID (not a numeric id).

query.name: page_size
query.description: Page size. Must be 1..100; outside that range is a 400 ('Limit should be between 1 and 100').

query.name: cursor
query.description: NUMERIC cursor from the previous response's next_cursor (this route uses a numeric cursor, unlike the base64 cursor on the plain build test-run listing). Omit on the first page.

capabilities.intent: List only the test runs in a build that actually have attachments or screenshots, with per-run counts — the discovery step before downloading artefacts run by run.
guidance: Returns a TRIMMED row per run — id, name, uuid, build_id, attachments_count, screenshots_count — not the full test-run object; use the per-run attachments read to get the actual download URLs.
Pagination is a numeric cursor: pass the previous response's next_cursor back as cursor; a null next_cursor means the last page.
The build is resolved by (uuid, group); an unknown uuid for the caller's group is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.name: cancel_test_run_auto_unmute

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: Declared in the route but NOT used for the lookup — the run is found by testRunId within the caller's group. Any placeholder value is accepted here.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id.

capabilities.intent: Convert a test that was muted with an automatic unmute condition (e.g. 'unmute after N passes' or after a date) into a permanently manual mute, so it will not be auto-unmuted.
guidance: No request body. On success it always returns the plain string 'Auto unmute cancelled successfully!' — the message never varies, so it is not a signal of whether anything actually changed.
If the mute is already MANUAL the call is a 200 no-op; if the test is not muted at all it will error (TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND applies to a missing run).
Requires the BUILD_MUTE_TESTS project permission on the run's project (403 otherwise), and it is refused for older builds with a 400 'Cannot cancel auto unmute for older test'.
Reversible: re-mute the test with an auto-unmute condition to undo this. There is no separate 'restore auto-unmute' call — this only removes the schedule.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_bug_report_draft

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: Declared in the route but NOT read by the handler — the draft is composed from testRunId alone (group-scoped). Any placeholder value is accepted.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id whose failure the draft describes.

capabilities.intent: Build the pre-filled bug-report draft for a failed test — test name/status/duration, platform/browser, failure category, CI and host info, build name, retries, screenshot/log attachments and the AI RCA snippet — i.e. everything the 'Report a bug to Jira/Azure' modal needs to compose a ticket.
guidance: Read-only despite the name: it COMPOSES a new draft description, it does not fetch a bug that was already filed. To record a filed bug use link_bug_to_test_run.
It requires screenshot/retry data to exist for the run — a run with no such data throws 'retry doesn't exist' (a 4xx), so treat that as 'nothing to report on yet', not an outage.
logStruct carries image/log attachment references and aiRca carries the AI RCA snippet; both can be empty/absent when the run has no screenshots or no RCA.

capabilities.name: link_bug_to_test_run

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: Declared in the route but NOT read by the handler. Any placeholder value is accepted; the run is resolved from testRunId.

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Numeric test run id to attach the bug to.

body.name: name
body.description: The external issue KEY (e.g. the Jira/Azure ticket id). Used for the idempotency check — a key already tracked on the run makes the call a no-op.

body.name: type
body.description: The PM-tool name the issue belongs to (e.g. Jira, Azure Boards).

body.name: url
body.description: Deep link to the created issue, shown in the UI.

body.name: status
body.description: The issue's status to display against the run.

body.name: uniqueUserId
body.description: Id of the user credited with filing the bug.

capabilities.intent: After a bug has been created in a PM tool (Jira, Azure Boards, …), link that external issue to the test run — recording it in the run's integration tables and marking the test as bug-reported so the UI shows the issue key/link.
guidance: Idempotent on the issue key: if that bug name is already tracked on the run (checked in both quoted-legacy and unquoted forms) you get 204 No Content with no body — treat that as 'already linked', not a failure.
On a fresh link it returns 200 with { id } — the created integration id. The caller must have permission to create defects on the run's project (403 otherwise).
Linking also fires the PM-Tools integration trigger as a side effect; if that trigger fails it is only logged and does not fail the link.
Reversible: an unlink route removes the association, so this is a write, not a destructive op. Send the issue KEY in `name` (not in `url`).

204.description: The bug key is already tracked on this run; nothing was changed and there is no body.

capabilities.name: list_build_test_runs_flat

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID (not a numeric id). Resolved by (uuid, group); unknown → BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Elasticsearch search_after cursor — pass the previous page's cursor back to continue. Omit on the first page.

query.name: testRunIds
query.description: Restrict to specific numeric run ids. When present it takes precedence over the clusterIds/latest path.

query.name: clusterIds
query.description: Restrict to runs in these unique-error clusters (only applied when testRunIds is not sent; that path also limits to the latest run per test).

query.name: virtualDevice
query.description: true restricts to virtual-device runs; false includes explicit-false AND runs missing the field.

capabilities.intent: List a build's test runs as a flat, filterable list (rather than the nested suite/folder hierarchy) — the data source for the flat test-listing view of a build.
guidance: Flat counterpart of the hierarchical build listing — returns a plain array under testRuns, no tree. Filters arrive as QUERY params bound onto a POJO, not as a JSON body.
In each row the top-level `id` is the test's HASH (a string); the numeric run id you need for other run reads is `details.id`. Do not pass the top-level id where a numeric run id is expected.

Pagination is Elasticsearch search_after: pass the prior page's cursor back as `searchAfter`. Note the underlying query fetches up to 10,000 hits, so on very large builds narrow with filters rather than relying on paging alone.
The ES indices queried are chosen from the build, so very old builds may resolve to different indices; results are limited to the latest run per test unless you pass explicit testRunIds.

capabilities.name: get_build_ai_failures

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string), not a numeric build id.

capabilities.intent: Get a build's AI failure analysis: the clustered failure themes and the workflows they map to, sorted by share of failures, to explain why a build failed.
guidance: Read-only: returns whatever analysis already exists and never starts a new one. If nothing has been computed the themes/workflows come back empty; use trigger_build_ai_failure_analysis to kick it off.
buildThemes and buildWorkflows are pre-sorted by failure share, highest first.
buildThemeWorkflow.status tells you where the analysis stands (e.g. SUCCESS, PENDING); a non-terminal status means results are still being produced.
trialQuota is present only for accounts on the build-level AI trial; its absence means the account is not on a trial, not that usage is zero.
This read is intentionally not plan-fenced, so a plan-downgraded account can still read prior analysis.

capabilities.name: trigger_build_ai_failure_analysis

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

capabilities.intent: Start build-level AI failure analysis for a build (get-or-trigger): returns existing themes/workflows if ready, otherwise enqueues the clustering and flags that it was triggered.
guidance: Get-or-trigger: if analysis already exists in a terminal state it is returned with triggered=false; otherwise it is enqueued and you get triggered=true. When freshly triggered the themes/workflows are NOT in the response (they may be null) and arrive later, so poll get_build_ai_failures.
Asynchronous: a triggered=true response is an acknowledgement, not results.
Requires AI opt-in consent, a non-disabled AI-enabled flag, and the build-level RCA feature on the account; missing any of these fails with an AI-feature error, not a plain validation error.
Trial accounts over their build-level quota are refused with a 403 plan-not-allowed error, and every fresh trigger consumes one unit of the trial quota.
A build excluded by source-fencing is rejected.
Takes NO request body; the build is identified entirely by the path.
Not reversible in the destructive sense, but there is no undo for the analysis run it starts (it only produces data, never removes it).

capabilities.name: list_build_ai_failure_cluster_test_runs

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

query.name: buildFailureThemeId
query.description: Integer id of the failure theme to drill into, from a build AI-failures read. Give this OR buildFailureWorkflowId to scope to one cluster.

query.name: buildFailureWorkflowId
query.description: Integer id of the failure workflow to drill into, from a build AI-failures read.

query.name: limit
query.description: ACCEPTED BUT IGNORED. Page size is fixed by the backend's Elasticsearch default and this value is not applied; do not rely on it to cap or size the result. Use searchAfter to page.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Opaque search-after cursor. Pass the pagingParams.searchAfter (JSON-encoded) from the previous response to fetch the next page.

capabilities.intent: Drill into one AI failure theme or workflow of a build and list the individual test runs behind it, with their details, going from a failure cluster to the actual failing tests.
guidance: Scope with buildFailureThemeId OR buildFailureWorkflowId (ids come from get_build_ai_failures). With neither, the lookup runs for the whole build.
limit is accepted but IGNORED; the backend uses its own default page size. Do not treat limit as a cap.
Paginate with the cursor: pass pagingParams.searchAfter back as searchAfter and stop when pagingParams.hasNext is false.
An empty testRuns with hasNext=false means the cluster resolved to no runs, not an error.
Adding a testRunIds query param routes to a DIFFERENT operation (list_build_ai_failure_test_runs_by_ids); omit it here.

capabilities.name: list_build_ai_failure_test_runs_by_ids

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

query.name: testRunIds
query.description: Comma-separated list of integer test-run ids to fetch directly (skips the theme/workflow lookup). Max 200 ids; more returns 400. Presence of this param is what selects this operation over the theme/workflow variant.

query.name: limit
query.description: ACCEPTED BUT IGNORED. Page size is fixed by the backend default; use searchAfter to page.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Opaque search-after cursor from the previous response's pagingParams.searchAfter.

capabilities.intent: List flat test-run details for an explicit set of test-run ids under a build, e.g. the specific runs a Release Readiness PR card cites, skipping the theme/workflow lookup entirely.
guidance: This variant is selected by sending testRunIds; without that param the same path routes to list_build_ai_failure_cluster_test_runs instead.
At most 200 ids; over that is a 400 naming testRunIds.

Group-scoped and IDOR-safe: the query filters on buildId AND testRunIds, so ids outside the caller's build simply do not match (no error). A result shorter than the id list can mean some ids were foreign, not an error.
limit is ignored (fixed backend page size); paginate via searchAfter and pagingParams.hasNext.
Intentionally not plan-fenced; a plan-downgraded account can still read prior content.

capabilities.name: get_build_ai_failures_via_public_api

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

capabilities.intent: Public API: get a build's AI failure analysis (clustered failure themes and their workflows, sorted by failure share), the summary a build-RCA agent uses to explain a build failure.
guidance: Public endpoint: authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.
Read-only: returns whatever has already been computed and never triggers analysis; use trigger_build_ai_failure_analysis_via_public_api to start it.
Themes and workflows are sorted by failure share, highest first.
trialQuota appears only for build-level trial accounts.
The build is resolved within the caller's group; a build in another group reads as not found.

capabilities.name: trigger_build_ai_failure_analysis_via_public_api

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

capabilities.intent: Public API: start build-level AI failure clustering for a build (get-or-trigger). Returns existing analysis if ready, otherwise enqueues it and flags that it was triggered.
guidance: Public endpoint: authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.
Get-or-trigger and asynchronous: triggered=true means analysis was enqueued and results are NOT in the response yet; poll get_build_ai_failures_via_public_api.
Gated by the AI-TFA plan fence plus AI consent, the build-level RCA feature, source-fencing and a trial quota; a blocked account gets a 403 plan-not-allowed error.
Runs only the theme/workflow clustering pipeline; this is NOT per-test RCA.
Takes no request body.
Produces data only, never removes any; there is no undo for the analysis run it starts.

capabilities.name: list_build_ai_failure_cluster_test_runs_via_public_api

path_params.name: buildUUID
path_params.description: Build UUID (opaque string).

query.name: buildFailureThemeId
query.description: Integer id of the failure theme to drill into, from a public AI-failures read. Give this OR buildFailureWorkflowId to scope to one cluster.

query.name: buildFailureWorkflowId
query.description: Integer id of the failure workflow to drill into.

query.name: limit
query.description: ACCEPTED BUT IGNORED. Page size is fixed by the backend default; use searchAfter to page.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Opaque search-after cursor from the previous response's pagingParams.searchAfter.

capabilities.intent: Public API: drill into one AI failure theme or workflow of a build and list the flat, paginated test runs behind it, going from a cluster to its tests.
guidance: Public endpoint: authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.
Scope with buildFailureThemeId or buildFailureWorkflowId (ids from get_build_ai_failures_via_public_api); with neither, the lookup runs for the whole build.
There is no explicit-testRunIds variant on the public flat endpoint.
limit is ignored; page with searchAfter until pagingParams.hasNext is false.

capabilities.name: stop_session

body.name: session_id
body.description: The session's hashed id to stop. Required; a missing/empty value is a 400 with the plain-string body "Session ID is required."

body.name: product
body.description: Which product the session belongs to. Required, case-insensitive; any value other than automate/app-automate is a 400 with plain-string body "Product is Invalid".

capabilities.intent: Stop a single running Automate or App Automate session (the stop-session control on a live run).
guidance: Both session_id and product are required and product must be automate or app-automate; otherwise a 400.
Ownership-checked: the session's group (resolved from the search index) must equal the caller's group, otherwise 401.
Pass-through to the Automate/App-Automate stop API; the upstream status code and body are relayed verbatim.
Unlike other build controls, its error bodies are PLAIN STRINGS (e.g. "Unauthorized", "An error occurred while stopping the session"), not the structured error envelope; do not parse them as JSON.
Stops the live run and cannot be undone, but does not delete the session; the session and its logs remain.

capabilities.name: list_queued_sessions

query.name: userId
query.description: The user whose queued sessions to list. Taken from the query, NOT the caller's identity, so any user id can be asked about.

query.name: product
query.description: Product to filter the queue by (e.g. automate / app-automate).

capabilities.intent: List the automation sessions currently queued for a user and product, each with session/build/project name, resolved capabilities, why it is queued and how long it has waited.
guidance: Both userId and product are required (400 otherwise).
userId comes from the query, so it is NOT scoped to the caller; only the build/project name enrichment is group-scoped (names resolve to null for builds outside your group).
queueReason explains the wait (e.g. no_terminal_available); duration is computed at read time.
The capabilities field's shape depends on the session's caps format (selenium / appium / default).

capabilities.name: list_build_sessions

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: NUMERIC build id (not a UUID and not a session id), despite the sessions base path. This is the build whose sessions to list.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number for the session listing.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text search over sessions (part of the FilterParamsV2 filter set bound from the query).

query.name: sessionStatus
query.description: Filter by session status. Part of the broad FilterParamsV2 filter set (also supports search, browserList, osList, deviceList, testTags and many more) bound directly from query params.

query.name: sortParam
query.description: Column to sort by (SortBy.sortParam).

query.name: sortOrder
query.description: Sort direction (SortBy.sortOrder, Elasticsearch SortOrder).

capabilities.intent: List the automation sessions recorded for a build, with per-session stats, filterable and sortable, as shown on the build's Sessions tab.
guidance: The path value is the NUMERIC build id even though the route sits under /sessions and sibling routes there take a session hashed id.
Public-link aware: when a public-link token header (Public-Link-Token or X-Public-Link-Token) is present, RUNNING sessions are excluded from what the viewer can see.

Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 query filter set (search, sessionStatus, browserList, osList, deviceList, testTags, and more) plus SortBy (sortParam/sortOrder) and page; the response is the pass-through TestHub session listing.
On the demo sandbox environment this returns canned sessions.

capabilities.name: get_session_app_profiling

path_params.name: sessionId
path_params.description: Session hashed id.

capabilities.intent: Get app-profiling data (CPU/memory/etc. captured during an App Automate session) for the Test Details app-performance tab.
guidance: App profiling is App Automate only; on an Automate session this is a 400 ("App Profiling is only supported for App Automate sessions").
An empty object ({}) is a normal 200 meaning the report is still generating (upstream 202) or was never captured (upstream 404); it is NOT an error, so re-poll rather than treating it as failure.
A missing session is SESSION_NOT_FOUND; a plan-locked build is 403 plan-not-allowed.
The body is the opaque upstream app-profiling JSON.
On the demo sandbox environment this returns an empty object.

capabilities.name: get_session_capabilities

path_params.name: sessionId
path_params.description: Session hashed id.

capabilities.intent: Get the raw desired/actual capabilities a session was started with (Automate or App Automate), so a user can see exactly how the run was configured.
guidance: Product-dependent: the session's origin (automate / app-automate) is resolved and the caps are fetched from that product's API.

The body is opaque JSON: normally the upstream sessionParams object, but if the upstream fetch fails it falls back to {outputCapabilities:{capabilities:...}} built from the stored session capabilities. Do not assume a fixed key.
A missing session is SESSION_NOT_FOUND; a plan-locked build is 403 plan-not-allowed.
On the demo sandbox environment this returns dummy capabilities.

capabilities.name: get_session_details

path_params.name: sessionId
path_params.description: Session hashed id.

capabilities.intent: Get the header/metadata block for a session on the Test Details page: video/audio log handles, session URL, platform/device, framework and timings the tabs are built from.
guidance: While the session is still being linked to its build the call returns a RETRYABLE 425 (BUILD_LINK_NOT_READY); retry shortly rather than treating it as fatal.
A missing session is SESSION_NOT_FOUND; a plan-locked build is 403 plan-not-allowed.
customMetadata and buildId are always null through this path today (buildId is not populated here despite the field name), so do not depend on them.
If the upstream media fetch fails, videoLogs/audioLogs come back null but the rest of the metadata is still returned with a 200.
On the demo sandbox environment this returns synthetic details with a sample video URL.

capabilities.name: get_session_test_code_via_public_api

path_params.name: session_id
path_params.description: Session hashed id.

capabilities.intent: Public API: get the test source code captured for an Automate session, one entry per test executed in that session, so external tooling (e.g. AI agents) can read the code behind a session.
guidance: Public endpoint: authenticate with your BrowserStack username + access key.
Cross-group safe: the resolved build's group is re-checked against the caller's group and a mismatch is reported as SESSION_NOT_FOUND (not a distinct 403).
A session that exists but captured NO code is reported as SESSION_NOT_FOUND, indistinguishable from a bad id, so not-found does not prove the id is wrong.
TestHub caps and truncates very large responses server-side; the truncation is only logged, never surfaced, so a returned code body may be incomplete without any flag.
A plan-locked build returns a forbidden-operation error.

capabilities.name: create_checks_mapping
capabilities.intent: Register a pull request's VCS checks (e.g. GitHub check runs) against existing BrowserStack check configurations, so the PR-checks / quality-gate pipeline can evaluate them and call back with results.

body.name: event_name
body.description: VCS event name that triggered the mapping. Mandatory and must be non-blank.

body.name: tool
body.description: Source tool (e.g. the VCS provider). Mandatory and must be non-blank.

body.name: callback_url
body.description: URL the evaluation pipeline calls back once each mapped check is evaluated. Mandatory and must be non-blank. Stored verbatim on every created ingestion row.

body.name: pr_data
body.description: Pull-request metadata. Mandatory. The whole object is also stored verbatim as the ingestion row's PR metadata blob (with githubCheckId merged in per check).

fields.name: organisationId
fields.description: VCS organisation id. Used (with repositoryId + group) to match existing check configurations; a mismatch means no config is found and the whole call is a 400.

fields.name: repositoryId
fields.description: VCS repository id. Used to match existing check configurations for the caller's group.

fields.name: number
fields.description: Pull request number, stored as pr_number on every created row.

fields.name: commitSHA
fields.description: Head commit SHA, stored as commit_sha on every created row.

fields.name: date
fields.description: Commit timestamp as an ISO-8601 instant (parsed with Instant.parse). An unparseable value fails the whole request with a 400 naming the check; when omitted, commit_timestamp is left unset.

fields.name: githubCheckId
fields.description: Optional; note the per-check GitHub id is normally supplied inside pr_checks, not here.

body.name: pr_checks
body.description: Non-empty list of the PR's checks to register. Each item's id is the CHECK CONFIGURATION id, and it must match an existing check configuration for the caller's group + this repository + organisation, or the whole call returns 400 'Check Configurations not found...'.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Check CONFIGURATION id as a string. Parsed with Long.parseLong, so a non-numeric value throws before validation and fails the call. NOT the GitHub check id.

fields.name: githubCheckId
fields.description: The GitHub check-run id for this check. Mandatory. Merged into the stored PR metadata blob for the matching ingestion row.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Check name. Mandatory and must be non-blank.

201.description: Array of the created vcs_ingestion rows (one per matched check configuration), each in state 'Not Started'. On success but with no matching configs the flow instead returns 400.

400.description: Plain-text (not JSON) body. Covers validation failures, the CHECKS_EVALUATION-not-accessible case, an unparseable commit date, a non-empty-but-unmatched pr_checks set ('Check Configurations not found...'), and any other exception whose message is echoed as the body.

guidance: Gated by the CHECKS_EVALUATION entitlement; when it is off the call still comes back as a 400 with the exception message as a PLAIN-TEXT body, so errors here are untyped strings, not JSON.
pr_checks[].id is the BrowserStack check-CONFIGURATION id, not the GitHub check id and not the ingestion id. Send the GitHub id separately as pr_checks[].githubCheckId.
A non-numeric pr_checks[].id throws (Long.parseLong) before bean validation, so it fails the whole request rather than returning a clean per-field error.

If none of the pr_checks ids match an existing check configuration for the caller's group + repositoryId + organisationId, the whole call is 400 'Check Configurations not found...' and nothing is created; register the check configuration first.

One vcs_ingestion row is created per MATCHED configuration; ids that match nothing are silently skipped rather than erroring individually. Read the returned array to see exactly which were registered, and take each row's integer id to look the mapping up later.
pr_data.date must be an ISO-8601 instant; an unparseable value fails the call with a 400 naming the check, and omitting it just leaves the commit timestamp unset.

capabilities.name: get_checks_mapping
capabilities.intent: Fetch a single previously-registered PR-check mapping (a vcs_ingestion row plus its joined check configuration) to see its current evaluation state, retry count, PR metadata and callback URL.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The vcs_ingestion row id returned by create_checks_mapping. NOT the GitHub check id and NOT the check-configuration id (the service calls it checkId, which is misleading).

404.description: Plain-text (not JSON) body: 'No check mapping found for checkId: N'. Returned when no row matches the id within the caller's group (another group's mapping reads as not-found).

500.description: Plain-text (not JSON) body: 'Error fetching check mapping: ...'.

guidance: The path id is the INGESTION row id from create_checks_mapping's response, not the githubCheckId or the check-configuration id.
Scoped to the caller's group: a mapping owned by another group returns 404, so a 404 does not prove the id never existed.
The 404 and 500 bodies are PLAIN TEXT, not JSON error objects, so do not try to parse them as {error:...}.
checkStates carries the evaluation status (created rows start at 'Not Started'); the joined checkConfiguration object gives the underlying check's name, project and type.

capabilities.name: list_check_configurations
capabilities.intent: List the SCM check-run configurations set up for a repository — the rules deciding which BrowserStack build/project a commit or PR check reports on, and whether it posts quality-gate or build status.

path_params.name: owner
path_params.description: VCS organisation / owner. Matched against the stored vcs_org_name.

path_params.name: repo
path_params.description: VCS repository name. Matched against the stored repo_name.

query.name: filter
query.description: Only the value 'enabled' (case-insensitive) is honoured: it restricts the listing to enabled checks. ANY other value is silently ignored and all checks are returned — this is not a general-purpose filter.

guidance: Gated by the CHECKS_EVALUATION entitlement (contrary to what one might assume for a read); without it the call is refused as feature-inaccessible.
Rows are scoped to the caller's group AND user, so you only see check configs you created — not the whole repository's.

When nothing is configured you get HTTP 200 with an empty checks list, not a 404; and if the lookup throws internally it also returns 200 with an EMPTY response object (null repoName/ownerName and no checks), so treat an all-null body as an error, not as 'no checks'.
filter accepts only 'enabled'; any other token is ignored rather than rejected, so a mistyped filter silently returns everything.

capabilities.name: create_check_configurations
capabilities.intent: Register up to 10 check-run configurations on a repository so BrowserStack posts a named check (quality-gate or build status) back to the VCS for commits/PRs, bound to a given project, build name and branch.

path_params.name: owner
path_params.description: VCS organisation / owner; stored as the check's vcs_org_name.

path_params.name: repo
path_params.description: VCS repository name; stored as the check's repo_name.

body.name: checks
body.description: The check configurations to create (1..10). Empty is rejected (400 'Checks list cannot be empty'); more than 10 is rejected. This is also capped against the repository's EXISTING count — max 10 per repository in total.

fields.name: checkName
fields.description: Display name of the check. Mandatory, non-blank. Part of the uniqueness key (checkName + repo + group + buildName + project).

fields.name: checkType
fields.description: What the check reports: QG_STATUS (quality-gate status) or BUILD_STATUS (build status). Mandatory.

fields.name: tool
fields.description: Source tool / VCS provider. Mandatory, non-blank.

fields.name: splitRepos
fields.description: Split-repos flag. Mandatory (@NotNull) — omitting it is a 400 even though it looks optional.

fields.name: buildName
fields.description: Target build name the check reports on. Mandatory, non-blank. Part of the uniqueness key.

fields.name: projectName
fields.description: Target project name. Mandatory, non-blank. Must resolve to an EXISTING project in the workspace, or the write is refused as project-not-found.

fields.name: branchName
fields.description: Branch to scope the check to (optional).

fields.name: buildTags
fields.description: Build tags used to select the build (optional).

fields.name: commitCheck
fields.description: Whether the check reports per-commit (optional).

fields.name: isEnabled
fields.description: Whether the check is active (optional).

guidance: Gated by the CHECKS_EVALUATION entitlement; without it the write is refused as feature-inaccessible.
Success is HTTP 201, but the SAME route returns HTTP 200 when nothing was actually saved (empty or all-dropped) — check the returned checks list, not just the status code.
At most 10 checks per repository IN TOTAL (existing + new), not just 10 per request; exceeding it is a 400 'Maximum 10 checks per repository'.
splitRepos is required despite reading like a flag — omit it and the call is a 400.
projectName must name a project that already exists in the workspace, otherwise the whole request fails with project-not-found.
Uniqueness is (checkName, repo, group, buildName, project); a duplicate collides on that key.
Checks are stored against the caller's group and user, so only you will see and be able to manage them afterwards.

capabilities.name: update_check_configuration
capabilities.intent: Edit an existing check-run configuration — its name, check type, tool, target project/build name, branch, tags, commit-check or enabled flag.

path_params.name: owner
path_params.description: VCS organisation / owner.

path_params.name: repo
path_params.description: VCS repository name.

path_params.name: checkId
path_params.description: Numeric check-configuration id (as a string in the path). A non-numeric value is a 400 'Invalid check ID format'.

body.name: checkName
body.description: Check name. Mandatory, non-blank.

body.name: checkType

Gated by CHECKS_EVALUATION; scoped to the caller's group and user — you cannot edit a teammate's check.
A missing/foreign check comes back as HTTP 204 with an empty body, NOT a 404 — do not read 204 as success without re-reading.
A non-numeric checkId is a 400 'Invalid check ID format'; projectName must resolve to an existing project.
To only flip the enabled flag, prefer toggle_check_configuration — it takes a single query param instead of the whole body.

guidance: isEnabled is a REQUIRED QUERY parameter (?isEnabled=true|false), not a body field — this is the most common mistake on this route.
Gated by CHECKS_EVALUATION and scoped to the caller's group and user.
A check that is not found comes back as HTTP 404 with an EMPTY body (unlike update, which uses 204 for the same case).
On success it returns the full updated check configuration, so you can confirm the new isEnabled value from the body.

capabilities.name: delete_check_configuration
capabilities.intent: Remove a check-run configuration so BrowserStack stops posting that check to the repository.

path_params.name: owner
path_params.description: VCS organisation / owner.

path_params.name: repo
path_params.description: VCS repository name.

path_params.name: checkId
path_params.description: Numeric check-configuration id (string in path); non-numeric is a 400 'Invalid check ID format'.

200.description: Plain-text (not JSON) body: 'Check configuration deleted successfully'.

guidance: Hard delete of the check-configuration row — there is no undo and no bin.

Only deletes a row matching the caller's group AND user, so you cannot delete a teammate's check config; that failure, like every other (including not-found and feature-inaccessible), is flattened into a generic 400 whose message oddly says '[updateCheckConfiguration]'.
Success returns a PLAIN-TEXT body 'Check configuration deleted successfully', not JSON, and there is no way to tell from the error whether the id existed.

capabilities.name: list_views
capabilities.intent: List the saved views (named filter presets) available to the caller for a screen — their own private views plus the group's public ones — to render the view switcher.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the views belong to. An unrecognised value is a 400 BAD_REQUEST ('Invalid view creation <value>'), not a 404.

guidance: Returns a bare JSON ARRAY of view objects (not wrapped in a data/success envelope) and is NOT paginated — the whole set for that screen comes back at once.

By default you get the caller's own views plus the group's public ones. If a Public-Link-Token / X-Public-Link-Token header is present, ONLY the group's public (level 2) views are returned — private views are never exposed on a shared link.
An unrecognised viewType is a 400, not a 404 — the valid set is builds, testRuns, testHealth, uniqueErrors, buildInsights.
Each row's id is the view UUID you carry into update_view / delete_view; level is 1 (private) or 2 (public).

capabilities.name: create_view
capabilities.intent: Save the caller's current filter selection as a named view for a screen, either private to them or public to the whole group, and return the stored view.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the view is for; sets the view's type. An unrecognised value is a 400.

body.name: name
body.description: View name. Required (@NotNull); note the internal surface does NOT reject a blank or over-long name (only the external surface does). Must be unique per screen type within the group (public) or within the creator (private).

body.name: query
body.description: The serialised filter this view stores, as a string. Required (@NotNull).

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility: 1 = private (only the creator), 2 = public (whole group). Required (@NotNull).

guidance: Requires the manage-custom-views permission (BUILD_MANAGE_VIEWS).
createdBy and groupId are taken from the session and cannot be set from the body — anything you send for them is overwritten.

Name uniqueness is enforced per screen type: within the group for public (level 2) views and within the creator for private (level 1) views. A clash returns a VIEW_NAME_EXISTS error (not an HTTP 409).
The internal surface only checks name/query are non-null — it accepts a blank or very long name. Use create_view_via_public_api if you want the stricter length limits enforced.
Returns the stored view (with its new UUID id) as a single object; take id for later update/delete.

capabilities.name: update_view
capabilities.intent: Rename a saved view, replace its stored filter query, or change its private/public visibility.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the view belongs to; sets the type used for the name-uniqueness check. An unrecognised value is a 400.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: View UUID. A view that does not exist is a 400 'View does not exists', not a 404.

body.name: name
body.description: New name. Omit to keep the stored name. Despite @NotNull on the model, an omitted field falls back to the stored value (partial update). A clash returns VIEW_NAME_EXISTS.

body.name: query
body.description: New serialised filter. Omit to keep the stored query.

body.name: level
body.description: New visibility (1 = private, 2 = public). Omit to keep the stored level.

200.description: Empty body — the updated view is NOT echoed back (unlike create_view). Re-list to see the result.

guidance: Requires the manage-custom-views permission (BUILD_MANAGE_VIEWS).
PARTIAL update despite being a PUT: omitted name/query/level fall back to the view's stored values.

For a PRIVATE view the caller must be the owner ('Not allowed to update this view'); the SQL also restricts updates to your own views OR public views in your group. A non-existent id is a 400 'View does not exists', not a 404.
A name clash returns VIEW_NAME_EXISTS (per screen type: within group for public, within creator for private).
Returns an empty 200 body on success — do not expect the updated view back; re-list to confirm.
There is no revision history: an overwritten name, query or level cannot be restored.

capabilities.name: delete_view
capabilities.intent: Delete a saved view the caller owns (or any public view in their group), removing it from everyone's view switcher.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: IGNORED by the handler — the delete is keyed only on the view id. Any string is accepted here and not validated.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: View UUID to delete. A non-owned / non-existent id surfaces as a 400 'not allowed to delete this view', not a 404 or 403.

200.description: Empty body on success.

400.description: Error (e.g. 'not allowed to delete this view') when the id is not owned by the caller and not a public view in their group, or does not exist.

guidance: HARD SQL delete of the view row — not a soft delete and NOT recoverable; the view vanishes from every group member's switcher immediately.
Requires the manage-custom-views permission (BUILD_MANAGE_VIEWS). The SQL further restricts deletion to views you created OR public (level 2) views in your group.
The viewType path segment is not validated or used — only the id matters — but it must still be present to match the route.
A non-owned or non-existent id comes back as a 400 'not allowed to delete this view', so a failure does not distinguish 'forbidden' from 'not found'.
There is no external (public-API) delete for views — this internal route is the only way to delete one.

capabilities.name: list_views_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: External/public API (used by the Atlas agent) to list the caller's saved views for a screen, so an integration can pick a saved view instead of rebuilding a filter query.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the views belong to. An unrecognised value is a 400.

guidance: Public /ext/v1 surface: authenticated with a BrowserStack username + access key over HTTP Basic, not the internal session token.
Returns a bare JSON ARRAY of view objects, scoped to the caller's user/group; not paginated. No public-link-token path here (unlike the internal list).
Thin adapter over the same view service as the internal list — results are the same set for the same caller. There is intentionally NO external delete operation.
An unrecognised viewType is a 400; valid values are builds, testRuns, testHealth, uniqueErrors, buildInsights.

capabilities.name: create_view_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: External/public API to save a filter query as a named view (private or shared with the org) for a screen.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the view is for; sets the view's type. An unrecognised value is a 400.

body.name: name
body.description: View name. Enforced at this public boundary to be non-blank and at most 100 characters (stricter than the internal surface). Must be unique per screen type within the group (public) or creator (private).

body.name: query
body.description: Serialised filter to store, as a string. Enforced non-blank and at most 4000 characters here.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility: 1 = private, 2 = shared with the org. Required; any other value is rejected with 'level must be 1 (private) or 2 (shared)'.

guidance: Public /ext/v1 surface: username + access-key HTTP Basic auth. Requires the manage-custom-views permission (works for both globalRBAC-on and -off orgs).
Stricter validation than the internal create: name must be non-blank and <=100 chars, query non-blank and <=4000 chars, level exactly 1 or 2 — each violation is its own 400 message.
type is set from the path and id/createdBy/groupId in the body are ignored; the creator and group come from the authenticated caller.
Name uniqueness is per screen type (group for public, creator for private); a clash returns VIEW_NAME_EXISTS.
Returns the stored view (with its UUID id) as a single object.

capabilities.name: update_view_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: External/public API to rename a saved view or replace its stored filter query / visibility level.

path_params.name: viewType
path_params.description: Screen the view belongs to; used for the name-uniqueness check and the ownership guard. An unrecognised value is a 400.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: View UUID. A non-UUID is a 400 'Invalid view id.'; an id not in the caller's own scoped view list is a 400 'View does not exist.' (closes a cross-tenant existence oracle).

body.name: name
body.description: View name. Validated non-blank and <=100 chars at this boundary.

body.name: query
body.description: Serialised filter to store. Validated non-blank and <=4000 chars.

body.name: level
body.description: Visibility: 1 = private, 2 = shared. Required; other values are a 400.

200.description: Empty body on success — the updated view is not echoed back.

guidance: Public /ext/v1 surface: username + access-key HTTP Basic auth, plus the manage-custom-views permission.
Unlike the internal update, this validates the payload the same way create does (name <=100, query <=4000, level 1|2) — all three are effectively required here.

Explicit ownership guard: the id must appear in the caller's own scoped view list, otherwise a 400 'View does not exist.' — this deliberately hides whether some other tenant's view id exists. A non-UUID is a 400 'Invalid view id.'.
Returns an empty 200 body; re-list to confirm. No revision history, so overwritten values cannot be restored.

capabilities.name: list_dashboard_views
capabilities.intent: List the dashboard views the current user can see (their own private ones plus group/shared ones) with name, visibility level, widget count and owner — the dashboard picker / dashboard list.

query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of project_id / project_name / project_identifier.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of project_id / project_name / project_identifier.

guidance: A project query param is mandatory here purely to satisfy the controller-wide project resolver; the returned list is not scoped by it, so passing any project the caller can access is enough.
The response is a bare `{data: [...]}` envelope with no `success` flag and no pagination — the whole visible set comes back in one call.

Each row carries the dashboard UUID under `data[].id`; carry that forward to get/update/delete/clone. The built-in views may or may not appear here, so address those by their `default` / `automation-trend` aliases on the read call rather than expecting them in this list.

capabilities.name: create_dashboard_view
capabilities.intent: Create a new custom dashboard view — its name, visibility level, global filters and widget layout — for the Test Observability (TO) or Test Management (TCM) dashboard page.

query.name: source
query.description: Which surface the dashboard belongs to. TO = Test Observability, TCM = Test Management.

query.name: project_id

query.name: project_name

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of project_id / project_name / project_identifier.

body.name: name
