guidance: The created dashboard is returned under `data`, with the assigned UUID at `data.id` — take that for subsequent get/update/delete/clone.
Name must be unique in the project; a clash is rejected rather than silently de-duplicated.
`level` defaults to 2 (group/shared); set it explicitly if you need a private dashboard.
`source` (TO vs TCM) decides which dashboard surface the view belongs to and is not part of the body — pass it as a query param (defaults to TO).

capabilities.name: get_dashboard_view
capabilities.intent: Load one dashboard view for rendering — its name, global filters and full widget configuration, with filter values injected for the built-in dashboards.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: A dashboard UUID, OR one of the read-only aliases `default` / `automation-trend`. `default` resolves to the TCM view when source=TCM and to the TO 'testing trends' view when source=TO; `automation-trend` resolves to the automation-trend view. Custom (non-built-in) UUIDs are scoped to the caller's user/group and read as not-found if they belong to someone else.

query.name: source
query.description: TO or TCM. Also disambiguates which view the `default` alias resolves to.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED (controller-wide project resolver).

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

guidance: SIDE EFFECT: reading a dashboard pushes it onto the caller's Redis 'recent views' list (capped at the most recent few), which is what the home recent-views listing returns. This write happens for ordinary users and is skipped only for super-users (except super-users in group 2). There is no read that avoids it.

For the built-in default dashboard the response is doctored: its date range is forced to the last 30 days regardless of what was stored, and widget filter values are injected — so what you read back is not necessarily what was persisted.
The aliases `default` and `automation-trend` work ONLY here (and other reads). Update, delete and clone-source require the raw UUID and reject the aliases.
The dashboard is under `data`; `data.isDefault` / `data.isAutomation` flag the built-in views, and `data.totalWidget` is the widget count.

capabilities.name: update_dashboard_view
capabilities.intent: Save changes to an existing dashboard view — rename it, change its visibility level, change its global filters, or persist an edited widget layout.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The dashboard UUID (raw UUID only — the `default` / `automation-trend` aliases are NOT accepted on this route). The update is additionally scoped to the caller's user/group.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED: it resolves the project and drives the DASHBOARD_UPDATE permission check.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

body.name: name
body.description: New name, 1-100 characters. Must stay unique within the project.

body.name: level
body.description: New visibility level.

body.name: desc
body.description: New description (capped at 100 characters).

body.name: filters
body.description: Replacement global filters (DashboardFilters shape — same as create).

body.name: widgets
body.description: Replacement widget layout (array of Widgets objects — same shape as create).

guidance: NO UNDO: dashboards keep no version history, so an overwritten name, filter set or widget layout is gone for good — read the current dashboard first if you need to preserve anything.
The three built-in dashboards (default TCM, default TO/testing-trends, automation-trend) cannot be updated — the call returns 400 'Cannot update default dashboard'.
The body replaces the fields it carries; send the full intended state (e.g. the complete widgets array) rather than a partial patch.
The path takes a raw UUID only. Unlike the read, `default` / `automation-trend` are not accepted here.

capabilities.name: delete_dashboard_view
capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a custom dashboard view and its widget layout.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The dashboard UUID (raw UUID only — aliases not accepted). The delete is scoped to the caller's user/group, so a UUID the caller has no permission on deletes nothing.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED: it resolves the project and drives the DASHBOARD_DELETE permission check.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

200.description: Deleted. Returns a bare success flag.

guidance: IRREVERSIBLE: the dashboard is hard-deleted with no version history and no bin — it cannot be restored.
The three built-in dashboards cannot be deleted — the call returns 400 'Cannot delete default dashboard'.
If nothing matched the scoped delete (wrong UUID, or a dashboard the caller cannot see/own), it fails with DASHBOARD_VIEW_NOT_FOUND rather than reporting success:true.
On success the body is just `{success: true}` — there is no echo of the deleted dashboard.

capabilities.name: clone_dashboard_view
capabilities.intent: Duplicate an existing dashboard — copy its filters, widgets, source and type into a new dashboard owned by the caller, under a new name.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: UUID of the SOURCE dashboard to copy (raw UUID only — aliases not accepted). The source is read with the caller's permission, so you can only clone a dashboard you can see.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED: it resolves the project and drives the DASHBOARD_CREATE permission check.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

body.name: name
body.description: Name for the NEW cloned dashboard, 1-100 chars, unique within the project. This is the only field of the body that is used — level, filters and widgets are copied verbatim from the source, not taken from the body.

The new name must be unique in the project; a duplicate is rejected.
The clone is owned by the calling user; the new dashboard (with its own UUID at `data.id`) is returned synchronously in `data`.
The source id must be a raw UUID — the `default` / `automation-trend` aliases are not accepted here even though the read accepts them.

capabilities.name: list_dashboard_view_widget_types
capabilities.intent: List the catalogue of widget types that can be added to a dashboard view (the 'add widget' palette) with their display names.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED by the controller-wide resolver even though this static catalogue does not use it.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

200.description: Static catalogue of addable widget types, returned as a BARE JSON ARRAY (no envelope).

This is static, hard-coded data (Test Case Statistics, Test Case Type, Test Case Trend) — it makes no DB or downstream call and does not vary by project, despite the mandatory project query param.
`key` is the WidgetTypeEnum value to send as a widget's `type` when building a dashboard layout or requesting widget data.

capabilities.name: list_dashboard_view_custom_field_filters
capabilities.intent: List the project's custom (user-defined) test-case fields that can be used as filters when configuring a test-case dashboard widget.

path_params.name: widgetType
path_params.description: A WidgetTypeEnum value. Only TEST_CASE_TREND, TEST_CASE_STATISTICS_CARD and TEST_CASE_TYPE are valid here; any other widget type returns 400 'Custom Filters are not available for widget type: X'.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED (controller-wide resolver); the custom fields returned are this project's.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

200.description: Custom-field filters for the project, as a BARE JSON ARRAY (no envelope).

capabilities.name: list_dashboard_widget_filter_values
capabilities.intent: Fetch the selectable values for one filter inside a dashboard widget's filter editor (the type-ahead / value picker) — e.g. the build names, tags, users, teams or test-case field values available for a project, given the currently applied filters.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number for the value list. Note the param is `page` (not `p`).

query.name: per_page
query.description: Values per page (default 30). No server-side upper bound was found in the resolved code — see guidance.

query.name: search
query.description: Type-ahead substring to narrow the returned values.

query.name: source
query.description: TO or TCM. With source=TCM the request is forced to includeManualAndAutomated=true.

query.name: project_id
query.description: One of project_id / project_name / project_identifier is REQUIRED. The resolved project OVERWRITES whatever `filters.projects` is in the body.

query.name: project_name
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

body.name: widgetKey
body.description: REQUIRED (@NotNull). The widget type (WidgetTypeEnum) the filter belongs to. Note the wire key is `widgetKey`, not `widget` or `type`.

body.name: filterKey
body.description: REQUIRED (@NotNull). Which filter's values to fetch. This is the field that selects the value set (the server switches on filterKey, not on widgetKey). filterKey=buildName additionally turns on selective project filtering.

body.name: filters
body.description: The currently applied filters (WidgetFiltersValue) used to scope the value list. Optional — an omitted/null value is treated as empty. Its `projects` is always overwritten by the project resolved from the query params, so setting it in the body is pointless.

body.name: filterId
body.description: Optional custom-field id, used when filterKey targets a specific custom field.

guidance: POST but READ-ONLY (@ReadOnly) — it fetches filter values and changes nothing.
The value set is chosen by `filterKey`, and `widgetKey` must also be present (both are @NotNull); the two are separate fields and the server dispatches on filterKey.

Pagination params are `page` and `per_page` (default 30), NOT `p`/`count`. `data` is a map keyed by the filter, each value a list of value structs; `info` carries page metadata and `fullList` says whether the whole set fit in the page.
`filters.projects` is always replaced by the project from the query params, so passing project ids in the body is ignored — set the project via project_id/project_name/project_identifier.
A public-link token may be supplied via the `Public-Link-Token` (or the observability public-link-token) header to run in shared read-only dashboard mode.
With source=TCM the request is forced to include both manual and automated runs.

capabilities.name: check_dashboard_widget_ignored_filters

query.name: project_name

query.name: project_identifier
query.description: Alternative project selector. Supply exactly one of the three.

The body is a full WidgetFiltersValue object, but ONLY five fields are actually read: testCaseRequirements (issueIds + issueType), testCasePriorities, testCaseTags, testCaseStatuses and testCaseTypes. Every other filter field you send is silently ignored here.

The response reports, per filter type, how many values still match vs are ignored (`filterMatches[]` with matchedValuesCount / ignoredValuesCount / isMismatched), a total `ignoredFiltersCount`, and an overall `isMismatched` flag — use these to flag or drop stale chips.

capabilities.name: create_log_redaction_rule

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (not its numeric id). Resolved within the caller's group; a project outside the group is treated as not found.

body.name: pattern
body.description: The RE2J regex whose matches are replaced with [MASKED] in future ingested logs. Required on create (a null/blank pattern is a 400). RE2J only — backreferences and lookaround are rejected. Must be unique within the project; a duplicate pattern is a 400.

body.name: description
body.description: Optional human note for the rule. At most 255 characters (enforced by validation).

body.name: enabled
body.description: Whether the rule masks logs. Omitted or null defaults to true. Only enabled rules cause masking; if a project has zero enabled rules it is dropped from redaction entirely.

capabilities.intent: Add a regex log-redaction rule to a project so matching substrings in future ingested test logs are masked with [MASKED] — use this to scrub secrets or PII from logs.
guidance: The pattern is a RE2J (Google RE2) regex, NOT java.util.regex: backreferences and lookaround compile fine in Java but are rejected here with a 400. Dry-run it first with test_log_redaction_pattern.
A project is capped at 10 redaction rules; the 11th create returns a 400 naming the limit.
The pattern must be unique in the project — re-posting an existing pattern is a 400, not a no-op.
Only affects logs ingested AFTER this call, and it takes effect with a small lag (the rule is mirrored to the pipeline cache only after the DB commit). Existing logs are never re-redacted.
The new rule is appended at the end of the priority order (highest priorityOrder). Use reorder_log_redaction_rules to change where it runs.
Returns the created rule at the TOP LEVEL (201) — not wrapped in a {rules:[...]} or {data:...} envelope. Take its integer id for later update/delete/reorder.

capabilities.name: list_log_redaction_rules

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name. Resolved within the caller's group; a foreign project is treated as not found.

capabilities.intent: List a project's log-redaction rules, in the priority order the ingestion pipeline applies them — the source of the integer rule ids that update, delete and reorder need.
guidance: Rules come back inside a {rules:[...]} wrapper, ordered by priorityOrder ascending (the order they are applied to each log line).
Returns every rule regardless of enabled state; check each rule's enabled flag to know which actually mask.
Not paginated — the whole list is returned (a project holds at most 10 rules).

capabilities.name: update_log_redaction_rule

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name. Resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: ruleId
path_params.description: Integer id of the redaction rule to edit (from list_log_redaction_rules). A rule id not in this project is a 404.

body.name: pattern
body.description: New RE2J regex. PARTIAL UPDATE: omit it (or send null) to leave the pattern unchanged — it is NOT cleared. When present it is re-validated (RE2J syntax + <=1024 chars) and must stay unique in the project.

body.name: description
body.description: New description. Null/omitted leaves it unchanged — there is no way to clear an existing description through this call.

body.name: enabled
body.description: Toggle the rule on/off. Null/omitted leaves it unchanged. Disabling the last enabled rule drops the project from redaction after the change commits.

capabilities.intent: Edit one log-redaction rule — change its regex, its description, or toggle it on/off — without deleting and re-creating it.
guidance: Partial semantics: a null/omitted field means 'leave as is', never 'clear'. To blank a description you cannot use this call.
A changed pattern is re-validated as RE2J and must remain unique; a duplicate or invalid pattern is a 400.
Toggling enabled takes effect on the pipeline with a small lag (Redis mirror refreshed post-commit); already-ingested logs are unaffected either way.
Returns the updated rule at the top level (no envelope), same shape as create.

capabilities.name: delete_log_redaction_rule

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name. Resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: ruleId
path_params.description: Integer id of the redaction rule to remove (from list_log_redaction_rules). A rule id not in this project is a 404.

capabilities.intent: Permanently remove a log-redaction rule from a project so its pattern no longer masks newly ingested logs.
guidance: Irreversible: there is no undo or version history — the rule must be re-created by hand to bring it back.
Logs already masked by this rule stay masked; the original text was never stored, so deletion never un-redacts past logs.
The remaining rules' priorities are compacted (renumbered) after the delete. Deleting the last enabled rule drops the project from redaction, applied to the pipeline after commit.
Success is an empty HTTP 200 with no body.

capabilities.name: reorder_log_redaction_rules

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name. Resolved within the caller's group.

body.name: orderedIds
body.description: The project's redaction-rule ids (integers) in the desired new priority order — first id becomes priority 1. Must be a non-empty list containing EXACTLY all the project's rule ids, each exactly once: a missing id, an extra id, a duplicate, or a null entry is a 400.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: A redaction rule id belonging to this project.

capabilities.intent: Re-prioritise a project's log-redaction rules by submitting all their ids in the desired order — order matters because rules mask each log line in priority sequence.
guidance: You must submit the COMPLETE set of the project's rule ids, no more and no fewer, with no duplicates; a partial list is rejected with a 400, not applied to a subset. List the rules first to get the full id set.
Priorities are rewritten to a contiguous 1..N in the order given (first id = priority 1 = applied first).
Reordering does not change which patterns mask or the enabled set — only their order — so it refreshes the per-project pipeline cache but not the project's redaction membership.
Returns the full reordered rule list inside a {rules:[...]} wrapper.

capabilities.name: test_log_redaction_pattern

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name. Used only to prove the caller has access to the project; nothing project-specific is applied to the evaluation.

body.name: pattern
body.description: The RE2J regex to dry-run. Must not be blank (400) and is compiled + length-capped exactly like a real rule (<=1024 chars, RE2J syntax).

body.name: logLines
body.description: Sample log lines to evaluate against the pattern. 1 to 50 lines; each line must be non-blank. An empty list, more than 50 lines, or a blank line is a 400.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: One sample log line (non-blank).

capabilities.intent: Dry-run a redaction regex before saving it: supply a pattern plus sample log lines and get back, per line, the original text, the [MASKED] result, whether it matched and how many matches — the 'preview' behind redaction settings.
guidance: POST but purely evaluative — nothing is stored and no existing rule is consulted; safe to call repeatedly to iterate on a pattern.
RE2J only (backreferences/lookaround rejected) and the same 1024-char cap as a real rule, so a pattern that passes here will pass create/update validation.
Response echoes the pattern and a per-line results array; each result carries original, redacted, matched and matchCount so you can confirm exactly what would be masked.

capabilities.name: list_log_redaction_rules_for_pipeline

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName

capabilities.name: validate_regex_pattern

capabilities.intent: Edit an existing repo configuration — change its build name or repository details (repo, branch, type) used for AI tag generation.
guidance: Requires the account's per-user AI feature to be enabled; refused with AI off.

Full replace, not a patch: BOTH `build_name` and a non-empty `repo_details` must be sent every time. Omitting `repo_details` to 'keep it as-is' is a 400, and a partial `repo_details` overwrites the whole stored set.
There is NO undo — the previous repository details are gone once replaced and no version history is kept. Read the configuration first if you need to preserve any existing entries.
The edit is synced to the downstream code-tag service with a single attempt and rolled back locally if that sync fails, so a failed edit leaves the stored configuration unchanged.
Returns the updated configuration under `result`.

capabilities.name: delete_repo_setting

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Integer id of the configuration to remove.

capabilities.intent: Unlink a repository configuration from a project, stopping further AI tag generation from that repo.
guidance: Requires the account's per-user AI feature to be enabled; refused with AI off.

Two-phase and best-effort atomic: the local link is deleted, then a single no-retry removal is pushed to the downstream code-tag service. If that downstream removal fails the local row is restored and the call errors (TCS_SERVICE_ERROR) — so a failed delete leaves everything as it was, and you can retry.
The success body is a small envelope, `result: {id, status: "deleted"}`, echoing the id you removed — not the deleted configuration's contents.
The configuration itself is removed; there is no restore for it through this API.

capabilities.intent: Kick off AI generation of test tags for a configured repository — optionally steered by a custom prompt — by syncing the config to the code-tag service and asking it to (re)scan the code. Poll the generation status afterwards for completion.
guidance: Requires the account's per-user AI feature to be enabled; refused with AI off.
This is where the configuration first reaches the downstream code-tag service — if you created it and never triggered generation, status and generated-tags reads will find nothing upstream.

Asynchronous: the response is the downstream service's own JSON acknowledgement passed through verbatim, NOT the finished tags. Observe completion by polling the tag-generation-status call; do not treat this response as the result.
The response shape is owned by the downstream service and is not fixed by this API. A blank or unparseable upstream response surfaces as TCS_SERVICE_ERROR rather than an empty success.
The `custom_prompt` is persisted onto the configuration (on the test-type repo entry) only after the downstream service accepts the call — a rejected call does not store it.

path_params.name: projectName

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Integer id of the configuration whose generation run you are polling.

capabilities.intent: Poll the progress/state of an AI tag-generation run for a repo configuration, so a UI can show 'in progress / done / failed'.
guidance: Pass-through of the downstream code-tag service's status JSON, unmodified; the shape is owned by that service and not fixed by this API.

'Not started' and 'nothing to report' look identical: when no generation run has ever been registered for this project+build+repo the downstream 404 is translated into an EMPTY JSON object with HTTP 200. An empty `{}` therefore means 'no run yet', not an error.
A configuration only registers with the downstream service on its first generation trigger, so an empty status right after create is expected — trigger generation first, then poll here.

capabilities.intent: Fetch a page of the AI-generated test tags for a repo configuration, for review before they are used.
guidance: Pass-through proxy: the body is the downstream code-tag service's JSON unmodified, so the tag/list shape is owned by that service and not fixed by this API.

Pagination clamps happen at this service (`per_page` 1..500), but the internal page ceiling and total-count shape come from the downstream response — read whatever paging fields that body carries to know when to stop.
Returns nothing meaningful until a generation run has produced tags; before that the downstream response may be empty. Trigger generation and confirm via the status poll first.

Pass-through proxy: the body is the downstream code-tag service's JSON unmodified and its shape is owned by that service.
Unpaginated and returns everything at once, so it can be large and slow. Use the paginated generated-tags read for interactive review and this one only for a full export.

capabilities.name: get_smart_tag_settings

capabilities.intent: Read a project's smart-tag thresholds — the rules that decide when a test is labelled Flaky, Always Failing, New Failure or a Performance Anomaly.
guidance: No permission check on this read — any caller who can reach the project can read the thresholds.
The four rule groups (`flaky`, `alwaysFailing`, `newFailure`, `performanceAnomalies`) are returned at the top level with no wrapper envelope — there is no `success`/`result` key on this response.

`flaky` has two sub-rules, `flakeInHistory` and `flakeInRerun`; the other three groups each carry an `enabled` flag plus their threshold fields. Read these before an update, since the update replaces the whole settings object.

fields.description: Required flag; defaults to true.

fields.name: flakeInHistory
fields.description: History-based flaky rule: `enabled` (boolean), `flippingCount` (integer 1..29) and `consecutiveRuns` (integer 5..30). CROSS-FIELD RULE: flippingCount must be strictly less than consecutiveRuns, else 400.

fields.name: flakeInRerun
fields.description: Rerun-based flaky rule: `enabled` (boolean) and `consecutiveRuns` (integer, max 30).

body.name: alwaysFailing
body.description: Always-failing rule.

fields.name: failureType
fields.description: Which failures count toward the streak. Default SAME.

fields.name: consecutiveRuns
fields.description: Consecutive failing runs threshold, range 2..30. Default 5.

body.name: newFailure
body.description: New-failure rule.

fields.name: failureType
fields.description: Default NEW.

fields.name: consecutiveRuns
fields.description: Range 2..30. Default 5.

body.name: performanceAnomalies
body.description: Performance-anomaly rule.

fields.name: durationPercentile
fields.description: Duration percentile threshold, range 80..99. Default 95.

fields.name: consecutiveRuns
fields.description: Consecutive-run window, range 30..100. Default 100.

capabilities.intent: Tune a project's smart-tag detection rules — e.g. how many status flips within how many consecutive runs make a test flaky — which changes how tests are tagged across the project's reports.
guidance: Requires the `modify_project_settings` permission on the project's tags setting; a caller without it gets 403.

The flaky `flakeInHistory.flippingCount` must be STRICTLY LESS than `flakeInHistory.consecutiveRuns`. This is checked FIRST — before the project is looked up and before the permission check — so an equal-or-greater flipping count returns 400 even for a caller who would otherwise be refused with 403.

Field ranges are enforced: flakeInHistory.flippingCount 1..29, flakeInHistory.consecutiveRuns 5..30, flakeInRerun.consecutiveRuns max 30, alwaysFailing/newFailure.consecutiveRuns 2..30, performanceAnomalies.durationPercentile 80..99 and performanceAnomalies.consecutiveRuns 30..100. Out-of-range values are 400.

This replaces the whole settings object rather than patching one rule; read the current settings first and send the complete structure back with your change. It is reversible by setting values again, but no prior-value history is kept.
Success returns only a small `{success, id}` envelope — NOT the saved settings. Re-read the settings to confirm the stored values.

Automate / app-automate / test-management hosts are rewritten to the observability print host; a numeric test-management project id in the path is swapped for the project's normalised name; and test-management report print URLs are tagged source=TCM so manual runs still render.
Any non-https scheme, an URL with embedded credentials, or a host outside the allow-list comes back as 400 INVALID_URL — the same error for every URL problem.
Requires the download-report plan feature; without it the call is 403 FORBIDDEN_OPERATION even though you hold the report/download-share permission.

capabilities.name: create_self_healing_pr

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: The build whose healing report the selectors were chosen from.

body.name: selectors
body.description: The healed selectors to apply. 1..200 items. Each carries `using`/`value` (NOT `type`/`value`) for both the original and healed locator — note this differs from the verdict endpoint, which uses `type`. There is no `elementIdentifier` here.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The healed-selector id from the healing report; must be non-blank. Used to group files and to derive the head branch name.

fields.name: originalLocator
fields.description: The broken locator to find and replace in source.

fields.name: using
fields.description: Locator strategy, e.g. xpath / css. Non-blank, max 64 chars.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The original locator string. Non-blank, max 4000 chars.

fields.name: healedLocator
fields.description: The replacement locator to write in.

fields.name: sessionId
fields.description: Session the selector broke in. Non-blank, max 64. Distinct sessionIds across the batch must be <= 25 (each triggers one source-file lookup); over that the whole request is rejected.

body.name: baseBranch
body.description: Branch to open the PR against. Optional — defaults to the build's recorded VCS branch; if neither is present the call fails as missing VCS info.

body.name: headBranch
body.description: Branch the changes are committed on. Optional — auto-generated as browserstack/heal-<buildUuid>-<hash> when blank. Must be a valid git ref: no '..', no leading/trailing '/', no '//'.

body.name: repository
body.description: Target repo in `owner/repo` form. Optional — auto-derived from the build's GitHub origin remote when blank. Auto-derivation is GitHub-only; a GitHub Enterprise / non-github.com host MUST pass this explicitly or the call fails as unparseable remote.

body.name: title
body.description: PR title. Optional — a default is generated. If supplied it must be 10..200 chars; it is prefixed with '[BrowserStack Heal] ' unless it already starts with that.

body.name: description
body.description: PR body. Optional — a default is generated. Control characters are stripped (newlines/tabs kept).

guidance: Asynchronous: returns HTTP 202 with only `{healingPrId, status:"IN_PROGRESS"}`. The PR is NOT open yet — there is no prUrl in this response. Capture healingPrId and poll get_self_healing_pr_status for the outcome and the PR URL.
The job id lives only in Redis with a short TTL and is not listed anywhere, so if you lose it or stop polling in time it is gone — store it from this response immediately.

Preconditions that reject synchronously before any work: an operational kill switch may disable the feature (global or per-group); the AI feature must be within plan/entitlement and the build must not be plan-locked; the build must carry VCS info and resolve to a GitHub owner/repo; at least one selector; <= 25 distinct sessions; and after source-file resolution <= 100 files.
Rate limited per user (25/hr) and per group (100/hr). Over-limit calls are rejected; a transient downstream failure refunds the token rather than burning your quota.
This is GitHub-only. A non-GitHub origin remote is silently skipped during auto-derivation (you then get an unparseable-remote error) — pass `repository` explicitly for those.
Each selector's locator uses `using`/`value`. Do not send `type` here (that is the verdict endpoint's field); an object missing `using` or `value` fails validation.
No API undo: this opens a real PR in the customer's repo. Closing/reverting is done in GitHub, not here.

429.description: Rate limited (per-user 25/hr or per-group 100/hr) via HEALING_PR_RATE_LIMITED.

capabilities.name: get_self_healing_pr_status
capabilities.intent: Poll a self-healing PR job started by create_self_healing_pr — get its in-progress/terminal state and, once ready, the created pull request URL.

path_params.name: healingPrId
path_params.description: The job id returned by create_self_healing_pr (strict lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 hex UUID).

guidance: `status` is one of IN_PROGRESS, SUCCEEDED, PARTIAL, FAILED, NO_CHANGES_NEEDED. Treat PARTIAL and NO_CHANGES_NEEDED as successful terminal outcomes, not failures.

prUrl / prNumber / headSha are null until a terminal, PR-producing state; perFileReport (per-file applied/skipped detail) and errorMessage appear depending on the outcome. Do not expect a PR URL while IN_PROGRESS.
Status is stored only in Redis under a group-scoped key with a TTL. An unknown or EXPIRED id returns HEALING_PR_NOT_FOUND — that is not a terminal failure state, just a lapsed/foreign id.
Only visible to the group that initiated the PR.

404.description: HEALING_PR_NOT_FOUND — the id is unknown or its Redis entry expired, or it belongs to another group.

capabilities.name: submit_self_healing_verdict
capabilities.intent: Record a reviewer's verdict on one AI-healed locator ('accurate' or 'inaccurate', with optional feedback) to feed the human-in-the-loop healing loop.

body.name: healedLocator
body.description: The healed locator being judged. Note the field is `type` here (xpath|cssPath), NOT `using` as in create_self_healing_pr.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Locator strategy; must be exactly 'xpath' or 'cssPath'.

fields.name: value
fields.description: The healed locator string. Non-blank.

body.name: verdict
body.description: The review outcome; must be exactly 'accurate' or 'inaccurate'.

body.name: elementIdentifier
body.description: Identifier of the element the locator targets; part of the hash that keys the verdict in TCG. Non-blank.

body.name: baseUrl
body.description: Web automate: the page URL; required for the web hash (baseUrl + elementIdentifier + groupId). Leave null/empty for app automate.

body.name: screenIdentifier
body.description: App automate only: native screen name used in the app hash (elementIdentifier + groupId + screenIdentifier). Null for web automate.

body.name: client
body.description: Platform client type: 'app-automate' selects the app hash formula; empty/null means web automate.

body.name: feedback
body.description: Optional free-form feedback (arbitrary JSON).

body.name: region
body.description: Optional session region code; only a lookup key into the TCG region-URL map (a miss is skipped, not an error). Max 64.

guidance: Gated on the human-in-the-loop healing feature per group: when it is OFF this is refused outright (FORBIDDEN_OPERATION) — unlike list_self_healing_verdicts, which silently returns []. Check the feature before submitting.
Requires a full product role (Product Admin, Product User, Admin or User); Viewer / Read Only is rejected.
Dual-writes to observability storage AND the TCG service (keyed by a hash of the element identifier), so a TCG outage can fail the call even though it looks like a local write.
Unknown body keys are ignored. For web tests supply baseUrl; for app tests supply screenIdentifier and client='app-automate' — the wrong pairing computes a hash that won't match the element.

capabilities.name: list_self_healing_verdicts
capabilities.intent: List the human-in-the-loop verdicts (accurate/inaccurate) already recorded against a build's AI-healed locators, to show which healed selectors have been reviewed.
guidance: Returns a bare JSON array of verdict objects (no wrapper envelope).

Feature-flagged: when the human-in-the-loop healing feature is OFF for the group this returns an empty array with HTTP 200 — NOT an error. Do not read [] as 'no verdicts recorded' without knowing the feature is on.

`isCarryover` is true when the verdict was first recorded against a different (earlier) build; `carryoverBuildSerialId` names that build. Join `elementHash` with the healing report to line each verdict up with its selector.
A build UUID outside the caller's group is rejected as build-not-found.

capabilities.name: get_build_self_heal_summary
capabilities.intent: Get a build's self-healing headline numbers for the build-insights page — how many tests and locators were healed, with counts and percentages.

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build UUID.

guidance: Numbers come from search aggregations over the build's runs: testSummary (totalTests, healedTests, percentHealedTests), locatorSummary (totalLocators, healedLocators, percentHealedLocators) and buildSummary (totalBuild, healedBuilds, percentHealedBuilds).
Refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / plan-feature-not-allowed when the build is locked by plan quota — you get an error, not zeroes.
In the demo-sandbox environment this returns hardcoded dummy stats, not real data.

capabilities.name: get_build_comparison_aggregation
capabilities.intent: Get the headline counts for a base-vs-target build comparison — additional, dropped, no-change, newly failed, started passing, and failed-with-a-different-reason — the summary strip at the top of the Build Comparison page.

query.name: base
query.description: Base build UUID (top-level parent build). Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: target
query.description: Target build UUID (top-level parent build). Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: filterParams
query.description: Standard V2 test filters bound from the query string (same filter keys as the build test listing), applied to both builds before comparing.

guidance: Plan-gated on the build-comparison feature: FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / plan-feature-not-allowed otherwise. A successful call also bumps feature-usage counters.

Both builds must be top-level parents and supported: a child/archived/locked build is rejected as unsupported (BUILD_COMPARISON_BUILD_NOT_SUPPORTED). Normalise UUIDs with resolve_build_comparison_parent_uuids first.
A cross-source (incompatible) pair is NOT an error: you get 200 with all six counts at 0 and `sourceFencingFlags` populated. Check sourceFencingFlags before trusting the zeroes.
Expensive: resolves both builds' child builds and runs search + aggregation across them.
The controller method is internally named getBuildUuid but it returns counts, not a UUID — ignore the name.

capabilities.name: check_build_comparison_available
capabilities.intent: Pre-flight check of whether two builds can actually be compared (and why not), so the UI can show a 'comparison unavailable' state before firing the expensive aggregation.

query.name: base
query.description: Base build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: target
query.description: Target build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

guidance: Same build-comparison plan gate as the aggregation — refused when the plan lacks the feature.

For an incompatible-source pair it returns `sourceFencingFlags` and NO availability payload (status/message null); otherwise status/message describe whether the comparison is available. Check the flags first.
Same unsupported-build rejection as the other comparison endpoints for child/archived/locked builds.
Use this before get_build_comparison_aggregation / list_build_comparison_bucket_tests to avoid the heavy call when the pair can't be compared.

capabilities.name: resolve_build_comparison_parent_uuids
capabilities.intent: Normalise two build UUIDs (which may be re-run/child builds) to their top-level parent build UUIDs — call this first so a rerun UUID pasted into the comparison picker is compared at the parent level.

query.name: base
query.description: Base build UUID to resolve (may be a child/rerun UUID). Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: target
query.description: Target build UUID to resolve. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

guidance: Returns `{base, target}` where each is the resolved top-level PARENT build UUID. Feed these into the other comparison calls.
NOT plan-gated (unlike the other four comparison endpoints) — works even without the build-comparison feature.

Any resolution failure is collapsed into a single BUILD_NOT_FOUND naming whichever of the two UUIDs appeared in the underlying error message; you cannot tell from the error which side genuinely failed.
sourceFencingFlags is part of the envelope but is not set on the normal success path here.

capabilities.name: list_build_comparison_bucket_tests
capabilities.intent: List the actual tests inside one bucket of a build comparison (e.g. newly-failed, started-passing, dropped, additional), grouped for display — the drill-down when a user clicks an aggregation tile.

query.name: base
query.description: Base build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: target
query.description: Target build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: bucket
query.description: Which comparison bucket to list (the categories returned by get_build_comparison_aggregation, e.g. newlyFailed / startedPassing / droppedTests / additionalTests / noChange / failedWithDifferentReason).

query.name: fileOffset
query.description: Pagination cursor (Long) over the grouped result; start at 0 and advance it to page through groups. Required.

query.name: filterParams
query.description: Standard V2 test filters bound from the query string, applied before matching.

guidance: Plan-gated on the build-comparison feature.

Returns `{bucketName, groups}` where each group bundles a file/browser/device/os and its `scopes`, each scope holding base/target element pairs. A cross-source pair returns an empty `groups` with `sourceFencingFlags` set rather than an error.
Expensive: pulls test-run ids for both builds (and their child builds) from search with a large per-build ceiling (~10k) before matching.
`fileOffset` is a cursor, not a page number; carry the last value forward to continue. The page size / total is not returned as a simple count — walk until a page comes back empty.

capabilities.name: get_build_comparison_meta
capabilities.intent: Get the two build summary headers shown side by side on the Build Comparison page — name, status, timings, framework and status counts for both the base and the target build.

query.name: base
query.description: Base build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

query.name: target
query.description: Target build UUID. Empty/missing → build-not-found.

guidance: Returns `{base, target}`, each a full build summary object. A cross-source pair returns the envelope with `sourceFencingFlags` set and base/target null.
NOT explicitly plan-gated (unlike aggregation/list/checkComparison), but it DOES apply the same unsupported-build rejection and source-fencing behaviour.

The status counts are AMR-corrected: it re-runs the same dedup/coalesce aggregation the buckets use so the header agrees with them, and silently falls back to raw automation counts if that recompute fails. This makes it heavier than a plain build-summary fetch.

capabilities.name: create_comment
capabilities.intent: Post a comment (or a reply, by passing threadId) on a build, test run or test with rich-text content and @mentions — the collaboration primitive on build-insights and test-detail pages.

path_params.name: normalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalised name; resolved to the project within the caller's group (this is what scopes access).

body.name: type
body.description: Which page/context the comment is on. Closed enum, serialised by NAME (not the display value).

body.name: commentHtml
body.description: Rich-text HTML body. It is sanitised and stored as the comment's `content` — note the response returns it under `content`, not `commentHtml`.

body.name: commentNode
body.description: The structured (editor node) representation of the body, stored alongside the HTML.

body.name: mentions
body.description: Group user ids (integers) to @mention. Each is notified shortly after the comment is posted.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: A group user id.

body.name: buildUuid
body.description: Build the comment is attached to.

body.name: buildSerialId
body.description: Numeric serial id of the build; this is what the comment reads key on.

body.name: threadId
body.description: Pass an existing threadId to REPLY into that thread; omit to start a new thread (a fresh threadId is generated and returned).

body.name: runUuid
body.description: Test-run UUID when the comment is on a specific run.

body.name: testHash
body.description: Test hash when the comment is on a specific test.

guidance: Plan-gated on the comments feature: refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / plan-feature-not-allowed when the plan lacks comments.

The returned comment has your HTML under `content` (sanitised), NOT under `commentHtml`. Capture `id` and `threadId` from the response — the id is the only handle for later edit/delete, and threadId is what you pass back to reply.
Omit threadId for a top-level comment (server mints one); pass it to reply into an existing thread.
@mentioned users are notified ~5s later as a side effect; the notification fires even though the call has already returned.
Access is scoped by resolving the project's normalised name within your group — a name outside your group fails to resolve.

capabilities.name: update_comment
capabilities.intent: Edit the body and mention list of an existing comment you authored.

path_params.name: normalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalised name. It is resolved but does NOT scope the update — the comment `id` in the body drives it (scoped to your own userId).

body.name: id
body.description: The comment id (UUID) to edit. The comment is located by this id AND the caller's own userId — you can only edit your own comment.

body.name: commentHtml
body.description: New rich-text HTML; sanitised and written to the comment's `content`.

body.name: commentNode
body.description: New structured (editor node) body.

body.name: mentions
body.description: Replacement mention list (group user ids). Overwrites the previous mentions.

body.name: createdAt
body.description: The comment's original creation timestamp. Accepted, but the update is actually located by `id` + your userId — this value is not used to find or re-key the document on this route, so a wrong/omitted value does not misdirect the edit.

guidance: Plan-gated on the comments feature.
Response is the PLAIN STRING "updated", not JSON — do not parse it as an object or read fields off it.
You can only edit your OWN comment: if no document matches the id + your userId you get COMMENT_NOT_FOUND (and MULTIPLE_COMMENTS_FOUND in the unlikely event of duplicates).
commentHtml is stored as `content`; commentNode, content and mentions are overwritten and modifiedAt is set to now. No version history — there is no API undo, the previous body is gone.
`createdAt` is accepted but ignored for locating the comment on this route; only `id` (plus your userId) is used.

capabilities.name: list_comments
capabilities.intent: Fetch the comments to render inline on a build-insights or test listing page — comments for a build (and a window of preceding build numbers), optionally narrowed to one test, to your own comments/mentions, and optionally excluding re-runs.

path_params.name: normalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalised name (resolved within the caller's group).

query.name: type
query.description: Comment page type (same enum as create_comment, by NAME). REQUIRED in practice — omitting it returns [] with 200.

query.name: buildSerialId
query.description: Numeric build serial id. REQUIRED in practice — omitting it returns [] with 200 (not an error). The read looks back over a fixed window of preceding serial ids from this value.

query.name: buildUuid
query.description: Build UUID to scope to when no runUuid is given.

query.name: runUuid
query.description: When set (and not in re-run mode), scopes to this run instead of the whole build.

query.name: testHash
query.description: Required when type=TESTS — type=TESTS without a testHash returns [] with 200. Also used to scope re-run/expand-all test queries.

query.name: expandAll
query.description: Expand the full set for the context rather than a collapsed view; changes how buildUuid/testHash filtering is applied.

query.name: showMyComments
query.description: Restrict to comments you authored or were mentioned in.

query.name: showReRunComments
query.description: Include comments across re-run builds. REQUIRES parentBuildUuid — set without it throws INVALID_PARAMETERS_FOR_COMMENTS.

query.name: parentBuildUuid
query.description: Parent build UUID; mandatory whenever showReRunComments=true.

guidance: Returns a bare JSON array of comment objects (no envelope). Note the array items carry `commentNode` but NOT the `content` HTML.

Silent empties: missing buildSerialId, missing type, or type=TESTS without testHash all return [] with HTTP 200 — easy to misread as 'no comments'. Supply buildSerialId and type (and testHash for TESTS).
showReRunComments=true without parentBuildUuid is a hard error (INVALID_PARAMETERS_FOR_COMMENTS), not an empty list.
Only looks back a FIXED number of preceding build serial ids from buildSerialId (so recurring discussion carries over), not all history, and is further bounded by the plan's data-retention window.

capabilities.name: list_build_comment_threads
capabilities.intent: Power the build-level comments side panel — list the comment threads across a build and all its re-runs, grouped by thread and ordered by most recent activity, with each thread's page type and test-run uuid for deep-linking.

path_params.name: normalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalised name (resolved within the caller's group).

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: PARENT build UUID. Threads are aggregated across all builds sharing this parent uuid — passing a re-run's own uuid returns nothing.

query.name: showMyComments
query.description: Restrict to threads involving comments you authored or were mentioned in.

guidance: Returns a bare JSON array of thread summaries (threadId, commentCount, the thread's page type and testRunUuid for deep-linking), not the individual comments — fetch a thread's comments via list_comments.
`buildId` must be the PARENT build uuid; a re-run's uuid yields an empty result, not an error.
Thread aggregation is capped at 1000 threads, and results are bounded by the plan's data-retention window so older threads silently drop out.

capabilities.name: list_test_run_comments_via_public_api
capabilities.intent: Public API: fetch the discussion thread on a test run — the comments testers left against that failure, with author info.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Numeric test-run id (Long).

guidance: Public /ext/v1 route: authenticate with the customer username + access key, not the internal session.
Read-only — there is NO external endpoint to post a comment; use the internal create_comment for that.
A run not in the caller's group returns TEST_RUN_NOT_FOUND.
Returns a bare JSON array of comment objects (same shape as list_comments items).

capabilities.name: list_unique_errors
capabilities.intent: List the Suite Health unique errors for a project — test failures clustered by error signature over a date window, each cluster with its occurrence count, impacted-test count and a sample of the error text — so a team can attack the few root errors behind many failing tests.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], sent as a repeated query param (dateRange=<from>&dateRange=<to>). Required — missing, or not exactly two values, is a 400. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only alternative.

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text match against the error signature / sample text.

query.name: status
query.description: Test-status filter values. Note the list is failed-only regardless.

query.name: sources
query.description: Product-source filter.

query.name: failureCategories
query.description: Failure-category ids to include.

query.name: uniqueBuildNames
query.description: Restrict to these unique build names.

query.name: users
query.description: Owner user ids (integers).

query.name: teams
query.description: Team ids (integers).

query.name: isMuted
query.description: Muted-tests visibility. Unmuted is the default; an unrecognised value is a 400 (IllegalArgumentException).

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the cluster-id constraint is dropped, so results span all builds of a test rather than one error cluster.

query.name: orderKey
query.description: Sort column. Ignored (forced to errorCount) for free / non-pro accounts.

query.name: pageNumber
query.description: Zero-based page index into the clustered result. Page size is fixed at 15. The response's pagingParams.pageNumber is the NEXT index to request (requested + 1), not the one you sent.

guidance: Take each row's `id` (a numeric string, the errorClusterId) — that is the cluster id every per-error detail view wants in its path.

Page with `pageNumber` (0-based) and a fixed size of 15. Walk pages while the response `pagingParams.hasNext` is true; note `pagingParams.pageNumber` is already the NEXT page to request, not the one you asked for.
An empty `errors` with a 200 is the honest answer for a demo tenant or a project with no builds — it does NOT mean the project is missing. A truly absent project is a 404.
Before concluding coverage is complete, check automateTestsSkipped / appAutomateTestsSkipped / lcncTestsSkipped — source fencing may have silently dropped whole product families from the clustering.
Free / non-pro accounts get exactly one error back (the top one) and the sort is forced to errorCount desc; do not read that single row as the only error that exists.
Heavy filter combinations run under an Elasticsearch time budget and can be cut short, so a smaller-than-expected result on an expensive query may be a budget cut rather than the true count.
Any unrecognised extra query params are collected into customParams rather than rejected, so a mis-typed filter name is silently ignored, not errored.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_summary
capabilities.intent: Get the header/summary block for one unique error — its test name, the sample error text (split into lines), and the OS/browser/device combinations it was seen on — to describe what the error actually is on the detail page.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: errorId
path_params.description: The error cluster id. Declared as a string but parsed with Long.parseLong: a non-numeric value throws a raw NumberFormatException and comes back as a 500, not a clean 400. Bound onto the query command object's clusterId.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the errorClusterId constraint is dropped and the summary aggregates across all failed runs of the test (by stability hash) rather than this one cluster.

query.name: browser
query.description: Optional single-value browser narrowing (pro accounts only).

query.name: os
query.description: Optional single-value OS narrowing (pro accounts only).

query.name: device
query.description: Optional single-value device narrowing (pro accounts only).

guidance: Pass the cluster id as a numeric `errorId`. A non-numeric id is NOT a 400 here — it is a raw 500 from Long.parseLong, because this handler does not validate or wrap exceptions the way its siblings do.

If no failing run matches the filters+window, the handler dereferences the first (absent) hit and 500s rather than returning an empty summary — treat a 500 here as possibly 'no sample found', and widen the window.
`error` is the sample text already split on newlines into an array of lines, not a single string.
`combinations` lists the platform combos the error appeared on ({os, browser} where browser also carries a `device`); combos that are NA on both os and browser are dropped from the list.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_occurrence_count
capabilities.intent: Get the total number of times one unique error occurred in the window, plus a per-day count series — the headline count and sparkline for the error detail panel.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: errorId
path_params.description: The error cluster id (parsed as a Long). Bound onto the query command object's clusterId.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the errorClusterId constraint is dropped and the count spans all failed runs of the test rather than this cluster.

guidance: `chartData` is a flat array of per-day occurrence counts with NO timestamps — reconstruct the x-axis yourself from the requested window (one bucket per calendar day, extended-bounds padded to the window).
`errorCount` is the total matching-run count for the window, independent of the bucket array length.
Buckets are fixed at one calendar day; the interval is not requestable.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_build_trend
capabilities.intent: Get the occurrence trend of one unique error across builds over time — matching runs (timestamp, status, duration) grouped by status series and enriched with build info — to plot when and in which builds the error appeared.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: errorId
path_params.description: The error cluster id (parsed as a Long). Bound onto the query command object's clusterId.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the errorClusterId constraint is dropped and the trend spans all failed runs of the test rather than this cluster.

guidance: Hard-capped at 5000 matching runs: for a very common error the trend is silently truncated to the first 5000 runs by start time, so totals here can understate the real count — use get_unique_error_occurrence_count for the true total.
Heavier than the other detail calls — it does a second relational lookup to enrich each run with build info — so expect higher latency.
`data` is a list of status series ({name, color, data[]}); `keys` is the parallel list of run start timestamps (epoch). A truly missing project is re-thrown as a 404; other failures surface as 500.

capabilities.name: list_unique_error_builds
capabilities.intent: List the builds in which one unique error occurred, cursor-paginated, so a user can jump from an error cluster to the actual runs and builds where it appeared.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: errorId
path_params.description: The error cluster id (parsed as a Long). Bound onto the query command object's clusterId.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Cursor: pass back the `pagingParams.searchAfter` array from the previous page verbatim. Follow this cursor rather than a page number; page size is fixed at 15.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the errorClusterId constraint is dropped so all failed runs of the test are listed, not just this cluster.

guidance: Cursor pagination only — there is no page number. Take `pagingParams.searchAfter` from the response and send it back as the `searchAfter` query array for the next page; page size is fixed at 15.
Stop when the response has no further rows: `pagingParams.hasNext` is set to false only on an empty page, so an empty `builds` (or hasNext=false) is the end of the list.
Each build carries isFailedWithSameError, saying whether that build's run failed with THIS exact cluster or merely contains the test; use it to distinguish same-error recurrences from unrelated runs.

Some fields are exposed only through computed getters, not raw columns: versionControlInfo ({url, commitId}), issueType ({isAutoAnalyzed, value}, null unless the run is failed) and historyAggregate ({isAlwaysFailing, isFlaky, isNewlyFailed}).

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_platform_breakdown
capabilities.intent: Break one unique error down by environment — which OS / browser / device combinations it occurred on and how often — so a team can tell whether the error is platform-specific.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: errorId
path_params.description: The error cluster id (parsed as a Long). Bound onto the query command object's clusterId.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: allBuilds
query.description: When true the errorClusterId constraint is dropped so the breakdown spans all failed runs of the test rather than this cluster.

guidance: Returns a FLAT array of platform buckets, not a nested os->browser->device tree; each entry is one {browser (with a `device`), os} combination.
Per entry, `totalFailure` is the occurrence doc count and `errorCount` is the distinct impacted-test count; `chartData` is per-day occurrence counts with no timestamps (reconstruct from the window).
Combos that are NA on both os and browser are dropped from the list.
The breakdown is a single composite aggregation page (up to 1000 combinations) and is not paginated, so a project with a very large platform matrix could be truncated.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_impacted_tests
capabilities.intent: Expand one unique-error cluster into the individual tests that hit it — each with the browsers/devices/platforms it failed on and an occurrence series — the timeline/detail view behind a row in the unique-errors list.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: Project name path variable, resolved within the caller's group.

path_params.name: clusterId
path_params.description: The error cluster id. It reaches the query only because Spring binds the URI variable onto the command object's `clusterId` setter — a query param of the same name would be overridden by this path value, so set it here.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

query.name: uniqueBuildNames
query.description: Restrict the breakdown to these unique build names (pro accounts only).

query.name: orderValue
query.description: Sorts the returned tests by occurrence count.

guidance: The response is a bare JSON array of impacted-test objects (no envelope). Each test's `id` is a stability hash (the test signature), not a numeric id; `testRunId` is one representative failing run.

Set the cluster id in the PATH — the {clusterId} path variable overrides any clusterId query param of the same name, because the handler never reads the path variable itself and relies on request binding.
The full Suite Health filter surface is accepted and narrows the matched runs, but pro-account filters (build names, flaky, etc.) are skipped for free / non-pro users.
It pages internally through all composite buckets under a loop deadline, so for a very large cluster the returned list can be truncated when the deadline is hit rather than erroring.
A genuinely absent project is re-thrown as a 404; other failures surface as a 500. `chartData` is per-day occurrence counts with no timestamps.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_timeline_charts
capabilities.intent: Get the Suite Health unique-errors timeline in one call — three day-bucketed time series over the window (unique errors, unique impacted tests, total impacted executions), each with its headline total — for the project's failed tests.

path_params.name: projectNormalisedName
path_params.description: Project normalised name, resolved within the caller's group. No permission check beyond project visibility.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Window as exactly two epoch-millisecond bounds [from, to], repeated query param. Required. lowerBound + upperBound singles are the only fallback.

guidance: Response is a map with exactly three keys: uniqueErrorChart, uniqueTestChart, impactedTestChart. Each is {data, insights}, where data is a single-entry map whose series key differs per chart (totalUniqueErrors / uniqueImpactedTests / totalImpactedTests).
Read the headline number from each chart's `insights.value` (a STRING, e.g. '42') with `insights.metric` as its label — not by summing the points.
Each series point carries x (bucket epoch), y (value, may be null), t and pointRange; the bucket interval is derived from the window, not requestable.

Only failed tests are counted; archived and usage-locked builds are excluded, and the failed-status field used depends on the group's new-build-listing flag, so totals can shift when that flag changes.

capabilities.name: get_unique_error_filters
capabilities.intent: Build the whole filter sidebar for a project's Unique Errors page in one call — the currently applied selections echoed back as display fields, the static dropdown option sets (failure categories, statuses, platforms, users, teams, sources, folders...), and the project's default hooks visibility.

guidance: `applied` echoes the caller's current selections resolved into display objects (each option is {id, value, label, count, pId}); `staticFilters` is the full set of selectable option lists for the page.

Options are fetched from Elasticsearch and TestHub concurrently and degrade to EMPTY dropdowns on timeout or rejection rather than failing the request — an empty option list does NOT mean there is no data.

This is the errors-page filter surface; do not confuse it with the general build/test sidebar filters. Use the sibling typeahead capabilities (branches / build names / build tags / host names / test tags) for search-as-you-type option lookups.

guidance: Uses the compact QueryRq body (query + dateRange + isManuallyOverridden + includeManualRuns) — NOT the full Unique Errors filter set. dateRange must be exactly two bounds; there is no lowerBound/upperBound fallback.
Returns a BOUNDED set under `data` (each {id, value, label, count, pId}), matched by wildcard on `query`; it is a typeahead, not the full branch list.

capabilities.name: search_unique_error_filter_test_tags

capabilities.name: trigger_bulk_test_rca

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: The build's UUID. All failed tests of this build (optionally narrowed by the filter body) are queued for AI RCA.

body.name: filters
body.description: Optional. Same test-listing filter shape (FilterParamsV2) the build's test list uses — narrows which failed tests are analysed. Omit to target the build's failures as a whole.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Test statuses to include (e.g. failed). Part of the shared build test-listing filter.

body.name: limit
body.description: Optional cap on how many failed runs are queued in this request.

capabilities.intent: Kick off AI root-cause analysis for all failed tests of a build in one go (the 'Analyse all failures' action) — optionally narrowed by the test-listing filters and capped by a limit.
guidance: Asynchronous: this only queues work. The reply's bulkRcaUuid is the handle for the batch and each run's finished RCA arrives later — poll the individual test runs' RCA (get_test_rca_data) rather than expecting analyses in this response.

Plan-fenced: a free group that is not test-level-trial eligible is refused with 403 (PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED). It also requires the group's AI opt-in consent and the test-runs-RCA feature on the AI token; a source-fenced build is refused with AI_FEATURE_FENCED.
Needs the caller's own BrowserStack username + Selenium access key, resolved server-side from the caller's user record; a caller whose record lacks them gets 400 'User details are not available'.
Disabled entirely in the demo-sandbox environment.
The body is optional — POST with no body queues the build's failures with no extra filtering.

capabilities.name: get_test_rca

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Integer test-run id (the numeric uuid of the run, not its TR-NNN identifier).

capabilities.intent: Fetch the AI root-cause analysis for a failed test run — the Test Details AI panel's main call; if none exists yet it creates the record and queues a generation so the answer streams in later.
guidance: This is get-or-create despite being a GET: on a run with no RCA it PERSISTS a record and QUEUES an AI generation, so it is not a safe/idempotent read. When you only want to read an existing analysis without triggering anything, use get_test_rca_data.

The reply carries a state, not necessarily a finished analysis: a freshly queued run comes back Pending / FETCHING_LOGS / GENERATING_RCA, and rcaData is only populated once state reaches Completed. Terminal error states are LLM_SERVICE_ERROR / LOG_FETCH_ERROR / AI_SYSTEM_ERROR / UNKNOWN_ERROR / TIMEOUT.

Requires AI opt-in consent and the test-runs-RCA feature on the AI token; a source-fenced build gives AI_FEATURE_FENCED. Resolves the caller's BrowserStack username + Selenium access key server-side and 400s ('User details are not available') if they are missing.
LTS-product callers are forced onto the non-agentic path (isAgentic false), regardless of group settings.
This is the internal-cookie/session route; the same operation for public-API (username+access-key) callers is get_test_rca_via_public_api.

capabilities.name: get_test_rca_data

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Integer test-run id.

capabilities.intent: Read an already-generated AI RCA for a test run with NO side effects — the safe counterpart to get_test_rca that never creates a record or queues a generation.
guidance: Pure read: no AI consent/feature checks and no generation queued. Use this to poll for a result after triggering one elsewhere.

When nothing has been generated yet this is a 400 (BAD_REQUEST, 'Test Run RCA not found for the given test run ID'), NOT a 404 or an empty 200 — treat that 400 as 'not generated yet', not as a bad request.
Group-scoped: the run is looked up within the caller's group, so a foreign run id also surfaces as not-found.

capabilities.name: save_test_rca

path_params.name: testRunId
path_params.description: Integer test-run id the RCA payload belongs to.

body.name: success
body.description: Whether the generation succeeded. A success payload MUST also carry `data` or the call 500s (AI_SERVICE_ERROR) and the AI worker retries; a failure payload legitimately omits `data`.

body.name: data
body.description: The generated analysis payload (RCA data, thinking data, resulting state). Required when success is true. Overwrites the run's existing RCA.

body.name: error
body.description: Error detail for a failed generation.

body.name: origin
body.description: When set to 'tfa_chat' the payload is treated as a chat turn and a conversation event is published instead of a plain RCA overwrite.

capabilities.intent: Ingestion callback used by the AI service to write back a finished (or failed) root-cause analysis for a test run — this is what makes the analysis appear in the UI.
guidance: This is effectively a webhook/callback from the AI service, not a user-facing write. It OVERWRITES the test run's existing RCA — there is no prior version to restore.
Returns a plain string body ('Test Run RCA Saved Successfully'), NOT JSON — do not try to parse the 200 as an object.
The body is arbitrary JSON (unknown keys are ignored). The only hard rule: success=true without a `data` object is a 500, which the worker interprets as retryable.
No extra role check beyond the standard auth chain — any authenticated caller for the group can write an RCA payload for a run, so this is not the read path; use get_test_rca_data to read.

capabilities.name: get_test_rca_via_public_api

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Integer test-run id.

query.name: peek
query.description: peek=true makes the call strictly read-only: it returns the current RCA state and never enqueues a generation. With the default peek=false the GET is get-or-create and CAN queue work — treat that form as a trigger, not a read.

capabilities.intent: Public-API fetch of a failed test run's AI root-cause analysis; by default get-or-create (queues a generation and returns the pending state if none exists), or a strict read with peek=true.
guidance: This is the public-API twin of get_test_rca and accepts username + access-key auth. Behaviour splits on peek: peek=true is safe (never enqueues); peek=false (the default) is get-or-create and has a side effect.

To poll without triggering, always pass peek=true. The peek-only fields isLive / pendingMessageId / alreadyTracked describe an in-flight generation; gate a re-trigger on isLive (alreadyTracked only reflects whether a chat row holds a handle and is null for web/MCP-started runs).
Requires AI opt-in consent and AI enablement; source-fenced groups get AI_FEATURE_FENCED. Resolves the caller's BrowserStack username/access key server-side and 400s if missing.
To register an https callback instead of polling, use the POST twin trigger_test_rca_via_public_api.

capabilities.name: trigger_test_rca_via_public_api

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Integer test-run id.

body.name: webhook_url
body.description: Optional https callback URL the pipeline POSTs the finished RCA to when a generation is actually queued. https only; localhost/.internal/.local/loopback/private/link-local/multicast hosts are rejected (SSRF-guarded at accept time and re-checked at dispatch). Absent/blank means no callback.

capabilities.intent: Public-API trigger for a test run's AI RCA with a fire-and-forget callback: same get-or-queue behaviour as the GET, plus an https webhook the pipeline notifies when the analysis is ready.
guidance: With no body this behaves exactly like get_test_rca_via_public_api with peek=false (get-or-queue). The only added capability is registering webhook_url.
The callback fires ONLY when a generation is actually queued — if the RCA already exists (or is already in flight) no callback is sent, so still read the 200 body's state.
webhook_url must be https and pass the SSRF host checks both at accept time and again at dispatch; a URL that resolves to a blocked host is rejected with a 400 naming the reason.
The field is named webhook_url on the wire (snake_case), not webhookUrl.

capabilities.name: list_build_groups

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id (NOT the observability project id) used by the build-group backend.

query.name: page
query.description: 1-based page number.

query.name: pageSize
query.description: Rows per page (passed through to TestHub; server default 30).

query.name: name
query.description: Substring name search over run groups.

query.name: ids
query.description: Comma-separated build-group ids to fetch a specific set instead of the full listing.

capabilities.intent: List a project's run groups (build groups) with paging and name search — the source of run-group ids for linking, closing, editing or deleting; can also fetch a specific set by ids.
guidance: The groups are at the top-level `data` array (there is no `success` wrapper on this route); paging is under `info` (page, pageSize, count, prev, next).
By default closed groups are excluded from this listing (the controller requests excludeClosed=true).
projectId in the path is the TestHub project id, not the observability project id — using the wrong one returns an empty/foreign result.
Each row's `state` is derived: ACTIVE until closed, then CLOSED. Take the integer `id` for the link/close/edit/delete calls.

capabilities.name: create_build_group

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id.

body.name: name
body.description: Run-group name. Required and must not be blank; the reserved name 'Ungrouped' (any case) is rejected with 400 'Please enter a valid group name'.

body.name: description
body.description: Optional description.

capabilities.intent: Create a new run group (build group) in a project so builds can be grouped for a release or test cycle.
guidance: Requires the project's BUILD_ADD_TO_RUN_GROUP permission.
The created group is at `data` (a build-group object with its integer `id`); `success` is true and `message` is 'Build group created successfully'.
Creation actually happens in TestHub and is mirrored back — the returned id is the TestHub group id used by the other build-group calls.
'Ungrouped' is reserved and rejected even though it is otherwise a valid name.

capabilities.name: update_build_group

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id.

path_params.name: buildGroupId
path_params.description: Integer build-group id to edit.

body.name: name
body.description: New name. Although the DTO marks it optional, the service REQUIRES a non-null name on every update: omit it and the call is 400 'Please enter a valid group name'. To edit only the description, resend the group's current name. 'Ungrouped' is rejected.

body.name: description
body.description: New description.

capabilities.intent: Rename a run group or edit its description.
guidance: Requires the project's BUILD_ADD_TO_RUN_GROUP permission.
Name is effectively mandatory even for a description-only edit: the handler rejects a null/blank name with 400 before touching TestHub, so read the group first and echo its current name back.
Pass-through to TestHub; the refreshed group comes back at `data`.
