Reversible edit (mode write) — but the group keeps no revision history, so an overwritten name/description is not restorable.

capabilities.name: delete_build_group

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id.

path_params.name: buildGroupId
path_params.description: Integer build-group id to delete.

capabilities.intent: Delete a run group from a project — the group and its build associations are removed (the underlying builds are kept).
guidance: Requires the project's BUILD_ADD_TO_RUN_GROUP permission. The delete happens in TestHub and is NOT undoable from this API.
Only the group is removed; the builds themselves survive. A delete event is published so the builds are detached asynchronously — they may briefly still reference the group.
Success is a thin body: `{success:true, message:'Build group deleted successfully'}` (no group data).

capabilities.name: close_build_group

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id.

path_params.name: buildGroupId
path_params.description: Integer build-group id to close.

capabilities.intent: Close a run group and everything in it — closes the group in TestHub, snapshots and freezes its test runs, flips its builds to 'closed', and reports how many builds were closed.
guidance: Requires the project's BUILD_ADD_TO_RUN_GROUP permission.
Closing FREEZES the runs (they become non-editable / locked) but deletes no data — it is a reversible-in-principle state, hence write, not destructive.

Multi-system fan-out (TestHub, a TestStack bulk snapshot, an Elasticsearch bulk build update, Redis locks, a Kafka event) that is only partially transactional and can be slow for large groups; a partial failure can leave systems briefly inconsistent.
`closed_builds` is how many builds were flipped to closed; `build_group_id` echoes the group.

capabilities.name: apply_build_bulk_action

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: TestHub project id (used as the ES thProjectId and the TestHub SDK project).

body.name: action
body.description: Which bulk operation to run. Send the WIRE value, not the constant name: 'BulkAssignTestPlan', 'BulkAssignAssignee' or 'LinkToBuildGroup'. Any other value is rejected 400 ('Unknown action type'). (The other enum members exist only for internal Kafka events and are not accepted here.)

body.name: buildIds
body.description: Explicit integer build ids to act on. Provide this OR selectedBuildGroupIds (unless selectAll=true). Ignored when selectAll=true.

fields.description: A build id.

body.name: selectedBuildGroupIds
body.description: Explicit run-group ids whose builds are acted on. Provide this OR buildIds (unless selectAll=true). Ignored when selectAll=true.

fields.description: A build-group id.

body.name: selectAll
body.description: Select-all-matching mode. When true, `filter` is REQUIRED and the explicit buildIds/selectedBuildGroupIds are ignored; the target set is the filter minus the excluded* lists.

body.name: filter
body.description: Build filter (GetBuildFilterRqV2), required only when selectAll=true — the same filter shape the build list uses. Resolves the set of builds to act on.

body.name: excludedBuildUuids
body.description: Build UUIDs to subtract from a selectAll set (applied as must_not).

fields.description: A build UUID to exclude.

body.name: excludedBuildGroupIds
body.description: Run-group ids to subtract from a selectAll set (must_not on buildGroupId), for grouped-view select-all with deselections.

fields.description: A build-group id to exclude.

body.name: testPlanId
body.description: Required for action 'BulkAssignTestPlan': the test plan to assign the matched builds to.

body.name: assignee
body.description: Required for action 'BulkAssignAssignee': the user id to set as owner/assignee on the matched builds.

body.name: linkToBuildGroupId
body.description: Required for action 'LinkToBuildGroup': the run-group the matched builds are linked into.

capabilities.intent: Apply one bulk operation across many builds at once — assign a test plan, assign an owner/assignee, or link builds to a run group — by explicit ids/group ids, or select-all-by-filter with exclusions.
guidance: Two execution modes by matched-build count: under 30 it runs synchronously and returns `{success:true, async:false, totalUpdated:<n>, requestId:null}`; at or above 30 it publishes a Kafka event and returns `{success:true, async:true, totalUpdated:0, requestId:<id>}` — the async body is an acknowledgement, so re-read the builds to confirm.

One bulk action per project at a time: it takes a 10-minute Redis lock, and a concurrent request is refused with HTTP 400 'Bulk action is currently locked for this project.' — retry, do not treat as bad input.

Permissions are per action (no blanket controller gate): 'BulkAssignTestPlan' and 'BulkAssignAssignee' need TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_EDIT; 'LinkToBuildGroup' needs BUILD_ADD_TO_RUN_GROUP. The check runs before validation, so an unauthorized caller gets a 403 with no validation feedback.

Selection rules: with selectAll=true you MUST send `filter` (else 400) and buildIds/selectedBuildGroupIds are ignored; without it you must send buildIds OR selectedBuildGroupIds. The action-specific id (testPlanId / assignee / linkToBuildGroupId) is also required for its action.
A sync run that resolves to zero builds returns `{success:true, async:false, totalUpdated:0}` — not an error.
Linking moves builds: a build belongs to at most one group. Updates are reversible, so this is write, not destructive.

capabilities.name: get_a11y_plan_details
capabilities.intent: Report what the caller's group is entitled to for Accessibility Testing — a11y plan type, free-tier flag, whether a free trial is still claimable — merged with the reverse-free-trial (RFT) details from the Accessibility service. Drives the a11y upsell/trial banners.
guidance: No parameters — group and user come from the session.

The body is a FLAT, mixed object: the RFT details fetched from the Accessibility service (snake_case upstream, converted to camelCase) with the local plan fields merged on top. The exact key set is not fixed here; treat it as an entitlement blob and read the fields you need defensively.
On an upstream JSON parse failure it returns a plain text 500 body ('Error fetching a11y plan details'), NOT the usual structured error envelope.

capabilities.name: list_build_accessibility_test_runs

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: Build UUID.

query.name: status
query.description: Filter by test status.

query.name: searchQuery
query.description: Substring search over test name.

query.name: run
query.description: Restrict to specific run ids.

fields.description: A run id.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number (see guidance on 0/1 indexing).

query.name: limit
query.description: Rows per page.

capabilities.intent: List the accessibility-scanned tests of one build for the build's Accessibility tab — per test: name, file, status, OS/browser, a11y score, page/component counts and a critical/serious/moderate/minor issue breakdown, with paging.
guidance: The build must have FINISHED (or TIMEOUT) and carry accessibility data, else a typed 4xx: A11Y_BUILD_NOT_FOUND (no build/no a11y), A11Y_BUILD_STATUS_INVALID (no status), or A11Y_BUILD_NOT_COMPLETED (still running).

Feature-flag fork: when the App-Accessibility flag is on for the group AND the build's source is the App-Accessibility automation source, the whole call is proxied to a separate Accessibility service and the RESPONSE SHAPE IS THAT SERVICE'S, not the one described here. Do not assume this shape for App-Accessibility builds.
Tests with no a11y summary/severity breakdown are SILENTLY DROPPED from the list, so the row count can be lower than the build's total tests.
Paging is re-based to 0-index for the frontend: pagingParams.nextRoot.page is (upstream next page - 1), and pagingParams.hasNext says whether to continue.
Accepts a public-link token in addition to the normal auth types (public dashboards).

capabilities.name: get_test_run_accessibility_meta

path_params.name: btcerId
path_params.description: TestHub build-test-case-execution-result (btcer) id — a plain integer, NOT a test-run TR-NNN identifier.

query.name: page
query.description: Page number. Page size is fixed server-side at 10 and cannot be changed by the caller.

capabilities.intent: Accessibility detail for a single test on the Test Details page — that test's a11y score, total issues and severity breakdown, and its report URL.
guidance: Error mapping is LOSSY: every failure except A11Y_SERVICE_USER_UNAUTHORIZED and A11Y_SERVICE_NOT_CONFIGURED is rewritten to A11Y_TESTCASE_RESULTS_NOT_FOUND — so a genuine upstream error surfaces as 'no results'. Do not read 'not found' as definitely empty.

App-Accessibility feature-flag fork again: when the flag is on and the run's source is the App-Accessibility automation source, the call is proxied to a separate Accessibility service and returns that service's shape, not the one described here.
Page size is fixed at 10 server-side; only `page` is caller-controllable.
reportURL points to the a11y report to fetch elsewhere; the response itself does not embed the full report.

capabilities.name: start_accessibility_free_trial
capabilities.intent: Claim/start the Accessibility free trial for the signed-in user from inside TRA, so the user need not leave for the Accessibility product.
guidance: Despite the read-ish shape, this MUTATES entitlement state upstream — it starts the trial. No request body is read: the upstream call is built from the session user id plus cad_a11y_integration=true.

Thin pass-through to the Accessibility service's own POST /api/v1/group/free-trial: on upstream failure the upstream status code and raw body are relayed as-is, so the body shape is the Accessibility service's, not TRA's.
No explicit undo through this API; treat re-claiming as idempotent-at-best and check the trial status afterward with get_accessibility_free_trial_status.

capabilities.name: get_accessibility_free_trial_status
capabilities.intent: Report whether the user's Accessibility free trial is active/claimed/expired, so TRA can render the right trial banner.
guidance: No parameters — user id is taken from the session and cad_a11y_integration=true is added.
Pure pass-through to the Accessibility service's GET /api/v1/group/free-trial-status; the body shape is that service's.
Returns a plain text 500 body if the upstream JSON cannot be parsed, rather than the usual error envelope.

capabilities.name: update_code_fix_preference

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Observability project id. Must belong to the caller's group (IDOR-checked) and must match the group+project the preference row was created under.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Integer id of the code-fix preference row to edit. The row is located by this id alone; buildName in the body does not select it.

body.name: buildName
body.description: Required and must be non-blank (validation), but its value is IGNORED on update — the row is located by the path id and buildName is never re-written. Send any non-blank string (echo the preference's existing build name).

body.name: instruction
body.description: Free-text code-fix guidance. Omit (null) to leave the stored instruction unchanged. There is no way to send null to clear it; to end up with no instruction you must keep at least one file attached, else the call is 400.

body.name: fileAttachments
body.description: TRI-STATE. Omit (null) = leave existing attachments untouched. Send [] = remove ALL existing attachments. Send a non-empty array = REPLACE them. On replace or remove the previously attached S3 objects are permanently deleted (no undo, no version history). At most ONE attachment (MAX_PREFERENCE_FILES=1).

fields.name: s3Key
fields.description: S3 key of the already-uploaded file from a prior code-fix-preference presign+upload. Confirmed against this group/project; an s3Key that is not confirmable is rejected.

capabilities.intent: Edit an existing AI code-fix preference for a project/build — change the instruction text and/or replace (or remove) its attached context file.
guidance: fileAttachments is tri-state: null (omit) leaves attachments untouched, [] removes all of them, a non-empty array replaces them. Replacing or removing permanently deletes the old S3 objects — there is no undo and preferences keep no version history, so an overwritten instruction or removed file is gone for good.

The final state must still carry either an instruction or at least one file: a request that would leave the row empty is rejected 400 'At least one of instruction or fileAttachments is required' before any S3 work runs.

buildName is required by validation on every update but its value is silently ignored — the update targets the row named by the path id and never rewrites buildName. Do not use this call to rename the build a preference is bound to.
instruction omitted (null) means 'unchanged'; only a non-null instruction overwrites it. Max 5000 characters.
Only one attachment is allowed (max 1). Each must reference an s3Key produced by the code-fix-preference presign+upload flow; a key not confirmable for this group/project fails the request.
The path id must belong to the SAME group and project as the path projectId, else 400 'Preference does not belong to this project' (not 404). A missing id is 404 code-fix-preferences-not-found.
Plan-gated: 403 plan-feature-not-allowed when the AI-TFA fence trips, and per-user AI must be enabled for the caller.

200.description: Updated code-fix preference. fileAttachments[].downloadUrl is a freshly presigned GET URL, omitted when its generation failed.

downloadUrl.description: Presigned GET URL for the attachment. Present only when it could be generated (NON_NULL).

capabilities.name: get_ai_orchestration_capabilities
capabilities.intent: Check which external AI flows this group may use — whether AI RCA v2 and project-repo settings are enabled — so an agent knows which AI capabilities to offer the customer.
guidance: POST but purely read-only: it takes no path, query or body — send an empty POST. It never changes state.
Returns two booleans with snake_case keys: is_ai_rca_v2_enabled and is_project_repo_settings_enabled, derived from the caller's group flags.
External API: authenticate with the customer's BrowserStack username + access key.

200.description: Capability probe result.

capabilities.name: retrigger_rca_analysis_via_public_api

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Integer test-run id. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group via its build.

body.name: instruction
body.description: Extra user instruction to steer the improved RCA. Optional.

body.name: attachments
body.description: Up to 3 context files, each already uploaded via the RCA-context presign flow.

body.name: usePreferences
body.description: Whether to fold the project's stored code-fix preferences into the retrigger.

body.name: webhook_url
body.description: Optional https callback the pipeline POSTs the finished RCA to. SSRF-validated at accept time and again at dispatch: https only, and NOT localhost/private/link-local/.internal/.local hosts — a violation is 400. Absent/blank means no callback.

capabilities.intent: Re-run ('improve') a test's RCA with an extra instruction and optional attachments, on behalf of an agent acting for the customer — returns the new conversation message id to poll.
guidance: Precondition-heavy: requires an existing RCA row for the test run, AI opt-in consent, and RCA-v2 eligibility, and the test run must not exceed the age limit — otherwise it is refused before any generation.
Refused with FORBIDDEN_OPERATION when the run is already owned by the MCP-driven agent flow.
webhook_url must be https and must not target localhost/private/link-local/.internal/.local hosts; it is validated when accepted and re-validated at dispatch, so a bad URL is a 400 up front.
instruction is capped at 5000 chars and at most 3 attachments are accepted; each attachment needs an s3Key from a prior RCA-context presign+upload.

Asynchronous: the body carries only messageId (a UUID) — poll the RCA conversation/turn-status read for the outcome; the RCA itself is delivered elsewhere (the polled read, or the webhook when supplied). trialQuota.used appears only for trial tenants.
This is the external mirror of the session-auth internal retrigger; authenticate with the customer's BrowserStack username + access key.

200.description: Retrigger accepted; poll the returned messageId.

messageId.description: UUID of the new conversation turn to poll.

capabilities.name: trigger_release_readiness

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

query.name: force
query.description: Explicit re-run. Bypasses ONLY the cached-report fast path; in-flight dedup (a 300s lock) and the repo gate still apply. A non-boolean value 400s at the Spring boundary.

capabilities.intent: Start (or re-run) Release Readiness analysis for a build — gathers its GitHub context and publishes a generate-report event, returning immediately with the current state; a fresh COMPLETED report is returned inline instead of re-running.
guidance: Asynchronous: a normal trigger returns {state:IN_PROGRESS, buildUuid, triggeredAt} and NO report — poll the summary/prs/workflows reads (completion is also pushed via Pusher). A cache-hit returns {state:COMPLETED, buildUuid, summary:{...}} inline.

force=true bypasses only the cached-report fast path. In-flight dedup still fires: a forced call while a generation is actively IN_PROGRESS does not start a second run — it returns IN_PROGRESS. A FAILED prior state, by contrast, regenerates immediately.
Returns error REPO_NOT_CONFIGURED when the project has no GitHub repo wired up — THIS internal route enforces the repo gate (the external mirror deliberately does not).
Plan+flag gated: 403 plan-feature-not-allowed unless the group passes the AI-TFA fence AND the release_readiness flag is on.
Writes but starts no destructible record — it enqueues analysis; re-running is the recovery path.

capabilities.name: trigger_release_readiness_via_public_api

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

query.name: force
query.description: Explicit re-run. Bypasses ONLY the cached-report fast path; in-flight dedup still applies. A non-boolean value 400s at the Spring boundary.

capabilities.intent: External/agent entry point to request a build's Release Readiness report — returns a cached COMPLETED report inline, otherwise marks it IN_PROGRESS, publishes generation, and returns immediately with that state.
guidance: Same async contract as the internal trigger: cache-hit returns {state:COMPLETED, buildUuid, summary}; otherwise {state:IN_PROGRESS, buildUuid, triggeredAt}. Poll the read lenses for the finished report.

Unlike the internal trigger, this route runs with the repo gate DISABLED (enforceRepoGate=false): a caller WITHOUT a connected repo is not rejected with REPO_NOT_CONFIGURED — generation proceeds on whatever GitHub context exists, possibly empty.
force=true bypasses only the cache fast-path; a forced call during an active IN_PROGRESS run still dedups and returns IN_PROGRESS.
Plan+flag gated (AI-TFA fence + release_readiness), else FORBIDDEN_OPERATION. Authenticate with the customer's BrowserStack username + access key.

capabilities.name: get_release_readiness_connect_state

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

capabilities.intent: Check whether a build's project is wired up for Release Readiness — whether a GitHub repo is connected (and how many) and whether a PR-list input file exists for this build — to drive the 'connect your repo' vs 'start analysis' CTA.
guidance: Pure read; never triggers analysis. github.configured / github.repoCount reflect the connected repos.

prList.present is an S3 object-existence check on the build's github-context file: a present-but-empty file still reads true, and any S3 error (or no configured repo) degrades to false rather than erroring the panel.

buildLevelRca.state is deliberately ALWAYS 'UNKNOWN' on this route — it is not read from S3, to stay within the latency budget. Read the authoritative workflowsState from the summary/prs/workflows reads instead.
observabilityLogs.comingSoon is always true (a placeholder source). There is no failed-test count here — the client uses the build summary's own failed count.
Plan+flag gated (AI-TFA fence + release_readiness), 403 otherwise.

capabilities.name: get_release_readiness_prs

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

capabilities.intent: Read the PRs lens of a build's Release Readiness report — the pull requests implicated in the build's failures, plus the report-level summary (verdict, counts). Pure read of the generated report.
guidance: Pure read; never triggers generation.
The summary fields are FLATTENED to the TOP LEVEL (state, verdict, totalPrs, faultyPrNumbers, workflowsState, ...), NOT nested under a 'summary' key; the PR inventory is the top-level 'prs' array.

If no COMPLETED report exists you still get 200 with prs:[] and a status-only summary carrying state = IN_PROGRESS / FAILED (+failureReason) / NOT_STARTED. An empty 'prs' therefore means 'not ready', not 'no PRs' — branch on state, not on prs being empty.

verdict is 'go' only for a COMPLETED report with no suspect PRs, 'partial-go' whenever any suspect PR exists (every PR in 'prs' is a revert candidate), and absent otherwise. faultyPrNumbers is the revert list.
Each PR carries a confidence band ('high' | 'medium' | 'low'), defaulting to 'medium' when the agent did not grade it.

capabilities.name: get_release_readiness_workflows

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

capabilities.intent: Read the workflows lens of a build's Release Readiness report — the CI workflows/jobs implicated in the build's failures, plus the report-level summary. Pure read of the generated report.
guidance: Pure read; never triggers generation.
The summary fields are FLATTENED to the TOP LEVEL; the workflow inventory is the top-level 'workflows' array.

If no COMPLETED report exists you still get 200 with workflows:[] and a status-only summary (state = IN_PROGRESS / FAILED+failureReason / NOT_STARTED). An empty 'workflows' means 'not ready', not 'no workflows' — branch on state.
Plan+flag gated (AI-TFA fence + release_readiness), 403 otherwise.

capabilities.name: get_release_readiness_summary

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build UUID. IDOR-scoped to the caller's group (404 BUILD_NOT_FOUND otherwise).

capabilities.intent: Read the compact Release Readiness summary for a build's Insights tab — the headline verdict/state and counts — without needing the separate PR or workflow lenses. Pure read.
guidance: Pure read; never triggers generation.

On a COMPLETED report the summary also carries the inline prs[] and workflows[] detail (the whole report renders from this one fetch). On a non-completed build you get a status-only summary: state = IN_PROGRESS / FAILED (+failureReason) / NOT_STARTED.
state NOT_STARTED is returned as 200, not 404 — it means 'no analysis yet' (show the Generate CTA), distinct from FAILED.

verdictProvisional is true while workflowsState = PENDING (build-level RCA not finished); the verdict may still change once workflows fill in. Legacy reports without workflowsState resolve to AVAILABLE.
Plan+flag gated (AI-TFA fence + release_readiness), 403 otherwise.

capabilities.name: list_split_build_legs

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The PARENT build's 40-char uuid. The child legs are resolved as builds whose parentId is this build's id.

query.name: pageLimit
query.description: Page size (child legs per page). Defaults to 10 when omitted. Bound from the query string despite the DTO marking it @JsonIgnore (that only affects JSON body binding, not query binding).

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Cursor for the NEXT page: the build UUID of the last leg you received, NOT an offset or page number. Must be a 40-char alphanumeric build uuid or the request is rejected. Echoed back to you in pagingParams.searchAfter.

capabilities.intent: List the individual legs (child builds) of a split / parallel build with their ids and uuids, so you can offer a leg switcher or aggregate stats across the whole split run.
guidance: Pagination is CURSOR-based, keyed by build uuid: read `pagingParams.searchAfter` (the last leg's uuid) from the response and pass it as the next call's `searchAfter`. There is no offset/page-number paging here.
Walk pages while `pagingParams.hasNext` is true; hasNext is set from whether the page came back full (>= pageLimit), so a final short page ends the walk.
An unknown parent uuid is ObservabilityException(BUILD_NOT_FOUND), not a 200 with an empty list.
Each leg in `builds` is a full build-summary object (same shape as get_build_details), so you get every leg's status and counts without a per-leg call.
`builds` are the CHILD legs only; the parent build itself is addressed by get_build_details.

capabilities.name: get_build_notification_summary

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The NUMERIC build id (not the 40-char uuid). This route takes the integer id; passing a uuid will not resolve.

capabilities.intent: Get the compact build summary used to render the build-summary email / notification card — name, project, run-by, status/issue-type/history aggregates, muted and total counts, build alerts and quality-gate status.
guidance: Takes the INTEGER build id, unlike almost every other build endpoint (which take the uuid). Get the integer id from a build read or listing first.
An unknown id returns HTTP 200 with a NULL body, not a 404 — treat an empty/null response as 'build not found', not as an empty summary.
This is NOT group-scoped in the lookup: it resolves the build by id alone. Do not rely on it to enforce workspace ownership.

This is a different payload from get_build_details / get_build_summary_stats — it is the trimmed 'email card' shape (BuildSummaryEmail) with formatted duration/date helpers, not the full detail object.
`accessibility` is present only for APP_ALLY_AUT builds (populated fail-open) and omitted entirely otherwise; do not treat its absence as a11y failure.
`startedAt` is not serialised as a raw timestamp — the payload exposes formatted date/time/duration helper fields instead.

capabilities.name: get_build_stability_tile

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Any extra query params not bound to the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded to the query. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the stability tile for a build — the share of tests that ran cleanly versus flaky / always-failing / new-failure noise, with a percentile insight versus recent builds — for the build insights page.
guidance: Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403 (FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / plan feature not allowed) — the stability tile is a gated feature.
An unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND, not an empty tile.
This is the stability TILE (single build, based on the last ~30 runs, `overview.meta` says how many) — not the historical stability chart (that is get_build_stability_chart).
This route accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set as query params plus arbitrary customParams; filters narrow which of the build's tests feed the stability number.
`overview.count` is a percentage string (e.g. "92.3") and `overview.insights` is a positive/negative/default verdict versus recent builds — it is only populated once there are >= 10 comparison runs.

capabilities.name: get_build_summary_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the headline test-count strip for a build under the currently applied filters — total / passed / failed / skipped / pending roll-ups plus AI-RCA and session counts — the summary strip at the top of the build insights page.
guidance: Name-collision trap: this is `/{uuid}/buildSummary` (headline counters, action getBuildStats). It is NOT `/{uuid}` build metadata (get_build_details) and NOT `/{uuid}/getBuildStats` (get_build_non_sdk_test_counts). The similar names back completely different payloads.
Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.
`data` is an array of colored metric tiles (each `{id, name, value, color, testsCount, hooksCount, ...}`), not a flat counts object — read each tile's `value`.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams; the counters reflect the applied filters, so an unfiltered total needs an unfiltered call.

capabilities.name: get_build_timeline_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

capabilities.intent: Get the build's execution timeline — per-status series (passed / failed / running) bucketed over the build's lifetime — for the timeline visualisation on the build page.
guidance: No filters apply on this route — it takes only the uuid; any query params are ignored.
Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.
The payload is a single top-level `data` array of chart series (one per status), each carrying `[time, value]` point pairs suitable for a column chart — not a list of discrete lifecycle events.

capabilities.name: get_build_details

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: run
query.description: Optional attempt / run number to scope the summary to a specific re-run attempt. Omit for the latest.

capabilities.intent: Get the main build-detail payload for one build — status, run counts, framework/CI metadata, cross-product and test-plan info — plus the per-build UI gates (whether to show the Self-Healing tab, the Authoring Agent tab, and whether App Accessibility is enabled).
guidance: An unknown uuid throws ObservabilityException(BUILD_NOT_FOUND) (a 404-equivalent), not a 200 with an empty body.

`showAuthoringReport` and `showHealingReport` are UI gates derived from an S3 key-existence check on the build metadata — they say whether the report EXISTS to show, not whether you may access it. On demo-sandbox environments `showAuthoringReport` is forced true regardless.
`appAccessibilityEnabled` is a per-group feature flag and fails CLOSED (false) if the flag lookup errors — do not read false as 'definitely no a11y data'.
`duration` is the consolidated duration when present, otherwise the raw duration — the field already resolves this, so use it directly.
`displayStatus` is the settled pipeline verdict and is preferred over `status` for the final outcome; `status` can still reflect a live aggregation mid-run.
Use the `run` query param to inspect a specific re-run attempt; omitting it returns the latest attempt's summary.

capabilities.name: get_build_failure_category_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the failure-category (defect) breakdown for a build — how many failures fall into each issue type/category, how many have AI RCA available, and the comment count — for the 'Failure Categories' panel.
guidance: While the build is still PENDING (or has no status yet) this returns HTTP 200 with an EMPTY `data` array, zeroed `aiRcaStats`/`commentCount`, and `message` = 'Failure Categories will be available after your build finishes'. That is a valid 200, not an error — check `message`/`data` before concluding there are no defects.
Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.
Each `data` entry is a category with a `value` count and optional nested `categories` sub-buckets; `aiRcaStats.completedCount` is how many of these failures already have AI RCA.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams; the breakdown reflects the applied filters.

capabilities.name: get_build_failures_by_module

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get a build's failures grouped by test module / file path, so you can see which modules or suites contribute most of the failures.
guidance: Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

Each `data` entry is a module node with a `value` (total) and `failedTests` count, plus `parent`/`customPathSplit` so you can rebuild the folder/module tree — the path separator is inferred per node (`/` or `\`).

`sourceFencingFlags` is present only when the group's source-fencing feature excludes the build's product; when present it names which products' tests were skipped from the aggregation, so counts may be partial.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams.

capabilities.name: get_build_filter_values

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: The build UUID (despite the `buildId` name, this is the 40-char uuid, resolved via getBuildbyUuId).

capabilities.intent: Get the distinct filter values available for one build's test listing (browsers, OSes, tags, issue types, statuses, plus static history/flaky options) so the UI can render the filter dropdowns.
guidance: This is the OLDER filter shape. The richer replacement is get_build_test_filters (route `/{buildUuid}/filters`), which additionally returns the currently-applied filters, hooks visibility, split-build children and freemium pro-gating. Prefer that one unless you specifically need this compact shape.
Not group-scoped in the lookup (resolves the build by uuid alone).

The payload is a single `filters` map keyed by facet name (browser, os, issueType, tags, status, folder, history, flaky), each a list of `{label, value}` options; `history` and `flaky` are static option lists always present.
Values are computed from the build's LATEST test runs, so a facet a filter narrowed away will not appear as an option here.

capabilities.name: get_build_flaky_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the flaky-tests tile for a build — how many of the build's tests were detected as flaky (with a 'out of total' meta) plus the tile's comment count.
guidance: Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

Same response shape (SingleMetricSummary: count/meta/commentCount/autoUnmuteCount) as get_build_muted_stats and get_build_new_failure_stats — only the metric differs. `count` is the flaky count; `meta` carries the 'out of N' context string.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams.

capabilities.name: list_build_test_folders

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: The build UUID (despite the `buildId` name it is the 40-char uuid). WARNING: there is no not-found guard — an unknown uuid NPEs into a 500, not a 404.

query.name: folder_path
query.description: Absolute folder path within the build's test listing. OMIT it (or send blank) to get the paginated ROOT folders with pass/fail roll-ups; provide it to get that folder's details and its immediate sub-folders.

query.name: p
query.description: Page number, used ONLY on the root-folder (no folder_path) branch. Ignored on the sub-folder branch.

query.name: size
query.description: Page size, used ONLY on the root-folder branch. The sub-folder branch ignores it and uses default paging.

query.name: after_key
query.description: Composite-aggregation cursor for the root-folder branch. Ignored on the sub-folder branch. NOTE: the response's `after_key` is returned null even on the root branch (see guidance).

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded.

capabilities.intent: Browse the folder-tree view of a build's test listing: with no folder_path, list the paginated root folders (with pass/fail roll-ups); with a folder_path, get that folder's details and its sub-folders. All the build's test-listing filters apply.
guidance: The response SHAPE depends on the branch. No `folder_path` -> root shape `{project_id, folders[], pagingParams, after_key}`. With `folder_path` -> folder-detail shape `{project_id, name, folder_path, cases_count, total_cases_count, sub_folders_count, sub_folders[], pagingParams}`. Do not expect `folders` on the detail branch or `sub_folders` on the root branch.
There is NO build-not-found guard on this route: an unknown uuid throws an NPE that surfaces as a 500, not a clean 404. Validate the uuid (e.g. via get_build_details) first.

Root-folder pagination is composite-aggregation based; walk it with `pagingParams` (and `after_key`/`p`). Note the top-level `after_key` in the response is set to null even on the root branch — rely on `pagingParams` to page.
Passing a `folder_path` on this route ignores `p`/`size`/`after_key` entirely and returns that folder with default paging.

The full FilterParamsV2 test-listing filter set (status, tags, users, dateRange, isFlaky, ...) is bound from query params and applied to the folder roll-ups; delegates to TestHub's folder-hierarchy API.
A blank/whitespace `folder_path` is treated as 'no path' (root branch); a non-blank but unresolvable path on the detail branch is a 400 'Invalid folder_path'.

capabilities.name: get_build_muted_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the muted-tests tile for a build — how many of the build's tests are muted (with a 'out of total' meta) plus the tile's comment count.
guidance: Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

Same response shape (SingleMetricSummary) as get_build_flaky_stats and get_build_new_failure_stats — only the metric differs. `count` is the muted count; `autoUnmuteCount` is how many are scheduled to auto-unmute.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams.

capabilities.name: get_build_new_failure_stats

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Extra query params outside the FilterParamsV2 fields are collected into a custom-params map and forwarded. Unknown keys are carried, not rejected.

capabilities.intent: Get the new-failures tile for a build — how many tests failed in this build that were not failing before — plus the tile's comment count.
guidance: Plan-locked builds return HTTP 403; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND.
Same response shape (SingleMetricSummary) as get_build_flaky_stats and get_build_muted_stats — only the metric differs. `count` is the new-failure count; `meta` carries the 'out of N' context.
Accepts the full FilterParamsV2 filter set plus arbitrary customParams.

capabilities.name: get_build_non_sdk_test_counts

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: The 40-char build uuid. The counts include the build's split child builds.

capabilities.intent: Get data-hygiene counters for a build (including its split child builds) — how many test runs are untitled, how many are unmarked, and how many have no failure reason — used to nudge non-SDK / untitled instrumentation setup.
guidance: Name-collision trap: this is `/{uuid}/getBuildStats` (data-hygiene counters, action getNonSdkUntitledTestCount). It is NOT the build headline counters — those are `/{uuid}/buildSummary` (get_build_summary_stats).

The body is a JSON *string* (a Gson JsonObject serialised via toString), not a JSON object — the caller must parse the string to read the three keys `untitled_test_count`, `unmarked_test_count`, `missing_failure_reason_count`.
Counts span the parent build AND its split child builds combined; there is no per-leg breakdown here.

capabilities.name: get_build_insights

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID. Looked up group-scoped; an unknown uuid is BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404).

capabilities.intent: One-call failure summary for a build, built for agents and CI bots — status metrics (test vs hook counts), failure categorisation (new failures / always-failing / flaky), defect stats and a top-errors analysis for the run.
guidance: This is the build-keyed sibling of the test-run buildInsights call. Because no test run is supplied, `failureContext` (the file / parent-module drill-down) is ALWAYS null on this route — use the test-run variant if you need it.

`topErrorsAnalysis.status` is one of ANALYSIS_PENDING / ANALYSIS_COMPLETE / ANALYSIS_NOT_STARTED. When it is not COMPLETE, `uniqueErrors` may be empty even though the build has failures — the clustering has not finished, so re-read rather than concluding there are no errors.
`summary.statusMetrics` splits every status into `testsCount` vs `hooksCount`; `summary.totalTests` and `summary.totalHooks` are the run-wide totals.

`topErrorsAnalysis.uniqueErrors[].truncatedError` is only the first ~200 chars of the error — an overview string, not the full message. Carry `clusterId` to the unique-errors endpoints for the full text.
`defectStats` is keyed by issueType, each with per-category failure test/hook counts.

capabilities.name: get_latest_build

query.name: project_name
query.description: Project name (normalised internally). Missing → 400 'Parameter project_name is required'. Resolved within the caller's group.

query.name: build_name
query.description: Exact original build name to match.

query.name: user_name
query.description: Triggering user's username. If it resolves to no user id, the whole call is BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404) — not a validation error.

query.name: build_tags
query.description: Comma-separated build tags; split and trimmed server-side into a tag set.

query.name: framework
query.description: Test framework name; enum-validated. An unrecognised framework is reported as BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404), not a 400.

capabilities.intent: Find the most recent build in a project matching optional filters (build name, triggering user, build tags, framework) and get its full build-details payload — the entry point for 'the latest run of X' when you don't know the build uuid.
guidance: Always returns a SINGLE build (the page limit is fixed at 1), not a list — the newest match. No match for the given filters is BUILD_NOT_FOUND (404).
The requester must hold automated-test-run view permission on the project (service-account project permission is enforced); otherwise the call is refused.

The response shape is feature-flagged per group: the newer build-listing flag returns the V2 build-details envelope, otherwise the v1 one. Both are FURTHER field-gated by the account's plan through the external JsonView wrapper — a field absent from the body may be plan-gated rather than empty, so do not treat a missing field as 'no value'.
Carry the returned `uuid` to the per-build endpoints (insights, reports, history); the display `tcmTestRunIdentifier` is not a build id.

capabilities.name: get_build_nl_automation_agent_report_url

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID. Blank/missing → 400 'Build UUID is required'; unknown uuid → BUILD_ID_NOT_FOUND. Looked up group-scoped.

capabilities.intent: Get a short-lived presigned S3 URL for the natural-language / low-code authoring agent report of a build, so you can download the artifact directly.
guidance: Returns a LINK map `{presignedUrl, expiresAt}`, NOT the report body. Fetch the report yourself from `presignedUrl`; it expires (see `expiresAt`, ISO-8601), so use it promptly and re-request rather than caching it.
Only builds that actually produced an authoring report resolve. If none exists, the presign fails and the call returns the report's not-found error rather than an empty URL.
Requires automated-test-run view permission on the build's project (enforced during presign).

capabilities.name: get_build_self_healing_report_url_via_public_api

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID. Blank/missing → 400 'Build UUID is required'; unknown uuid → BUILD_ID_NOT_FOUND. Looked up group-scoped.

capabilities.intent: Get a short-lived presigned S3 URL for a build's self-healing report — the record of which broken locators the SDK healed during the run.
guidance: Returns a presigned-link map `{presignedUrl, expiresAt}`, NOT the report body. Download the report yourself from `presignedUrl`; it expires (`expiresAt`, ISO-8601).
Only builds whose metadata advertises a self-healing report will resolve; otherwise the presign fails and the report's not-found error is returned.
Requires automated-test-run view permission on the build's project (enforced during presign).

capabilities.name: update_build_metadata_via_public_api

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build UUID to update. Looked up group-scoped.

body.name: build_tags
body.description: List of build tag strings to attach to the build. Send EITHER this or test_plan_id (or both) — a body with neither is rejected with 400 'No parameters provided for update operation'.

body.name: test_plan_id
body.description: Test Management test plan IDENTIFIER (not a numeric id) to link this build to. If the identifier matches no plan, the handler dereferences a null and 500s — verify the plan exists first. Send EITHER this or build_tags (or both).

capabilities.intent: Tag a finished build after the fact from CI and/or link it to a Test Management test plan, so the run shows up under the right plan and tag filters.
guidance: At least one of `build_tags` / `test_plan_id` is REQUIRED — an empty body (or one with only unknown keys) is a 400. Unknown body properties are ignored, not rejected.

Linking a test plan is a cross-service write (TestHub plus the Elasticsearch mirror). A `test_plan_id` that resolves to no plan currently causes a 500 (null dereference), not a clean validation error.
Returns only a success envelope `{success, message}` — it does NOT echo the updated build, so re-read the build to confirm the new tags / plan link.
Requires TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_EDIT permission on the build's project; otherwise 403.
There is no dedicated 'unlink' or 'clear tags' variant here — this call attaches; it does not remove tags or plan links.

capabilities.name: delete_project_builds

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric TRA project id. The project must belong to the caller's group, else PROJECT_ID_NOT_FOUND.

body.name: build_ids
body.description: Build UUIDs to delete. Required and non-empty (@NotEmpty), max 50 entries (@Size max=50). Duplicates are de-duped server-side.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: A build UUID belonging to this project and the caller's group.

capabilities.intent: Bulk-delete up to 50 builds of a project by UUID — retention / cleanup automation over the public REST API.
guidance: IRREVERSIBLE — there is no undo for a deleted build; it also enqueues the archive/delete pipeline that drops the build's test data. Confirm the id list before calling.

All-or-nothing validation runs BEFORE anything is removed: any unknown UUID → BUILD_UUID_NOT_FOUND; a UUID that exists but belongs to another project → 400 'Builds do not belong to project ...'; a non-manual build still in `running` status → 400 'Builds are running and cannot be deleted'.
Requires the BUILD_ARCHIVE permission ('archive_builds') on the project; otherwise 403.

Deletion runs asynchronously downstream (the delete flag is set and the archive pipeline is enqueued) — the 200 `{success:true}` is an acknowledgement that validation passed and the job was dispatched, not proof the builds are already gone.
In the demo-sandbox environment this route returns 404 'NOT FOUND' regardless of the body.
Concurrent archive/delete on the same project is blocked — 'Archiving / Deletion already in progress' (400). Retry rather than treating it as bad input.

capabilities.name: list_project_builds_via_public_api

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric TRA project id.

query.name: unique_build_names
query.description: Filter to these build names.

query.name: build_tags
query.description: Filter to builds carrying any of these tags.

query.name: users
query.description: Triggering user ids (numeric).

query.name: frameworks
query.description: Test framework names; enum-validated. An invalid framework value is a 400.

query.name: teams
query.description: Team ids (numeric).

query.name: build_status
query.description: Build display statuses; enum-validated. An invalid status value is a 400.

query.name: branches
query.description: VCS branch names.

query.name: is_archived
query.description: Restrict to archived (true) or non-archived builds.

query.name: is_ci_run_only
query.description: Restrict to CI-triggered builds.

query.name: exclude_lock
query.description: Exclude locked builds.

query.name: date_range
query.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond values [start, end]. OPTIONAL despite the DTO's @NotNull — this route binds it without validation, so when omitted it DEFAULTS to the last 7 days. Provide both to widen the window.

query.name: next_page
query.description: Opaque base64 pagination cursor from the previous page's `pagination.nextPage`. Omit for the first page.

capabilities.intent: List a project's builds over the public REST API with status, counts and a deep link back to the TRA UI — filterable like the UI build listing (names, users, teams, tags, branches, frameworks, statuses, date range) and cursor-paginated.
guidance: Cursor pagination only: read `pagination.hasNext` and pass `pagination.nextPage` back as `next_page`. There is NO caller-settable page size on this route — the page is fixed at the server default (10 builds); walk the cursor until `hasNext` is false.

The response shape is feature-flagged per group: with the 'new build listing' flag on you get the V2 build items (which carry `workflowStatusStats` and `isManuallyOverridden` instead of v1's `statusStats`), otherwise the v1 items. Same route, so tolerate both item shapes.
When `date_range` is omitted the window is the LAST 7 DAYS — older builds simply will not appear unless you pass an explicit [start,end] in epoch millis.
Builds come back newest-first (the fetched page is reversed before returning).
Requires automated-test-run view permission on the project.
Each build carries an `observabilityUrl` deep link and `tcmTestRunIdentifier`; use `uuid` for follow-up per-build calls.

capabilities.name: bulk_close_builds

path_params.name: normalisedName
path_params.description: Project's normalised name.

body.name: builds
body.description: Explicit build UUIDs to close.

body.name: buildGroups
body.description: Build group ids (numeric) whose builds should be closed.

body.name: selectAll
body.description: Close every build matching `filter`, minus the excluded lists, instead of an explicit id list. When true the target set comes from `filter`.

body.name: excludedBuildUuids
body.description: Build UUIDs to exclude from a `selectAll` close.

body.name: excludedBuildGroupIds
body.description: Build group ids to exclude from a `selectAll` close.

body.name: filter
body.description: GetBuildFilterRqV2 scope for `selectAll` — the same large build filter used by the build listing (statuses, sources, types, users, teams, frameworks, tags, branches, dateRange, search, state, isArchived, ...). Only consulted when `selectAll` is true.

body.name: skipQgRecalculation
body.description: Suppress quality-gate recomputation for the closed builds.

body.name: skipWebhooks
body.description: Suppress outbound webhooks for the closed builds.

capabilities.intent: Mark many running/stale builds as closed in one action — by explicit UUIDs / build groups, or 'select all matching a filter' with exclusions — so a project's listing is not left full of never-finished builds.
guidance: Asynchronous: returns `{success:true, jobId}` immediately — the builds are NOT closed yet. `success` is ALWAYS true (symmetric with bulk-archive); treat the body as an acknowledgement and re-read the listing to confirm, tracking `jobId`.

Two selection modes: an explicit `builds` / `buildGroups` id set, OR `selectAll:true` scoped by `filter` minus `excludedBuildUuids` / `excludedBuildGroupIds`. With `selectAll`, a wrong/empty `filter` changes which builds are closed — scope it deliberately.
Closing is reversible (a build can be reopened), so this is a write, not a destructive delete — no data is removed.
`skipQgRecalculation` and `skipWebhooks` let you suppress quality-gate recomputation and outbound webhooks for the affected builds.
Requires TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_EDIT permission on the project; this is checked in-handler, so a missing permission is an AccessDenied (403). This route does NOT accept username+access-key auth.

capabilities.name: list_project_builds

path_params.name: normalisedName
path_params.description: Project's normalised name.

query.name: statuses
query.description: Build display statuses to include (enum).

query.name: sources
query.description: Product sources (e.g. Automate / App Automate) (enum).

query.name: types
query.description: Build types (enum).

query.name: teams
query.description: Team ids (numeric).

query.name: frameworks
query.description: Test framework names (enum).

query.name: buildTags
query.description: Build tags to filter on.

query.name: branches
query.description: VCS branch names.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond values [start, end] (@Size min=2,max=2).

query.name: search
query.description: Free-text search over builds.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Cursor for the next page (from the previous response's paging params).

query.name: pageLimit
query.description: Page size. Defaults to 10 when omitted. No hard maximum is enforced in this handler — see could_not_determine.

query.name: sortOrder
query.description: Sort direction on the build ordering.

query.name: state
query.description: Build state filter (defaults to `active`).

query.name: isArchived
query.description: Restrict to archived / non-archived builds.

capabilities.intent: The main build-listing endpoint: a filtered, sorted, cursor-paginated page of a project's builds with their status and run counts, for the builds table.
guidance: Takes the project's NORMALISED NAME in the path, not a numeric id. Uses the same large filter object as the build-groups listing.

SIDE EFFECT: this call marks the project as subscribed for the calling user — a read that quietly changes the user's subscription state. It also applies the group's custom data-retention window for the duration of the request, so builds older than the retention window will not appear regardless of `dateRange`.
Cursor pagination via `pagingParams` / `searchAfter`; page through until the paging params report no next cursor. `pageLimit` defaults to 10.
Each build row is a rich BuildSummary (status, statusStats, run/session counts, quality-gate status, tags, etc.), not the trimmed external shape.
This route does NOT accept username+access-key auth (it is not on the /ext/v1 public surface).

capabilities.name: submit_sdk_instrumentation

body.name: (root)
body.description: Arbitrary JSON object — the SDK/CLI instrumentation or error payload. The WHOLE body is stored verbatim as rawData on the emitted event; only the optional top-level `error` string is read out explicitly.

fields.name: error
fields.description: Optional. If present, its text is attached to the event as the error message. Everything else in the object is kept as opaque raw data.

capabilities.intent: Telemetry sink for the BrowserStack SDK/CLI: post the SDK's instrumentation / error payload so it is forwarded as an SDK_CLI_ERROR event (tagged with the caller's user/group) to the data-warehouse pipeline for SDK reliability analysis.
guidance: Returns void — HTTP 200 with an EMPTY body. There is no id, echo or confirmation to read.

Fire-and-forget: the event is dispatched to the EDS pipeline over UDP on a bounded executor, so delivery is best-effort — a full executor SILENTLY DROPS the event with no error to the caller. Do not treat a 200 as proof the event was delivered.
The entire request body is logged at INFO on the server — do not put secrets in the payload.
Authenticated with the customer's BrowserStack username + access key (HTTP Basic) on the /ext/v1 surface.

200.description: Accepted. Empty body (void handler).

capabilities.name: list_running_builds_on_device

query.name: product
query.description: Product; mapped to Automate ('automate') vs App Automate (anything else). Missing/empty → 400.

query.name: os
query.description: Operating system. Missing/empty → 400.

query.name: osVersion
query.description: OS version. A trailing '.0' is also matched without it. Missing/empty → 400.

query.name: device
query.description: Device name. Missing/empty → 400.

capabilities.intent: Show which of the group's builds are currently queued/running on a specific device+OS combination, with the number of parallel sessions each consumes — used to explain why a device tier is saturated.
guidance: All four query params (product, os, osVersion, device) are REQUIRED — any missing/empty one is a 400.
Only counts test runs in `pending` status for the caller's group; a build with no pending runs on that device+OS will not appear.
Returns `{data: []}` (empty list) when nothing matches — that is a normal 'tier not saturated' result, not an error.
Each build in `data` carries `parallelsUsed` — the count of unique parallel sessions that build is consuming on the combination.
This route does NOT accept username+access-key auth.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_user_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List the users to offer in the build-list sidebar's Users facet - the people who actually triggered builds under the current filter, returned as {id, name} and searchable by name.

body.name: projects
body.description: Observability project ids to scope the facet to (array of integers). Omit or send empty to default to the projects of the caller's sub-group.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Observability project id.

body.name: query
body.description: Substring searched against each user's FULL NAME (wrapped as a *query* wildcard inside Elasticsearch); special characters are escaped. Blank/absent returns the top users by build count.

body.name: dateRange
body.description: Optional [startEpochMillis, endEpochMillis] bounding builds by start time. Only projects, query and dateRange from the body affect this route.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Epoch milliseconds; element 0 is the start, element 1 the end.

guidance: POST but read-only - the body is a build filter but nothing is created or changed.

Only `projects`, `query` and `dateRange` from the body affect the result on this route. Every other build-filter field you send (teams, statuses, buildTags, branches, sources, buildIds, ...) is accepted and SILENTLY IGNORED here - it does not narrow the users returned.
Each element is an object {id, name} where `name` is the user's full name - NOT a bare string. `id` is the user id you would pass back as a `users` filter value.
`query` matches the full name as a substring; ids are aggregated from the builds index, then names are resolved from the database.
Results are an unordered, de-duplicated set capped at 100 options. There is no paging on this route, so a filter matching more than 100 users returns only the first 100 the aggregation surfaces.
When `projects` is omitted the scope defaults to the caller's sub-group projects.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_tag_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List build-tag options for the build-list sidebar's Tags facet - the top tags on builds under the current filter, or the tags matching a search string.

body.name: projects
body.description: Observability project ids to scope the facet to (array of integers). Omit or send empty to default to the caller's sub-group projects.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Observability project id.

body.name: query
body.description: Tag search substring (wrapped as *query* wildcard, special chars escaped). Blank/absent switches to the top-tags-by-frequency path instead of a search.

body.name: dateRange
body.description: Optional [startEpochMillis, endEpochMillis] bounding builds by start time.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Epoch milliseconds; element 0 is start, element 1 end.

guidance: POST but read-only - the body is a build filter but nothing is created or changed.

Two different code paths depending on `query`: a blank/absent query returns the top build tags by frequency (terms aggregation), a non-blank query runs a wildcard substring tag search with highlighting. Elements are bare tag strings either way.
Only `projects`, `query` and `dateRange` from the body affect the result. Every other build-filter field in the body is accepted and SILENTLY IGNORED on this route.
Results are an unordered, de-duplicated set capped at 100 options; there is no paging, so more than 100 matches returns only the first 100.
When `projects` is omitted the scope defaults to the caller's sub-group projects.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_team_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List the team options for the build-list sidebar's Teams facet - the BrowserStack teams whose sub-groups own builds under the current filter, returned as {id, name} and optionally filtered by name.

body.name: projects
body.description: Observability project ids to scope the facet to (array of integers). Omit or send empty to default to the caller's sub-group projects.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Observability project id.

body.name: query
body.description: Team-name search substring. NOTE it is applied by the BrowserStack teams service AFTER the sub-group aggregation, not inside Elasticsearch - see guidance.

body.name: dateRange
body.description: Optional [startEpochMillis, endEpochMillis] bounding builds by start time.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Epoch milliseconds; element 0 is start, element 1 end.

guidance: POST but read-only - the body is a build filter but nothing is created or changed.

Two-step and `query` does NOT filter at the Elasticsearch stage: the sub-group ids that own matching builds are aggregated first (capped at 100), then the BrowserStack teams service resolves those ids to team names and applies `query` to the names. So a very large group can have owning sub-groups beyond the 100 aggregated that never appear.
Each element is an object {id, name} (team id + team name) - NOT a bare string. Names come from central/rails team data, not the builds index.
Only `projects`, `query` and `dateRange` from the body affect the result; every other build-filter field is accepted and SILENTLY IGNORED here.
When `projects` is omitted the scope defaults to the caller's sub-group projects.

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_test_case_status_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List the manual test-case status options (Test Management's TestResult custom-field values) configured for the selected projects, to offer manual test-case statuses as a build-list sidebar filter.

body.name: projects
body.description: Observability project ids. The ONLY body field this route reads; they are translated to Test Management project ids before the lookup. Omit/empty to default to the sub-group projects, then to the group's first 100 projects.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: Observability project id.

guidance: POST but read-only. Only `projects` is read - `query`, `dateRange` and every other body field are ignored, and the result is NOT scoped by the current build filter at all; it returns the configured status options for the projects regardless of which builds exist.

Pure pass-through to Test Management's custom-fields API for entity `TestResult`: the response body is the RAW TestHub JSON, not the {data:[...]} envelope the other sidebar facets return. Do not assume a `data` array here.
Observability project ids are converted to Test Management project ids first; a project with no Test Management mapping contributes nothing.
Unlike the other sidebar facets this route is not exposed to public-link tokens.

capabilities.name: list_home_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List the selectable values for one dropdown of the Observability home/overview page's personal filters (build status, product source, framework, build tag, unique build name, or folder).

query.name: key
query.description: Which filter dropdown's values to return. Required - omitting it fails the call. One of the UserFilterKey values.

guidance: `key` is required and must be one of the six UserFilterKey values; a value outside the enum is a 400, and omitting `key` entirely fails the request.
`buildStatus` and `sources` are computed purely from enums with no backend call, so they always return the full option set.

`frameworks` FAILS OPEN: on any internal error (ES or the fence setup) it returns the full hardcoded framework list rather than erroring - so a framework in the list may not correspond to any current build. It also unions in the user's saved framework selection so an aged-out saved value still appears.

The build-backed keys (`buildTags`, `uniqueBuildNames`, `folders`) aggregate Elasticsearch scoped to the caller's sub-group, and to visible projects only when UDAC is enabled, returning up to 10000 values. There is no paging - the whole set comes back in one call.
Each element is {label, value, meta}; `meta` is an empty string on this route.

capabilities.name: get_home_personalization_filters
capabilities.intent: Get the signed-in user's saved home/overview personalization - their sticky filter selections and the isFilteredBuilds / isMyBuilds toggles - so the landing page reopens in the state they left it.
guidance: Per-user, not per-group. A user with nothing saved gets data = {isFilteredBuilds:false, isMyBuilds:true} and no filter selections.
`teams` is stripped out of the saved selections when the group does not have team-based access, even if a value was previously stored.
Errors are swallowed and logged: on failure the response is HTTP 200 with an empty object and NO `data` key. Check that `data` is present before reading it, and do not read its absence as an outage.

Under `data`, each saved filter category (buildTags, projects, uniqueBuildNames, folders, users, teams, sources, buildStatus, frameworks) is a list of {value, label} objects, alongside the two boolean toggles. This is the same shape the save call accepts as its body.

capabilities.name: save_home_personalization_filters
capabilities.intent: Save the signed-in user's home/overview personalization: their filter selections and whether the home page shows filtered builds and/or only their own builds.

query.name: isFilteredBuilds
query.description: Whether the home page shows the user's filtered build set. Optional; only applied when present, so it can be updated without sending a body.

query.name: isMyBuilds
query.description: Whether the home page shows only the user's own builds. Optional; only applied when present.

body.name: buildTags
body.description: Saved build-tag selections. Each element {value, label}.

body.name: projects
body.description: Saved project selections, each {value, label}.

body.name: uniqueBuildNames
body.description: Saved unique-build-name selections, each {value, label}.

body.name: folders
body.description: Saved folder selections, each {value, label}.

body.name: users
body.description: Saved user selections, each {value, label}.

body.name: teams
body.description: Saved team selections, each {value, label}. Defaults to an empty list.

body.name: sources
body.description: Saved product-source selections, each {value, label}. Defaults to an empty list.

body.name: buildStatus
body.description: Saved build-status selections, each {value, label}. Defaults to an empty list.

body.name: frameworks
body.description: Saved framework selections, each {value, label}. Defaults to an empty list.

guidance: Per-user, not per-group. The body is OPTIONAL - send only the `isFilteredBuilds` / `isMyBuilds` query flags to change the toggles without touching the saved filter selections.

When a body IS sent it REPLACES the entire saved filter object (it is not merged), so any category you omit is dropped from the saved set. There is no undo - the previous selection is overwritten and cannot be restored through the API.
A flag omitted from the query is left unchanged (only non-null flags are applied); an omitted body leaves the saved filters unchanged.
Always returns {success:true}, even when only the flags changed.

capabilities.name: list_project_webhook_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List type-ahead/facet values for a project's webhook rule builder (build names, tags, test names, folders, and other trigger-condition fields), with search and cursor paging - the values behind 'fire only when <field> is ...'.

path_params.name: projectName
path_params.description: The project whose values to aggregate. Scope is this project only on this route.

query.name: type
query.description: Which condition field's values to return. The returned set depends ENTIRELY on this. Types qg_status, build_status, smart_tags and alert_severity have no aggregation wired and return empty `data`.

query.name: projectIds
query.description: IGNORED on this route - the scope is the path `projectName` only. Use the group-level webhook filter route to scope by projectIds.

query.name: query
query.description: Case-insensitive substring to filter the returned options (applied after the aggregation).

query.name: afterKey
query.description: Composite-aggregation paging cursor. Pass back the `afterKey` from the previous response to get the next page.

guidance: The value set returned depends entirely on `type`. Only build_name, build_tag, test_name, test_tag, folder, failure_category, alert_name, os, browser, device and test_status are wired; the remaining enum values (qg_status, build_status, smart_tags, alert_severity) return empty `data`.
`projectIds` in the query is IGNORED here - scope is the path `projectName`. This is the opposite of the group-level route, which reads projectIds and ignores any project path.
Cursor-paged via a composite aggregation: read `afterKey` from the response and pass it back as the `afterKey` query param for the next page; a null/absent `afterKey` means the last page.
Per-page size is 10 for most types and up to 1000 for `folder`. `query` and `afterKey` are each capped at 100 characters.
Each element is {label, value, pId, count}. For `folder`, `label` is 'name(count)', `value` is the full path, and `pId` is the parent path; for other types `pId` echoes the value.

capabilities.name: list_group_webhook_filter_options
capabilities.intent: List type-ahead/facet values for the group-level webhook rule builder across selected projects (build names, tags, and the other supported condition fields), with search and cursor paging.

query.name: type
query.description: Which condition field's values to return. The returned set depends ENTIRELY on this. Types qg_status, build_status, smart_tags and alert_severity have no aggregation wired and return empty `data`.

query.name: projectIds
query.description: Comma-separated Test Management project ids to scope the aggregation to; each is translated to a TO project id before the query. A non-numeric entry throws and fails the request; a blank/empty value resolves to no projects and empty `data`.

query.name: query
query.description: Case-insensitive substring to filter the returned options (applied after the aggregation).

query.name: afterKey
query.description: Composite-aggregation paging cursor. Pass back the `afterKey` from the previous response for the next page.

guidance: Gated by a controller-wide entitlement: WEBHOOKS (non-TM groups) or GROUP_WEBHOOKS (TM groups) must be accessible, otherwise the whole controller is refused as feature-inaccessible.

`projectIds` is a comma-separated string of Test Management project ids mapped to TO project ids before the aggregation. A non-numeric entry throws (parse failure) and fails the call; an empty/blank value yields no projects and empty `data`.
The value set returned depends entirely on `type`; qg_status, build_status, smart_tags and alert_severity return empty `data`.

Cursor-paged like the project route: read `afterKey` and pass it back for the next page; null/absent means last page. Per-page size is 10 for most types and up to 1000 for `folder`. `query` and `afterKey` are capped at 100 characters.
Each element is {label, value, pId, count}; for `folder`, `pId` is the parent path and `label` is 'name(count)'.

capabilities.name: list_project_build_names

path_params.name: normalisedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (URL slug). It is URL-decoded and every '+' is turned back into a space before lookup, so a project named 'My App' is addressed as 'My+App'. A name that matches no project returns 404.

capabilities.intent: List the distinct build names seen in a project — the values that populate the build-name filter dropdown on the build listing.
guidance: The 200 body is a bare JSON array of strings (the build names), with no wrapper object — not {success, ...}.
Names are drawn only from builds inside the account's retention window, so a very old build's name may not appear even though the build once existed.
No product-source filter is applied on this route, so names from every source (Automate, App Automate, SDK, etc.) are merged into one list.
The path takes the normalised name, not the numeric project id; '+' in the slug is decoded to a space.

200.description: Distinct build names for the project.

capabilities.name: get_project_non_sdk_summary

path_params.name: normalisedName
path_params.description: The project's normalised name (URL slug); '+' is decoded to a space. Resolved to the project first, so an unknown name returns 404.

query.name: dateRange
query.description: Exactly two epoch-millisecond longs, [lowerBound, upperBound]. OPTIONAL despite the DTO marking it required: when the range (or either bound) is absent the handler substitutes the last 7 days. If you do send it, send both bounds — a one-element range is rejected.

fields.name: lowerBound
fields.description: dateRange[0], epoch millis, inclusive start.

fields.name: upperBound
fields.description: dateRange[1], epoch millis, inclusive end.

capabilities.intent: Get, over a date range, how many of a project's builds were ingested WITHOUT the BrowserStack SDK plus the resulting data-quality gaps (untitled tests, unmarked tests, tests with no failure reason) — the numbers behind the 'switch to the SDK' nudge.
guidance: Elasticsearch-backed and scoped to a date range: with no dateRange it reports the last 7 days, so a zero here can just mean 'nothing in the last week', not 'nothing ever' — use get_project_non_sdk_build_count for the unbounded count.
Deleted and archived builds (and their tests) are excluded from every count, so the numbers track the live project view rather than raw ingest.

The three test-quality counts (unnamedTestCount, unmarkedTestCount, missingFailureReasonCount) come from a separate aggregation over the test index; each is the count of non-SDK tests hitting that gap in the window.
The other QueryRq fields (query, isManuallyOverridden, includeManualRuns) are not consulted on this route — only the date range matters.

200.description: Non-SDK build count and data-quality gap counts for the window.

nonSDKBuildCount.description: Builds in the window ingested without the SDK.

unnamedTestCount.description: Non-SDK tests with no title in the window.

unmarkedTestCount.description: Non-SDK tests left unmarked in the window.

missingFailureReasonCount.description: Non-SDK tests with no failure reason in the window.

capabilities.name: get_project_non_sdk_build_count

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: The observability project id (numeric). Note this route takes the numeric id, not the normalised name that the summary/build-names routes take.

capabilities.intent: Get just the count of non-SDK builds in a project — a cheap, all-time yes/no signal for whether to show SDK-onboarding prompts.
guidance: The 200 body is a JSON STRING, not a JSON object: the payload {"project_id":..,"non_sdk_build_count":..} is serialised to a string and returned as-is, so you must JSON-parse the response body a second time before reading the fields.
Unbounded in time — unlike get_project_non_sdk_summary there is no date range, so this counts every non-SDK build ever (excluding deleted/archived builds).
Keys are snake_case here (project_id, non_sdk_build_count), unlike the camelCase summary route.
The count falls back to 0 rather than erroring when the search returns no total.

200.description: A JSON-encoded STRING of {project_id, non_sdk_build_count}. Parse the string to get the object.

capabilities.name: get_project_by_id_or_name

path_params.name: idOrName
path_params.description: Either the numeric project id OR the (normalised) project name — the handler resolves both. Because this is a catch-all mapping, the literal segments 'lite', 'lite/v2', 'pusherAuth' and any other declared path win first, so you cannot address a project whose name collides with a reserved segment through this route.

capabilities.intent: Fetch one project's full resource representation by either numeric id or normalised name — the project header/settings context (id, name, entry type, configuration, permissions).
guidance: Accepts either the numeric id or the normalised name in the one path segment — carry whichever you have, no separate lookup needed.

configuration.attributes is always present; configuration.subTypes and configuration.alertConfiguration are omitted when null (the DTO is NON_NULL), so treat their absence as 'none configured', not an error.
permissions is a JSON array node reflecting the caller's rights on this project — read it to decide which mutating project actions to offer.

200.description: Single project resource.

attributes.description: Map of project attribute key -> value.

subTypes.description: Map of issue type -> list of issue sub-type resources. Omitted when null.

alertConfiguration.description: Project alert config. Omitted when null.

permissions.description: Caller's permission entries for this project.

capabilities.name: list_projects_full
