capabilities.intent: List the caller's group's projects as full records with complete metadata (attributes, issue types, alerts) — the heavyweight variant to use when you need full project detail rather than a picker payload.
guidance: This is the heaviest of the project-list variants (full entity records, no paging). For pickers, sidebars and dashboards prefer list_projects_lite, list_projects_lite_paginated or list_projects_for_sidebar instead.
The group is taken from the session — there are no parameters; you get exactly the projects the caller's group owns.
The 200 body is a bare JSON array of project objects, with no wrapper and no pagination envelope, so the whole group is returned in one response.

200.description: All of the group's projects as full records.

projectIssueTypes.description: Issue-type rows configured on the project.

alerts.description: Alert rows attached to the project.

capabilities.name: get_default_project

query.name: normalisedName
query.description: Optional. If given and it resolves, that project is returned; if it does not resolve the call silently falls back to the group's most recently updated project rather than 404-ing.

capabilities.intent: Resolve which project the UI should land on: the named project if normalisedName is given and exists, otherwise the group's most recently updated project — for app load and deep links where the named project may no longer exist.
guidance: Fault-tolerant by design: a normalisedName that does not resolve does NOT 404 — it falls back to the last-updated project. So a 200 does not confirm the name you asked for exists; compare the returned normalisedName if you need to know.
If the group has no projects at all, this returns HTTP 200 with a null body (not 404). Guard for a null/empty response.
Returns a single lightweight project object, not a list.

200.description: The resolved landing project (lightweight), or null when the group has no projects.

capabilities.name: list_projects_lite

query.name: th_project_id
query.description: Optional TestHub project id. When present the route SWITCHES BEHAVIOUR: instead of the whole group's list it returns a one-element list containing just that project (looked up by TestHub id). When absent it returns the full lite list for the group.

capabilities.intent: Get a cheap id/name/normalised-name list of the group's projects for pickers and navigation — or, with th_project_id, resolve a single project by its TestHub id (returned as a one-element list).
guidance: Same route, two behaviours: with th_project_id you get a ONE-element list (single-project lookup by TestHub id), without it the whole group's lite list. Either way the body is an array, so a single lookup still comes back wrapped in a list.
Unpaged — the entire group's lite list is returned at once. When you need paging use list_projects_lite_paginated; when you need per-project build activity use list_projects_with_build_aggregates.
Lightweight records only (no attributes/issue-types/alerts); use get_project_by_id_or_name or list_projects_full for full metadata.

200.description: The group's lite project list, or a one-element list when th_project_id is supplied.

capabilities.name: list_projects_with_build_aggregates
capabilities.intent: List the group's projects enriched with per-project build aggregates from Elasticsearch (build count, stability, stability chart, last run) so a landing page can show activity per project without a request each.
guidance: Not a drop-in for list_projects_lite: it runs Elasticsearch aggregations over all of the group's builds, so it is considerably more expensive — use it only when you actually need the per-project activity numbers.
Only projects with at least one build are returned — projects with buildCount 0 are dropped from the list, so the count here can be smaller than the plain lite list.
Unpaged: the whole (filtered) group is returned in one array. For a paged version of the same shape use list_projects_with_build_aggregates_paginated.
Applies product-source fencing, and outside TM also the manually-overridden filter, so counts reflect the caller's product context rather than raw totals.

200.description: Projects (with at least one build) plus their build aggregates.

capabilities.name: rename_project

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: The observability project id to rename.

body.name: name
body.description: The new project name. Trimmed server-side; a blank or whitespace-only name is rejected with 400 ('Project name cannot be empty.'). Sent flat at the top level of the body.

capabilities.intent: Rename a project — use this to change a project's display name (and, as a side effect, its URL slug).
guidance: Renaming CHANGES THE URL SLUG: the new normalised name becomes the project's slug, so existing links and any saved normalisedName keyed on the old name stop resolving. There is no automatic redirect — update stored slugs from the returned normalisedName.
No true undo: to reverse it you must rename back to the old name, and links broken in the meantime are not restored — treat it as a write with no history.
Blocked in demo-sandbox environments: returns 400 'Cannot rename default project' there.
The rename happens in TestHub and is mirrored locally; TestHub's own 400/401/404 are translated into observability errors, so a 404 here can mean TestHub could not find the project.
The 200 body carries a human-readable message and the new normalisedName — read normalisedName, not the message, to rebuild links.

200.description: Rename succeeded.

capabilities.name: assign_issue_types_to_test_runs

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Project id scoping the test runs. Despite the project-scoped path this call updates TEST RUNS, not the project. In TM the id is interpreted as a TestHub project id.

body.name: issues
body.description: The list of (test run -> issue type) assignments to apply. Sent flat at the top level as 'issues'.

fields.name: testRunId
fields.description: The test run's integer id to categorise. The wire key is 'testRunId' — a plain 'id' will not bind.

fields.name: issueTypeId
fields.description: The issue-type / failure-category id to assign. The wire key is 'issueTypeId' — not 'issueType'.

capabilities.intent: Bulk-assign a failure category / issue type to a list of test runs (the 'mark failure reason' action on the failure-analysis screens) and get back how many rows were updated.
guidance: Despite the action's project-scoped path and 'updateProject'-style naming, this updates TEST RUNS — it does not modify the project itself.
Each item's wire keys are testRunId and issueTypeId; a body using id/issueType (the shape some callers assume) silently fails to bind those fields. Send exactly testRunId and issueTypeId.
Reversible: re-run with a different issueTypeId to re-categorise, so this is a write, not destructive. There is no per-call undo, though.
Rejected with 400 while a project archive is in progress — retry after the archive completes rather than treating it as bad input.
The 200 body is just {updatedCount}: the number of test-run rows actually changed. A count lower than the number you sent means some ids did not match — it is not an error.

200.description: Count of test runs updated.

updatedCount.description: Number of test-run rows whose issue type was updated.

capabilities.name: list_projects_for_sidebar

body.name: queryStr
body.description: Optional name search. Filters the page by project name substring.

body.name: projects
body.description: Optional list of selected project ids (Long) to PIN into the result, so the currently selected project(s) appear even if they would fall outside the page. Nulls in the list are dropped.

fields.name: (item)
fields.description: A selected project id to include.

body.name: pageNumber
body.description: 1-based page number. Values <= 0 (and absent) default to 1.

capabilities.intent: Populate the build-list sidebar project picker: a page of lightweight project records for the group ordered by most recent build activity, with optional name search and the ability to pin the currently selected project ids into the page.
guidance: POST but READ-ONLY — the body is only search/paging/selection state; nothing is mutated.

hasNext is inferred from 'the page came back non-empty', so the last full page still reports has_next=true and next_page = pageNumber+1; the empty page after it is how you learn you are past the end. Stop when data is empty, not when has_next flips.
Page size is fixed server-side at 10 records and cannot be changed from the request.
Pagination keys are snake_case here (has_next, next_page under pagingParams) — different from the GET lite/aggregate routes which use hasNext/searchAfter.

Each row is the sidebar-lite shape (thProjectId, id, displayName, normalisedName) — note displayName, not name. This is distinct from list_projects_lite_paginated (a GET with offset paging and no id-pinning).

200.description: A page of sidebar-lite projects plus pagination.

has_next.description: True whenever the page was non-empty; not a true 'more rows exist' signal.

next_page.description: pageNumber+1 as a string, or null when has_next is false.

capabilities.name: list_projects_lite_paginated

query.name: search
query.description: Optional project-name search.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: Despite the cursor-style name this is a PLAIN OFFSET (integer). Defaults to 1 when absent. In demo-sandbox environments it is forced to 0. Advance it using the value returned in pagingParams.searchAfter.

query.name: nextRoot
query.description: Optional JSON-map cursor param carried through PagingParams; effectively inert on this offset-paged route — paging is driven by searchAfter.

capabilities.intent: Get a paginated, optionally name-searched list of the group's projects in lightweight form (id, name, normalised name, TestHub id) for pickers and listing pages that do not need per-project metrics.
guidance: searchAfter is an OFFSET, not a cursor — the name is misleading. Page by reading pagingParams.searchAfter back into the next request; hasNext is computed by over-fetching one row.
Page size is hardcoded at 100 and cannot be changed.
In demo-sandbox environments the offset is forced to 0, so you always get the first page there regardless of searchAfter.
Ordered by most recent build activity (build_updated_at desc). The 200 wraps the rows under projectLiteList with pagingParams alongside — not a bare array.
Overlaps heavily with list_projects_for_sidebar (POST /api/v2/projects/lite): that one pins selected ids and pages at size 10; this one does neither and pages at 100.

200.description: A page of lite projects plus pagination.

searchAfter.description: The offset to send as searchAfter on the next request.

capabilities.name: list_projects_with_build_aggregates_paginated

query.name: search
query.description: Optional project-name search.

query.name: searchAfter
query.description: A PLAIN OFFSET (integer) despite the cursor-style name. Defaults to 1 when absent; forced to 0 in demo-sandbox. Advance using pagingParams.searchAfter from the response.

query.name: nextRoot
query.description: Optional JSON-map cursor param carried through PagingParams; effectively inert on this offset-paged route.

capabilities.intent: Back the Projects landing page: the same paginated project list as the lite paginated variant but enriched with per-project build aggregates (build counts/status roll-ups, stability) from Elasticsearch, so each project card can show its health at a glance.
guidance: Heavier than list_projects_lite_paginated because it runs an aggregate pass over builds for the page — use it only when you need the per-project numbers.

Same paging quirks as the lite paginated route: searchAfter is an offset (not a cursor), page size is hardcoded at 100, hasNext is computed by over-fetching one row, and the offset is forced to 0 in demo-sandbox.
When the project page is empty the response still returns 200 with an empty projectWithAggregates list (no aggregate pass is run).
The 200 wraps rows under projectWithAggregates with pagingParams alongside — not a bare array.

200.description: A page of projects with build aggregates plus pagination.

searchAfter.description: The offset to send as searchAfter on the next request.

capabilities.name: get_general_settings
capabilities.intent: Read a project's general settings block by normalized name — the misc project-level toggles on the Settings > General tab (build inactivity timeout, hooks visibility).
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; scoped to the caller's group.
Path takes the project's NORMALIZED NAME (slug), not the numeric id.
The body is a FLAT untyped map of setting-key -> string value, with every expected key present (defaults filled in when the project has never set them) — so a value is never missing, only defaulted.

General keys are `buildTimeout` (build inactivity timeout, in SECONDS as a string; default 3600) and `hooksVisibility` (one of all/failed/beforeFailed/none; default failed). All values are strings even when they represent a number or boolean.
Feed the same key/value pairs back to update_general_settings to change them.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: get_rerun_settings
capabilities.intent: Read a project's re-run configuration by normalized name — how re-running failed tests from a report is wired up for this project.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; scoped to the caller's group. Path takes the project's normalized name.
The body is a FLAT untyped map of setting-key -> string value, with defaults filled in for keys the project never set.
Re-run keys are `reRunViaCli` (default "true") and `reRunViaDashboard` (default "false") — booleans serialized as strings.
Feed the same key/value pairs back to update_rerun_settings to change them.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: get_testhash_settings
capabilities.intent: Read a project's test-hash (test identity) configuration by normalized name — which platform attributes are combined to decide that two executions are 'the same test' across builds.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; scoped to the caller's group. Path takes the project's normalized name.
The body is a FLAT untyped map of the five attribute keys -> string value: `device`, `browser`, `browserVersion`, `os`, `osVersion`.

Each value is one of `consider`, `ignore` or `regex`. On THIS read, any key the project never set is returned as `consider` (the read forces that default for testhash specifically), not the attribute's own stored default.
Feed the same key/value pairs back to update_testhash_settings — which requires ALL FIVE keys to be present.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: list_failure_category_sub_types
capabilities.intent: List a project's custom failure sub-categories by normalized name — the user-defined issue sub-types (with parent category and colour) used when triaging a failed test.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; scoped to the caller's group. Path takes the project's normalized name.

Results are under `data`, a MAP keyed by parent failure-category (e.g. productBug) -> list of sub-categories. When the project has NO custom sub-categories, `data` is `null` (not an empty object or `{}`) — check for null before iterating.
Only project-custom sub-types are returned; built-in/predefined issue types are filtered out.

Each sub-type's `id` is the STRING locator — that is the value update_failure_category_sub_type and the sub-category DELETE take as `id`. Each also carries `name`, `color` and its parent `category` key.
This is the newer normalized-name surface; the numeric-projectId settings read bundles sub-types differently (see get_project_settings_by_integer_id).

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: get_failure_category_display_names
capabilities.intent: Read a project's custom labels for the built-in failure categories, so the UI can show the org's own wording instead of the default category names.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; scoped to the caller's group. Path takes the project's normalized name.
Results are a list under `data`, one row per built-in failure category (only the default categories, not custom sub-types).
`displayName` FALLS BACK to `name` when the project has set no override — it is never blank, so you cannot tell 'no override' from 'override equal to the default name' from this field alone.
Each row's `issueTypeId` (numeric) is what update_failure_category_display_names takes to rename that category; `name` is the built-in default label.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: list_project_alerts
capabilities.intent: List a project's configured alerts by normalized name — the rules (thresholds per severity level) and the notification channels each one fires to, for the Settings > Alerts tab.
guidance: Ungated read — no permission check; the project is resolved by normalized name within the caller's group.

Results are under `data`, a MAP keyed by alert-type (buildStability / buildPerformance / flakinessPercentage / mutedDays / numberOfAlwaysFailingTests / spanOfAlwaysFailingTests) -> list of alerts. When the project has no alerts, `data` is ABSENT from the body entirely (an empty object), not an empty map.
Each alert is the SAME shape create_project_alert / update_project_alert take, plus the alert's stored integer `id`. Carry that `id` into update_project_alert's body to edit it.
`alertRules` is a map keyed by severity level (CRITICAL / WARNING) -> {value, condition}; `notificationRules` maps notifier type (SLACK / EMAIL) -> channel-key -> notifier mappings.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

capabilities.name: preview_auto_close
capabilities.intent: Before saving an auto-close threshold, find out how many currently-open runs that threshold would close and when the next auto-close sweep is scheduled — the info banner in the settings panel.
guidance: Read-only (no state change), but DELIBERATELY GATED on the same write permission as the auto-close PUT — hasProjectPermission(PROJECT_SETTING_GENERAL, 'modify_project_settings'); 403 otherwise. It is the feature's heaviest query, so it is not reachable with mere project visibility (unlike the other settings reads here).
`thresholdDays` is REQUIRED as a query param and must be one of 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 180, 240, 360 — anything else is a 400.
The count is bounded: `openRunsToClose` is capped at 200 and `capped:true` means the real number is higher (the value shown is a floor).

DEGRADED PATH: the query runs on a bounded executor with a ~350ms budget. On timeout, pool saturation or an upstream error it still returns 200 but with ONLY `thresholdDays` and `nextRunAt` — `openRunsToClose` and `capped` are omitted. Treat a missing count as 'unknown', never as zero.

`nextRunAt` is epoch MILLIS (accounts for the 7-day grace window after enabling), and may be null if the sweep cron is unusable. Note the unit differs from get_auto_close_settings' `enabledAt`, which is epoch seconds.

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

query.name: thresholdDays
query.description: Candidate staleness threshold in days to preview. Required; must be one of the allowed values or the call is a 400.

capabilities.name: update_general_settings
capabilities.intent: Save changes to a project's general settings toggles (build inactivity timeout, hooks visibility) by normalized name.
guidance: Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_GENERAL permission ('modify_project_settings'), checked in-handler against the project's TestHub id — 403 otherwise. Path takes the project's normalized name.
Body is a FLAT map of setting-key -> string value (no wrapper object). Send only the keys you want to change.

UNRECOGNISED KEYS ARE SILENTLY IGNORED — only known setting keys are applied, with no error for the rest, so a mis-typed key is a 200 that changes nothing. Known keys: `hooksVisibility` (all/failed/beforeFailed/none) and `buildTimeout` (seconds).
An invalid VALUE for a known key IS rejected with 400 'Invalid value for setting: <key>'.

This route shares the generic settings handler with update_auto_analyser_settings and the pattern-analysis update — nothing constrains which keys may be sent on which route; the key/value pairs, not the route, decide what changes.
Sending the `autoClose` key here is rejected with 400 — auto-close must go through update_auto_close_settings.
Returns {success:true}. Reversible: re-send the prior values to roll back (settings keep no version history, so read them first if you need the old values).

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project's normalized name (slug).

body.name: hooksVisibility
body.description: Hooks visibility toggle. Sent as a top-level key in the flat map body.

body.name: buildTimeout
body.description: Build inactivity timeout in SECONDS, as a string. Sent as a top-level key in the flat map body.

capabilities.name: update_auto_analyser_settings

capabilities.intent: Rename, recolour or re-parent an existing custom failure sub-category in a project's triage taxonomy, by normalized name.
guidance: Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission ('modify_project_settings'), checked in-handler — 403 otherwise. Path takes the project's normalized name.

capabilities.name: update_project_alert
capabilities.intent: Update an existing project alert's rules, notification mappings, build-name scope or enabled flag, by the project's normalized name.
guidance: Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_ALERTS permission ('modify_project_settings'), checked in-handler — 403 otherwise. Path takes the project's normalized name.

COLLECTION-LEVEL PUT: the alert to edit is identified by the body's `id`, NOT a path segment — unlike the alert DELETE which takes /{id}. Omitting `id` is a 400 'Please specify alert Id'; an id that is not an alert of this project is a 400 'Alert '<id>' not found. Did you use correct alert ID?'.

VERSIONED UPDATE: this disables the old alert row and creates a NEW one, so the returned `id` (a STRING) is the NEW alert's id — NOT the id you sent. Carry the returned id forward for any subsequent edit/delete.

`name` is required and non-empty. `alertType` is effectively required and must be one of buildStability / buildPerformance / flakinessPercentage / mutedDays / numberOfAlwaysFailingTests / spanOfAlwaysFailingTests — an unknown or omitted alertType fails as a 500, not a clean 400.

`alertRules` is a MAP keyed by severity level (CRITICAL / WARNING) -> {value (1–32 chars), condition (<=32 chars)}. This differs from the older numeric-id surface, where alertRules is a flat set with the level as a field.
Build scoping is `buildNames` (PLURAL); `alertType` is a string (not the older integer `alertTypeId`). To edit by numeric project id use update_project_alert_by_integer_id.
Returns 200 {success:true, id:'<new alert id>'}.

capabilities.name: update_auto_close_settings
capabilities.intent: Enable the auto-close policy for a project at a chosen staleness threshold, or disable it — after which a background sweep closes runs left open longer than the threshold. By normalized name.
guidance: Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_GENERAL permission ('modify_project_settings'), checked in-handler — 403 otherwise. Path takes the project's normalized name.

`enabled` is required. When `enabled=true`, `thresholdDays` is required and must be one of 15, 30, 45, 60, 90, 180, 240, 360 — otherwise 400 'thresholdDays is required when enabling' / 'thresholdDays must be one of [...]'.

`enabled=false` DELETES the stored policy attribute rather than storing a disabled flag, and returns just {enabled:false}. Re-enabling recreates it (recoverable), which is why this is a write, not destructive.

This call does NOT close anything itself: enabling anchors a 7-day GRACE window at the enable time, and a background sweep closes stale runs later, asynchronously. Use preview_auto_close first to see how many runs a threshold would affect.

On enable the response carries `enabledAt` (epoch SECONDS, the grace-window anchor) and `projectsConfigured` (how many projects were configured — 1 for this per-project call). `projectsConfigured` is only populated on a write.

body.name: thresholdDays
body.description: Staleness threshold in days. Required when enabled=true, must be one of the allowed values; ignored when enabled=false.

capabilities.name: get_test_runs_history_details
capabilities.intent: For a batch of test runs (or hook runs), get each one's execution history across previous builds together with its logs and failure/issue-type info — the data behind the test details 'history' panel, used to judge flakiness and whether a failure is new.

body.name: testRunIds
body.description: Integer ids of the test runs to fetch history for. When `isHook` is true these are HOOK run ids, resolved against a different backing store — mixing test-run and hook-run ids in one call returns history for whichever set matches the `isHook` flag.

fields.name: item
fields.description: A test run id (or hook run id when isHook=true).

body.name: isHook
body.description: Routes the whole request. false (default) treats `testRunIds` as test run ids via the test-run service; true reinterprets them as hook run ids and resolves them through the hook-run service instead. Bound from the JSON key `isHook` exactly (a differently cased key is ignored and defaults to false).

guidance: This is a POST that only carries a filter body — it reads and changes nothing (routed to a read replica), so it is safe to call freely.

`isHook: true` switches the ENTIRE lookup to hook runs: the ids you send are then hook run ids, not test run ids. Sending test run ids with isHook=true returns history for the hook runs (if any) with those ids, not your tests.

The response is a JSON OBJECT keyed by the id you asked for (`{ "<id>": {…history…} }`), not an array. An id with no history is simply absent from the map — iterate the ids you sent rather than assuming every one comes back.

Each entry's `logs` is an object with only the keys that exist for that run: `TEST_FAILURE` (backtrace), `TEST_LOG` (an array of screenshot/attachment URLs the caller fetches directly from storage), and `BROWSERSTACK_ERROR`. All three are omitted when absent.
Scoped to the caller's group in the repository query — ids outside the caller's group are dropped from the result, not errored.

capabilities.name: get_test_run_retry_logs

path_params.description: Declared in the route but NOT read by the handler — any value satisfies routing; the run is located by testRunUuid alone.

path_params.description: UUID of the retry attempt / test run whose evidence to fetch. This route keys off the UUID, unlike the sibling /testRuns/{testRunId} routes which take the numeric id. A malformed UUID throws before any lookup.

capabilities.intent: Get the screenshot/log attachment structure captured for a single retry attempt of a test, so the retries tab can render that attempt's evidence.
guidance: Identify the run by UUID here — the numeric id that the other /testRuns/{…} endpoints take will not resolve on this route.

The response is a log-structure object with only the keys that exist: `TEST_FAILURE` (failure backtrace), `TEST_LOG` (an array of screenshot URLs — fetch each from storage yourself; they are not proxied through this API), and `BROWSERSTACK_ERROR`. An attempt with no captured evidence throws `IllegalArgumentException("retry doesn't exist")` rather than returning an empty object, so treat that error as 'no screenshot data', not a missing run.
Reads through the group-scoped repository factory, so a run in another group behaves as absent.

query.name: cursor
query.description: Opaque forward cursor — pass back `cursorInfo.nextCursor` from the previous page. Omit it for the first page; the per-build `totalAttachments` count is computed ONLY on that first (cursor-absent) page and is absent on later pages.

capabilities.intent: Page through the test runs in a build that have SDK-captured logs/attachments, with the per-build attachment total — backs the build's log/attachment viewer.
guidance: Page size is fixed at 15 and cannot be changed; walk pages by feeding `cursorInfo.nextCursor` back as `cursor` until `cursorInfo.hasMore` is false.
`totalAttachments` is returned only on the first page (when `cursor` is omitted). Read it there and carry it; do not expect it on subsequent pages.
Each row's `url` is a direct attachment/log URL fetched from storage, not through this API. `attachmentsCount` and `screenshotsCount` are per-test-run totals.
Path variable is named buildId but is bound to the build UUID string — sending a numeric id yields BUILD_NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.name: assign_test_run_failure_categories

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: A PROJECT id, despite the /builds/ route prefix. Interpreted per product: when the caller's CAD product is TM it is a TestHub project id and mapped to the observability project; otherwise it is the observability project id directly.

body.name: issues
body.description: The per-run category assignments to apply. Required and validated (@NotNull); each item is validated too.

fields.name: testRunId
fields.description: Id of the test run to categorise. Bound from the JSON key `testRunId` (maps to the internal `id`); required per item.

fields.name: issueTypeId
fields.description: Id of the issue type / sub-type to assign to that run. Required per item.

capabilities.intent: Bulk-assign failure categories (issue types / sub-types) to a set of test runs — the 'categorise these failures' action on the test listing; returns the resulting issue types.
guidance: Requires the BUILD_UPDATE_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission on the (resolved) project; otherwise AccessDenied. The path id is a project id, not a build id — do not pass a build id.
This overwrites each run's current category; there is no version history, so the previous category is not recoverable through this API. Read the runs first if you need to record what they were.
A 409 (AUTO_ANALYSIS_IN_PROGRESS) means auto-analysis is running — it is SAFE to retry, because the whole batch is validated up front and nothing is written until it passes, so a 409 wrote nothing.
The whole batch is pre-checked before any write, so an invalid item fails the entire request rather than partially applying.
Response is a flat array of the resulting IssueType objects, not a per-run map.

path_params.description: Declared in the route but NOT read by the handler; the run is located by testRunId alone within the caller's group.

path_params.description: Numeric id of the test run to mute/unmute. Looked up group-scoped (findByIdForGroup).

query.name: mute
query.description: true mutes, false unmutes. Declared Optional in code but effectively required: a missing value returns 400 'mute param missing' (and emits a MUTE_TEST_UPDATE_FAIL error event). Muting is plan-gated (the MUTE feature must be accessible, else FORBIDDEN_OPERATION); UNmuting (false) is never gated.

body.name: unmuteConditionConfig
body.description: Optional auto-unmute condition; the whole body defaults to empty (manual unmute only) when omitted. Unknown top-level keys are ignored. Only meaningful when mute=true.

fields.name: unmuteType
fields.description: Auto-unmute strategy; defaults to MANUAL when the body/config is absent.

fields.description: Auto-unmute once the test passes/stabilises this many runs.

fields.description: Auto-unmute after this many days.

fields.description: Status the run must reach to count toward auto-unmute.

fields.name: notifyUsers
fields.description: User ids to notify on auto-unmute.

fields.name: expiry
fields.description: Expiry time in epoch milliseconds.

capabilities.intent: Mute or unmute a test run so its failures stop (or resume) counting towards build status and alerts, optionally with an auto-unmute condition (e.g. unmute after it passes N times).
guidance: `mute` is a QUERY parameter, not a body field, and is effectively mandatory — omitting it returns 400 'mute param missing' even though the code marks it Optional.
This is reversible: call again with mute=false (or configure an auto-unmute condition) to restore the run. There is no separate undo endpoint.
Muting requires the MUTE plan feature; without it you get FORBIDDEN_OPERATION / plan-feature-not-allowed. Unmuting is always allowed.
The auto-unmute config rides inside `unmuteConditionConfig`; the request body is optional and defaults to a manual (no auto-unmute) config. It only applies when muting.
Success returns `{"success": true}` — a JSON object, even though the handler's return type is a string.

guidance: Identical tree to list_build_test_runs_hierarchy (same underlying query) with two deliberate differences: this route does NOT read the Public-Link-Token / X-Public-Link-Token headers, and it does NOT collect arbitrary query params as custom filters. Prefer this only for internal/session views; use the public-link-aware twin for shared reports.
Because it ignores the public-link headers, a public-link caller hitting this route is NOT given the pending/in-progress suppression — do not use it to serve shared/public reports.
Only the declared query params are honoured here; unknown params are dropped rather than forwarded.
Paging is by top-level ROOT nodes (5 per page, or 1 for builds over 2000 runs); walk `pagingParams` (nextRoot + searchAfter). `showRunCount` is forced false outside the demo sandbox.

capabilities.name: list_build_test_run_counts

path_params.name: buildId
path_params.description: The build UUID, resolved by (uuid, groupId). BUILD_NOT_FOUND if not in the caller's group.

capabilities.intent: For every unique test in a build (keyed by test hash), get how many times it ran across the build and its re-runs, and whether those runs spanned different platforms — what the UI uses for rerun/retry badges.
guidance: Returns per-test rows under a top-level `data` array (`{testHash, count, isDifferentPlatformsUsed}`), NOT a single total. Sum `count` yourself if you need a build total.
Counts are aggregated over the PARENT build id, so a re-run chain (a build and its re-runs) is counted as one build, not per re-run.
`isDifferentPlatformsUsed` is true when the run count for that test hash spanned more than one platform.

capabilities.name: trigger_build_rerun

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid to re-run.

query.name: type
query.description: What to re-run: the whole build, all failed tests, or one test. An unrecognised value is NOT a 400 — it returns HTTP 200 with {created:false} and nothing is triggered, so check `created`, not the status code.

query.name: testId
query.description: Required only when type=TEST — the test whose file is re-run. When type=TEST and this is omitted the call returns 200 {created:false} and does nothing (no error).

capabilities.intent: Trigger a re-run of a build — the whole build, all its failed tests, or one test — in the customer's CI (Jenkins, Azure DevOps/Pipelines, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, CircleCI) or directly on App-Automate for eligible Maestro builds; if the CI cannot be reached the call hands back the CI URL and credentials so the frontend can trigger it instead.
guidance: This is a GET that mutates the outside world — it calls the customer's CI and starts a real build. Do not treat it as a safe read.

Plan-gated: without the RERUN plan feature it is 403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED. It also requires the re_run_tests (BUILD_RERUN_TESTS) permission on the build's project, else 403 AccessDenied — auth alone is not enough.
Refused (400) if the build is already archived or already closed.
Success path returns 200 {created:true}; the Maestro/App-Automate direct path returns created:true with username/authToken/paramUrl/buildUrl all null.

Fallback path: when the CI is unreachable or the trigger fails you get 200 {created:false} but WITH username, authToken, paramUrl and buildUrl populated — that is the signal for the caller to trigger the CI itself, not an error. The body carries CI credentials.
CI_NOT_CONFIGURED / CI_PARAMS_NOT_FOUND are thrown (not created:false) when the CI integration is missing or the build has no stored re-run params.
testOpsParams is always {BROWSERSTACK_RERUN_TESTS:<files|null>, BROWSERSTACK_RERUN:"true"}.

capabilities.name: get_build_self_healing_report_url

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid.

capabilities.intent: Get the download URL for a build's self-healing report — the artefact listing the selectors that were auto-healed during the run — plus whether the group uses the Authoring Agent and its healing quota.
guidance: Returns a presigned, EXPIRING S3 URL (presignedUrl + expiresAt), NOT the report body — fetch the artefact yourself from that URL before it expires.
Check availability first via the build detail read's showHealingReport flag; when no report bucket is on the build this throws not-found rather than returning an empty URL.
healingQuota (cap + usage) is best-effort — it is silently omitted when the product/CAD lookup or the quota service fails, so its absence does not mean zero.
groupUsesAuthoring is present on this internal route only; the public self-healing report route does not include it.
In the demo-sandbox environment this returns canned data, not a real presigned URL.

capabilities.name: get_build_smart_test_selection_report

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid.

query.name: tab
query.description: Which test set to page through: 'acted-on' (default) vs not-acted-on. The `tests` array returned is scoped to this tab.

query.name: page
query.description: 1-based page number.

query.name: size
query.description: Page size. Forwarded to the backing TCS service uncapped — no server-side ceiling is enforced here.

capabilities.intent: Get the Smart Test Selection report for a build — which tests the selection model recommended to run or skip and what the pipeline actually did — as a paginated, tabbed listing for the AI reports section.
guidance: Feature-flagged per group via a Redis set: a disabled group always gets a 'not-run' status envelope, NOT an error — read `status`, do not assume failure.
status is one of not-run | pending | ready | partial | failed | awaiting-execution | no-report; terminal statuses (not-run, pending, failed) return a minimal envelope with most fields absent.
Response is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL): null fields are omitted, so treat an absent field as 'not applicable' rather than missing data.
Paginate with page over the current `tab`; the next page is pagination.nextPage (null on the last page). Switching tab restarts paging.
Demo-sandbox serves canned data only for the seeded 'Regression #376' build.
Backed by a live TCS round-trip, so a slow/absent TCS surfaces as a failed/partial status rather than a 500.

capabilities.name: get_build_top_error_stats

path_params.name: buildUuid
path_params.description: Build uuid.

query.name: filter
query.description: FilterParamsV2 listing-filter set (statuses, frameworks, tags, date range, search, etc.) bound from flat query params; the panel is computed over the tests these match.

query.name: customParams
query.description: Any extra query params are collected verbatim into a custom-params map and folded into the filter.

capabilities.intent: Get the 'Top unique errors' insight panel for a build — the most frequent error clusters with their test-run counts, respecting the active listing filters.
guidance: Handle the not-ready state: while the auto-analyser is still running you get ready:false with only a `message` ('Unique Errors are being detected') and the default 'Analysis yet to run' overview — not an error and not the final data.
While clustering is incomplete the panel comes back with an empty `data` set; poll again rather than concluding there are no errors.
`data` is sorted by count descending; each row carries the cluster id, title (the error), count, impactedTests and the contributing testRuns.
Build lookup is group-scoped, so a build uuid from another group reads as not found.

capabilities.name: mark_build_rerun_expected

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid — used only to resolve the build's NAME; the flag is keyed on the name, not this uuid.

capabilities.intent: Mark a build name as 'a re-run is expected' so the next incoming build with that name is linked as a re-run rather than treated as a fresh build.
guidance: No request body is read — the uuid in the path is the only input.

Sets a Redis flag keyed on the build NAME (<buildName>_RERUN) with a 1-hour (3600s) TTL, so the linking window closes after an hour and the flag applies to any build sharing that name, not just this uuid.
Returns the plain string 'Saved!' (not JSON).
An unknown uuid throws a raw IllegalArgumentException ('launch doesn't exist') rather than a structured 404.

capabilities.name: recalculate_build_quality_gate

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid.

body.name: close
body.description: Part of the RecalculateQGBody shape; effectively ignored on this route — the handler forces the recalculation branch regardless.

body.name: reCalculateQG
body.description: Ignored — the handler forces reCalculateQG=true. The body must be PRESENT (a valid RecalculateQGBody), but its contents do not change behaviour; unknown keys are ignored.

capabilities.intent: Re-run the quality-gate evaluation for a build (e.g. after profile rules or a status override changed) — use after quality-gate inputs change to refresh the build's gate result.
guidance: Asynchronous: responds immediately with 200 {message:'Quality Gate result will be available after recalculation finishes'} — the result is NOT ready yet. Poll the build's quality-gate summary read for the outcome.
This OVERWRITES the build's previous quality-gate result; there is no undo for the prior result.
A request body must be sent (an object; {} is fine) even though its fields are ignored — the handler forces the recalculation.
403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when the build is plan-locked.

capabilities.name: stop_build

body.name: build_uuid
body.description: Uuid of the build to stop. Missing/empty is a 400 'Build UUID is required.'

capabilities.intent: Stop an in-progress build — all of its running sessions — from the build view.
guidance: Stopping is NOT reversible — a stopped build cannot be resumed. Classified write (the build record survives), but warn the user there is no undo.
Resolves the build's product from the DB and proxies the stop to Automate / App-Automate; Espresso builds take a dedicated app-automate stop-by-uuid path and are then marked stopped locally.
Build lookup is group-scoped, so a foreign uuid will not stop a build.
Failures come back as a classified structured error body (with an errorTraceId), never a bare 500; the 200 body is the upstream stop response passed through.

capabilities.name: update_build_metadata

path_params.name: uuid
path_params.description: Build uuid.

body.name: name
body.description: New build name. Applied ONLY when the build's creationType is MANUAL; for SDK/CI builds the rename is silently ignored and the call still returns 200.

body.name: tags
body.description: Replacement tag list (REPLACES all existing tags, not merged). Max 50 tags; each tag non-blank and ≤ 100 chars.

fields.name: tag
fields.description: A single tag; must be non-blank and at most 100 characters.

capabilities.intent: Rename a build and/or replace its tags — the 'edit build' action on the build page — writing the change through to TestHub.
guidance: Success is an empty 200 body — there is nothing to read back; re-read the build to confirm the change.
Rename only takes effect for MANUAL builds; for SDK/CI-created builds the name is left unchanged and you still get 200, so verify rather than trusting the status.
Tags are replaced WHOLESALE, not merged — send the full desired list. To keep existing tags, read them first and include them.
If neither name nor tags is set the call is a no-op 200.
403 PLAN_FEATURE_NOT_ALLOWED when the build is plan-locked; unexpected failures return a bare 500 with no body.

capabilities.name: resolve_build_uuid_from_identifiers

query.name: creationType
query.description: Build.CreationTypeEnum. AUTOMATION uses the name/serial identifiers below; any other (manual/TCM) type uses ONLY tcmTestRunId and ignores the name/serial params.

query.name: buildNormalisedName
query.description: Normalised build name (AUTOMATION path).

query.name: projectNormalisedName
query.description: Project normalised name (AUTOMATION path); pair with buildNormalisedName + buildSerialId.

query.name: buildSerialId
query.description: Per-project sequential build number (AUTOMATION path). On a serial-id collision the first match wins (logged).

query.name: tcmTestRunId
query.description: TCM test-run id — the only identifier used for non-AUTOMATION creation types.

query.name: thProjectId
query.description: TestHub project id, an alternative to projectNormalisedName for scoping the AUTOMATION lookup.

capabilities.intent: Resolve a build UUID from human/CI-facing identifiers — project name (or TestHub project id) + build name + serial id for automation builds, or a TCM test-run id for manual/TCM runs — so a caller can deep-link to a build without already knowing its uuid.
guidance: No match returns HTTP 200 {uuid:null} — NOT a 404. Check the uuid value, not the status code.
For non-AUTOMATION creation types only tcmTestRunId is consulted; buildNormalisedName / projectNormalisedName / buildSerialId are ignored on that path.
Serial-id collisions are possible — the first matching build wins (a pager marker is logged).

capabilities.name: list_sidebar_build_runs

body.name: projects
body.description: Project ids to scope to. When null and UDAC is on, the accessible project list is resolved for the caller's sub-group.

body.name: query
body.description: Free-text search over build names/identifiers.

body.name: afterKey
body.description: Forward cursor — pass the response's pagingParams.afterKey to page down.

body.name: beforeKey
body.description: Backward cursor — pass the response's pagingParams.beforeKey to page up.

body.name: selectedBuildUuid
body.description: Centre the returned window on this build (roughly half a page above it, the rest below) so a deep-linked build appears in context.

body.name: includeManualRuns
body.description: Include manual/TCM runs in the listing (default true).

body.name: isManuallyOverridden
body.description: Optional filter on the manual-override flag.

body.name: buildNames
body.description: Part of the inherited GetBuildFilterRqV2 filter surface: build-name filter. The body also accepts users, teams, frameworks, statuses, sources, tags, branches, dateRange, search, etc.

body.name: isArchived
body.description: Filter to archived vs live builds (inherited filter field).

capabilities.intent: List a page of unique build runs for the build sidebar/list rail, matching a large filter body, with bidirectional cursor paging and optional centring on a deep-linked build.
guidance: POST but a pure READ — the body is a filter; nothing is written.

Page size is fixed server-side (BUILDS_PAGESIZE); it is NOT caller-controllable, so there is no page-size body field. Page with the afterKey/beforeKey cursors from pagingParams (hasNext/hasPrev tell you when to stop).
Honours UDAC project scoping: with projects null and UDAC on, only the caller's accessible projects are returned.
Each row's usageQuotaStatus splits retention-accessible builds from 'pro quota' ones — a build can appear but be gated by quota.
Use selectedBuildUuid to keep a deep-linked build visible in the window rather than paging to find it.

capabilities.name: delete_build_via_public_api

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build uuid to delete.

capabilities.intent: Delete a build and all of its test data from the project (archive-with-delete) — for pruning runs via the public API.
guidance: Irreversible: the build and all its test data are removed. Refused at the consent gate.
Requires the archive_builds (BUILD_ARCHIVE) permission on the build's project — a valid username/access key is NOT sufficient (403 otherwise).
Refused with 400 if the build is still 'running' and was not manually created.
Build lookup is group-scoped, so a build uuid from another group returns 404.

Deletion is delegated to the archive-builds path with isDelete=true and processed ASYNCHRONOUSLY downstream — the 200 {success:true} is an acknowledgement that removal was queued (child builds are pulled in too), not confirmation it has completed.
In the demo-sandbox environment this returns HTTP 404 with body 'NOT FOUND'.

capabilities.name: generate_build_report_via_public_api

body.name: requestingCi
body.description: The CI requesting the report (e.g. the Jenkins plugin). Missing → error.

body.name: requestType
body.description: FIRST for the initial request, POLL for follow-ups. An unknown value raises a 400 'Invalid request_type'. Missing → error.

body.name: reportFormat
body.description: List of requested report formats. Missing → error.

body.name: buildUuid
body.description: Resolve the build directly by uuid. Provide this OR originalBuildName + buildStartedAt.

body.name: originalBuildName
body.description: Resolve the build by name together with buildStartedAt when the uuid is not known.

body.name: buildStartedAt
body.description: Build start time in epoch milliseconds; pairs with originalBuildName for resolution.

body.name: userTimeout
body.description: Caller's overall timeout budget, used to bound the polling protocol.

capabilities.intent: Ask for a build's summary report in the requested formats — the CI-plugin endpoint. It is a polling protocol: the first request usually returns IN_PROGRESS with the retry count and interval to use, and later poll requests return the finished report once the build's data has settled.
guidance: Polling contract, not a single call: on reportStatus IN_PROGRESS you also get retryCount and pollingInterval — wait that interval and POST again with requestType=POLL until reportStatus is COMPLETED/TEST_AVAILABLE (or NOT_AVAILABLE/DATA_NOT_AVAILABLE).
Body is an untyped map validated by hand: requestingCi, requestType and reportFormat are each required and their absence is a distinct error; an unknown requestType is a 400.
Resolve the build by buildUuid, OR by originalBuildName + buildStartedAt. If the resolved build row is missing you get a 200 with a NULL body — handle that as 'not found', not a report.
The report itself (report.richHtml/richCss/basicHtml/plainText) is only populated on the terminal statuses; the envelope is @JsonInclude(NON_NULL) so absent fields are omitted.
In the demo-sandbox environment this returns HTTP 404 with body 'NOT FOUND'.

capabilities.name: get_build_details_via_public_api

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build uuid. A re-run uuid resolves through its parent, so you get the parent build's aggregate.

capabilities.intent: Get the full public build record for one build uuid — identity and naming, resolved status, duration, timestamps, owner, framework/SDK metadata, per-status test counts, alerts, re-run stats and top-error insights — the payload CI plugins and API consumers report on.
guidance: Enforces the TEST_RUN_AUTOMATED_VIEW service-account project permission on the build's project.
Passing a re-run uuid returns the PARENT build's aggregate, not the re-run's own numbers.
A build in 'deleted' state raises BUILD_ID_DELETED, not a plain 404 — distinguish 'deleted' from 'never existed'.
The response SHAPE is feature-flagged: when new build listing is enabled it is the V2 build-details shape, otherwise the legacy one — do not hard-code one envelope.
Pro-only fields (smart_tags, unique_errors, failure_categories, alerts) are stripped by JsonView for non-pro plans, so their absence reflects the plan, not the build.

capabilities.name: get_build_history_via_public_api

path_params.name: build_id
path_params.description: Build uuid the history is anchored on.

query.name: limit
query.description: How many builds to return (this build plus prior runs of the same name). Silently CLAMPED to 1..10 — asking for more than 10 is ignored, not an error.

capabilities.intent: Get the trend context for a build for an automated failure agent — this build plus up to N earlier runs of the same build name, newest first, each with number, status, timings and a pass/fail/skip plus defect-type count summary.
guidance: Not a general history read — distinct from the internal build-history capability: this is the agent-facing trend view with per-build defect and status counts.
limit is clamped server-side to 1..10; there is no paging beyond 10 runs.
Only the anchor build and EARLIER runs of the same name are returned; later runs of the same name are filtered out. The anchor build is flagged current:true.
Build lookup is group-scoped (the IDOR gate), so a foreign uuid is not found.

Per-build counts (statusStats + defectStats: automation bug / product bug / to-be-investigated / not-determined / environment issue) come from a single Elasticsearch aggregation; per-entity recurrence (flaky/theme names) is intentionally not included.

capabilities.name: delete_comment

path_params.name: normalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalized name. Resolved to the project, but the delete itself is NOT scoped by it (see guidance).

path_params.name: commentId
path_params.description: The comment's id (the search-index document id returned when the comment was created/listed).

query.name: createdAt
query.description: Comment's creation timestamp as an ISO-8601 offset date-time (e.g. 2024-05-01T10:20:30+00:00). Required in practice: the handler parses it unconditionally and errors if it is absent. A space before the zone offset is tolerated (it is converted to '+'). Its year/month are computed but not used to locate the doc, so an approximate value still works as long as it parses.

capabilities.intent: Delete one of your OWN comments from a build or test discussion — use to retract review feedback or a note you left.
guidance: OWN-COMMENT ONLY: the delete matches on the comment id AND your own user id, so another user's comment (even with a valid id) is treated as not-found and left untouched. There is no admin override on this route.
Plan-gated on the COMMENTS feature: a workspace without it is refused with a forbidden error before anything is deleted.

`createdAt` is a REQUIRED query param even though it does not narrow the target — omit it and the request fails while parsing it (no comment is deleted). Pass the comment's own createdAt as an ISO-8601 offset timestamp.
Irreversible: the comment is removed from the comment search index with no undo and no version history; a matching notification-log entry for it is cleared too.
Returns the literal JSON string "deleted". A comment that is missing, already deleted, or not yours comes back as not-found (COMMENT_NOT_FOUND).

capabilities.name: delete_project_alert_by_integer_id

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Numeric project id.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Numeric alert id.

capabilities.intent: Delete an alert rule from a project so it stops firing notifications — the form addressed by the numeric project id.
guidance: This is a SOFT delete: the alert row is not physically removed — it is disabled and retired (enabled=false, latest=false) so it stops firing and disappears from the active alert list. Classed as `write` because the record survives, but there is NO API to re-enable it, so treat it as effectively permanent.
Its notifier mappings ARE hard-removed as part of the delete, so re-creating the alert later also means re-adding all of its recipients; use create_project_alert_by_integer_id to make a fresh one.
Path takes the INTEGER project id and the numeric alert id. An alert whose id does not belong to this project, or an unknown id, returns not-found.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_ALERTS permission on the project; otherwise forbidden.
Returns {message: "Alert delete operation completed successfully."}.

capabilities.name: delete_project_alert

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalized name.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Numeric alert id — numeric even though the project is addressed by its normalized name.

capabilities.intent: Delete an alert rule from a project so it stops firing notifications — the form addressed by the project's normalized name.
guidance: Same underlying operation as delete_project_alert_by_integer_id: a SOFT delete that disables and retires the alert (record survives) and hard-removes its notifier mappings. Classed `write`, but there is no re-enable endpoint, so treat it as permanent and recreate with create_project_alert if needed.
The {id} segment is the numeric alert id; only the project is addressed by normalized name.
Permission is checked in-handler: PROJECT_SETTING_ALERTS with modify_project_settings on the project; a caller without it gets a 403.
Returns {success: true} (the SettingsResponseV2 `id` field is null here and omitted).

capabilities.name: delete_failure_category_sub_type_by_integer_id

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Numeric project id.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: Numeric issue sub-type id.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a custom failure-category sub-type from a project — the form addressed by the numeric project id and numeric sub-type id.
guidance: HARD delete with reclassification: every test run currently classified with this sub-type is first moved to the group's DEFAULT issue type, then the sub-type row is deleted and the search index updated. Both the removal and the reclassification are irreversible.
Only custom sub-types owned by your group can be removed; predefined/global issue types are refused with a forbidden error.
Path takes the INTEGER project id and the numeric sub-type id. An id not present in the project, or belonging to another group, returns not-found.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES permission on the project.
Returns {message: "Issue sub-type delete operation completed successfully."}.

capabilities.name: delete_failure_category_sub_type

path_params.name: projectNormalizedName
path_params.description: Project normalized name.

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The sub-category's LOCATOR string (not the numeric id). This surface resolves the sub-type by locator, not by primary key.

capabilities.intent: Permanently delete a custom failure sub-category from a project's triage taxonomy — the form addressed by the project's normalized name.
guidance: DOES NOT take a numeric id: the {id} segment here is the sub-category's LOCATOR string. Passing the numeric id that delete_failure_category_sub_type_by_integer_id uses will resolve by locator and return not-found — use the numeric form for numeric ids.

Same hard delete + reclassification as the numeric form: test runs classified with this sub-category are moved to the default issue type, then the record is removed; irreversible. Predefined global types cannot be deleted.
Permission is checked in-handler: PROJECT_SETTING_FAILURE_CATEGORIES with modify_project_settings on the project; otherwise 403.
Returns {success: true} (SettingsResponseV2 with `id` null and omitted).

capabilities.name: delete_notification_subscriptions

path_params.name: projectId
path_params.description: Project id. With source=TO this is the observability/TO project id; with source=TCM it is a TCM project id that is converted to its linked TO project before the delete.

query.name: source
query.description: Selects the id space of {projectId} and the permission-check path. TO (default) uses the project id directly; TCM treats {projectId} as a TCM project id and resolves its linked TO project first (400/not-found if none is linked).

body.name: notifications
body.description: The subscriptions to remove. Each item identifies ONE notifier-to-target mapping; ids live here in the body, not in the path.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The notification-mapping id to delete (the id of the build-insight or alert notification subscription).

fields.name: notifierType
fields.description: Which notifier channel the subscription is for. Matched case-insensitively.

fields.name: notificationType
fields.description: The subscription kind. Only ALERTS and BUILD_INSIGHTS have a delete path; any other value (DAILY_SUMMARY / WEEKLY_SUMMARY / TEST_FAILURE, or an unknown token) falls through to not-found. Matched case-insensitively.

capabilities.intent: Remove notification subscriptions in bulk — stop a specific email or Slack notifier from being notified about a given build name (build-insights) or alert.
guidance: DELETE with a request BODY: the targets are in `notifications`, not the URL. Each item needs all three of id, notifierType and notificationType — all are mandatory and a missing one is a 400.

NO transaction across items: the list is processed one-by-one, so a failure part-way through leaves the earlier deletions applied. Re-read the project's notifications afterwards to see what actually remains.
Each item is validated against the project and the caller's group/user; a mapping in another project or group, or an id that does not exist, fails that item with not-found.
Hard delete of the subscription mapping row — no undo. Recreate it with add_notification_recipients if removed by mistake.
Permission PROJECT_SETTING_NOTIFICATIONS (modify_project_settings) is enforced for this non-GET route before the handler runs; the check uses the TCM or TO branch according to `source`.
Returns {message: "Notification deleted"} — a single acknowledgement regardless of how many items were removed, so do not read the count from it.

capabilities.name: delete_slack_notifiers
capabilities.intent: Disconnect Slack for the entire group — delete EVERY Slack notifier configured across all of the group's projects in a single call.
guidance: GROUP-WIDE WIPE with NO scoping: there is no id, project, or channel parameter and no request body — it removes ALL Slack-type notifiers for the caller's whole group at once, so every project loses its Slack build and alert notifications together. Confirm intent before calling.
The group is taken from the authenticated session; nothing is passed in.
Irreversible: the notifier rows are hard-deleted, so reconnecting Slack means recreating every configuration by hand.
Requires the PROJECT_SETTING_NOTIFICATIONS permission (modify_project_settings), checked at group level.
Returns {message: "Deleted slack notifiers"}.

ErrorResponse.description: Standard TRA error body built by GlobalExceptionHandler.

errorTraceId.description: UUID correlating the error to server logs.

message.description: Human-readable error message; for relayed TestHub errors this is the upstream message.

code.description: Application/TestHub error code. Present on many 4xx; absent on generic 500s.

classification.description: Blame classification when stamped, e.g. USER_ISSUE. Never present on /ext responses.

OperationCompletion.description: Short completion acknowledgement; NON_NULL serialization so typically only message appears.

BuildGroupAggResult.description: One build-group aggregation row in a grouped build listing (summary for the group's latest build). Stub pending the build_group entity.

SourceFencingFlags.description: Cross-source feature-fencing flags; embedded in many widget/build responses. A true flag means results for that product were skipped for this caller.

prev.description: Previous page number, null on the first page.

next.description: Next page number, null on the last page.

CITrigger.description: A CI trigger as returned to the client (CITriggerDto). Never carries the stored Jenkins/auth token values — only booleans indicating whether they are set.

uuid.description: The trigger id used in all trigger paths.

ciTool.description: jenkins, gitlab_ci, github_actions, circleci, travis_ci, bitbucket_pipelines, azure_devops, buildkite, teamcity or custom (unrecognised values may also be stored).

webhookUrl.description: May still contain unresolved [SECRET] placeholders as stored.

hasJenkinsApiToken.description: True when a Jenkins API token is stored. The token value itself is never returned.

hasAuthToken.description: True when an auth token is stored. The token value itself is never returned.

enabled.description: A disabled trigger cannot be fired.

httpMethod.description: Custom-tool only; null for built-in tools.

requestHeaders.description: Custom-tool only; a JSON object encoded as a string; null for built-in tools.

requestBody.description: Custom-tool only; null for built-in tools.

contentType.description: Custom-tool only; null for built-in tools.

userId.description: The owning user's id; only the owner may edit or delete.

CITriggerSecret.description: A CI-trigger secret as returned to the client (CITriggerSecretDto). The stored value is write-only and is never included.

uuid.description: The secret id used in secret paths.

name.description: UPPER_SNAKE token that triggers reference as [NAME].

userId.description: The owning user's id; only the owner may edit or delete.

usedInTriggers.description: Names of the triggers in the group whose URL, headers or body contain this secret's [NAME] placeholder.

IntegrationScore.description: An org's integration health score row, keyed by group id.

score.description: Weighted health score across the categories.

preferences.description: Parsed per-category preference breakdown; null until first calculated.

IntegrationScorePreferences.description: Per-category integration preferences. Each category object carries only its own boolean signals plus an optional notApplicable reason (and, for the build categories, cannotIntegrate/otherReason).

lastCalculated.description: Unix epoch millis of the last recalculation.

bStackBuilds.description: {totalBuilds, bStackSdkBuilds, isAutomate, isAppAutomate, cannotIntegrate?, notApplicable?, otherReason?}

UserIntegrationCredential.description: A user's stored integration credential. authToken is returned DECODED to plaintext and is a secret.

authToken.description: Auth token in plaintext (decoded from the base64-at-rest value).

EmailTypePreferenceV1.description: Legacy per-type email preference: subscription flag plus the projects the type applies to.

projects.description: Project ids this type applies to; empty for types other than daily-summary and build-finish.

EmailTypePreferenceV2.description: Newer per-type email preference: subscription flag plus configured rule count. Null fields are omitted.

ruleCount.description: Number of configured notification rules for this type.

IntegrationNotificationPreference.description: Per-project notification preference for one type, with resolved project name and the individual rules. Null fields are omitted.

IntegrationNotificationLineItem.description: One notification rule line: a named build/alert scope with its enabled flag and id.

name.description: Build name or alert name; 'All' for the catch-all alert scope.

id.description: Notification row id (null on create/edit input).

all.description: Subscribed to all builds/alerts. Serialized from the internal isAll flag.

allEnabledCondition.description: The trigger condition applied when `all` is true (JSON; e.g. ["all"] or an array of statuses/levels).

enabled.description: Whether this section is switched on.

BuildNameNotificationMapping.description: A per-build-name build-insight subscription. Nulls omitted (JsonInclude NON_NULL).

condition.description: JSON array of build statuses that trigger the insight.

AlertNotificationMapping.description: A per-alert subscription. Nulls omitted (JsonInclude NON_NULL).

alertName.description: Alert display name (transient; may be null).

condition.description: JSON array of alert levels (or ["all"]) that trigger the notification.

alertId.description: The project alert this subscription targets.

BuildInsightNotification.description: Build-insight section: a NotificationItem plus per-build-name specifics. `allSpecifics` is not serialized.

AlertsNotification.description: Alert section: a NotificationItem plus per-alert specifics. `allSpecifics` is not serialized.

NotificationSummary.description: One notifier's full subscription config. Wire keys: dailySummary, buildInsights, alerts, testFailure.

NotificationSummaryResponseRow.description: One recipient row in the project notification-settings summary.

name.description: Email name, or Slack channel (team) id for Slack rows.

description.description: Email address, or Slack channel visibility for Slack rows.

buildInsights.description: Count of specific build-insight subscriptions, or -1 for 'all builds'.

alerts.description: Count of specific alert subscriptions, or -1 for 'all alerts'.

userId.description: Populated for EMAIL rows only; null for Slack.

NotificationPreferenceResponse.description: Recipient list for one channel plus the channel's overall enabled flag.

NotificationLogDto.description: One home-feed notification log entry. Unknown props ignored on parse.

projectName.description: Resolved project name; null if lookup missed.

normalisedName.description: Resolved normalised name; null if lookup missed.

NotificationLogsResponse.description: Home notification feed page. data and pagingParams are both null when the feature is disabled for the group.

hasNext.description: Only true while offset <= 40 (feed capped near 50 entries).

BuildAggregate.description: Run counts by status for one build name.

BuildSummary.description: Full build summary used in daily-summary email bodies.

BuildAggregateV2.description: Top failed build entry, optionally enriched with best-effort AI summaries (omitted when null).

aiRcaSummary.description: Best-effort; may be absent if enrichment failed.

IssueTypeSummary.description: Failure-category counts (pb=Product Bug, tbi=To be Investigated, ei=Environment Issue, ab=Automation Bug, nd=No Defect).

filterQueries.description: Fixed canned query strings (dateFilter, buildRuns, topFailedBuilds, failedTests, issueTypes) used to deep-link filtered views.

notificationType.description: Map of attribute name -> boolean for this user.

QualityProfile.description: A quality-gate profile: a named rule set plus the build filters it applies to. Serialized with null fields omitted (JSON include NON_NULL). Note the @JsonProperty renames: the wire fields are `isGlobalProfile` (internal isRootProfile) and `applicableBuilds` (internal buildFilters).

id.description: Internal DB id; changes on every edit because an edit writes a new version row.

uuid.description: Public profile identifier. NOTE: a new UUID is minted on every edit, so it is not stable across updates.

ruleStatus.description: 'pass' = profile passes only when all rules hold; 'fail' = profile fails when any rule holds.

applicableBuilds.description: Wire name for the internal buildFilters.

isGlobalProfile.description: Wire name for the internal isRootProfile. True = applies group-wide.

isLatest.description: Whether this is the current version of the profile; a retired/deleted version has this false.

QualityProfileRule.description: One rule inside a quality profile. Serialized with null fields omitted.

id.description: Client-generated rule UUID; required on write.

RuleLHS.description: Left-hand side of a rule. Null fields omitted.

helperConfig.description: Scoping for SELECTED_* rules: {regex, testTags[], folders[], alert}.

with.description: Operand (test status, smart tag, failure-category key, ...).

displayWith.description: Human display name for a failure-category operand; populated only on the single-profile detail reads for FAILURE_CATEGORY / FAILURE_CATEGORY_THRESHOLD rules.

RuleRHS.description: Right-hand side / threshold of a rule. Null fields omitted.

BuildFilter.description: Which builds a profile is evaluated against.

allBuilds.description: Required. True = every build; otherwise scope with buildNames/buildTags.

QualityProfileLiteDto.description: Compact profile row in the settings/list response.

QualityGateResponse.description: A project's quality-gate settings: the project-level switches plus the profiles mapped to it.

enabled.description: Whether Quality Gates is on for the project (from a project attribute).

shouldOverrideBuildStatus.description: Whether a failing gate also marks the build failed (from a project attribute).

qualityProfiles.description: Default profile sorted to the front.

QualityProfileResultStats.description: Per-status rule counts for a profile on a build.

QualityProfileResultLiteDto.description: Per-profile result summary for a build.

QualityGateSummary.description: Readiness-aware build gate summary. Exactly one of qgResult / message / state is populated per response.

message.description: Present instead of results when the build is pending or the auto-analyser is still running.

state.description: A cached evaluation state string, present instead of results/message when one is cached.

QualityProfileRuleResult.description: One rule's outcome for a build in the profile detail drawer.

ruleStatus.description: Per-build status of this rule (e.g. running/passed/failed).

ruleResult.description: Rendered result/value for this rule on the build.

QualityRuleResult.description: One rule's evaluated result inside the CI quality-gate result. Null fields omitted.

QualityProfiles.description: A profile block inside the CI quality-gate result.

ExtQualityGateResult.description: CI-facing quality gate result for a build. Serialized with null fields omitted (JSON include NON_NULL), so while running only build_uuid/status/quality_gate_result appear.

build_url.description: Deep link to the build in the product; absent while the build is still running.

quality_gate_result.description: While running, a human 'try again' message; once done, the same value as status.

FilterStruct.description: One filter value option for the quality-profile filter builder.

displayName.description: Present only when set (JSON include NON_NULL).

QGFilterResponseData.description: Filter values for the quality-profile filter builder, with a cursor.

afterKey.description: Cursor to pass back as `afterKey` for the next page; null/absent when no more values.

query.description: Echo of the search prefix used.

TrendTimelineDataPoint.description: One point of a Testing Trends timeline series. `y` is the serialised metric value (derived from the internal string value; null when the bucket had no runs). `t` is the total unique tests in the bucket (present on the percent-timeline cards, null elsewhere). `pointRange` is [bucketStart, bucketStart+interval] epoch ms and is omitted on some series (e.g. performance-chart lineData).

y.description: Metric value for the bucket (count, percentage or duration depending on the card). Null when no tests ran in the bucket.

t.description: Total unique tests in the bucket; set only on the flakiness/new-failures/always-failing/test-growth/test-executions cards, null otherwise.

pointRange.description: [bucketStart, bucketEnd] epoch ms. Absent on series that do not emit it (e.g. performance-chart lineData).

TrendInsight.description: Headline card summary. Fields are computed on serialisation: `count` is the headline number as a STRING (a percentage for flakiness/new-failures/always-failing, a raw total for test-executions); `meta` is a human sentence ('N of M unique tests are <metric>') or null; `metric` is the metric label or null.

metric.description: Metric label (e.g. 'flaky', 'new failures'); null when not applicable.

meta.description: Human summary sentence; null when there is no metric.

count.description: Headline value as a string - a percentage (one decimal) for the gated cards, or a raw count for test-executions.

PercentTimelineCard.description: Standard Testing Trends card: a timeline series plus an optional headline insight. `insights` is null on the test-growth card.

FailureCategorySeries.description: One defect/failure category with its own timeline.

color.description: Display colour from the group's defect-type mapping.

data.description: Per-bucket counts. Each point's y is null when no tests ran in that bucket (distinct from 0 failures).

y.description: Failure count in the bucket; null when the bucket had no runs.

CbtDataPoint.description: A cross-browser coverage slice. Primary (top-level) points carry name/value/percentage/drilldown/color; secondary (drill-down) points additionally carry os/browser/device.

value.description: Raw execution count for the slice.

percentage.description: Share as a formatted string (two decimals).

drilldown.description: Key linking a primary slice to its drill-down entry; null on secondary points.

StabilityLeaderboardRow.description: One build's row in the stability leaderboard.

id.description: Row id: "all" for the project-wide row, otherwise "buildName-<name>".

percentage.description: Pass-rate / stability percentage as a formatted string (one decimal).

buildName.description: Build name, or "All" for the project-wide row.

chartData.description: Per-bucket pass-rate series; entries may be null for empty buckets.

PerformanceLeaderboardRow.description: One build's row in the performance leaderboard.

avgDuration.description: Average execution duration over the window.

lineChartData.description: Per-bucket test COUNTS (null for empty buckets).

barChartData.description: Per-bucket average DURATIONS (null for empty buckets).

TrendPagingParams.description: Fixed-page pagination echo. Note the leaderboards nest this under the key `pagingParam` (singular) while recent-runs uses `pagingParams` (plural).

pageNumber.description: One-based page number just returned (the requested zero-based pageNumber + 1).

id.description: Positional index into the list, NOT a build id.

runs.description: Number of runs of this build name in the window.

TrendBuildSummary.description: Standard build summary as used by the recent-runs picker. Large object; the salient fields are listed. Serialised with default (nulls included) inclusion; vcsInfo is write-only and not returned.

statusStats.description: Aggregated pass/fail counts for the build.

GroupUser.description: A user in a BrowserStack group as Test Observability returns it. Minimal profile: only id, email and display name.

email.description: User email. Blanked to an empty string on the group-users listings when the request carries a public-link token; never blanked on the sub-group listing.

full_name.description: Display name. Serialised as `full_name` (accepts `fullName`/`full_name` on the way in).

BrowserstackTeam.description: A BrowserStack team within a group.

UserPagingParams.description: Cursor pagination metadata for the searchable group-users listing. Absent when the backend returned no paging info (e.g. last/only page).

hasNext.description: True when another page is available.

searchAfter.description: Cursor to pass back as the `searchAfter` query param for the next page.
