Fetching an RCA is get-or-create by default: asking for one that does not exist yet creates the record and queues a generation, so the plain fetch is NOT a safe read. There is a separate pure-read that never has side effects, and a peek option on the public route.

Both fetch and trigger need the caller's own BrowserStack username and Selenium access key; these are resolved server-side from the caller's user record, and a caller whose record lacks them is refused before the AI pipeline runs.

The feature is gated three ways: the group must have accepted the AI opt-in consent, the group's plan/AI token must carry the RCA feature, and the build's source must not be fenced off — any of these missing turns every RCA call into a refusal rather than a result.
There is no version history for an RCA: a fresh generation overwrites the stored analysis for that test run, and the previous one is gone.
The completed analysis body is opaque model output whose internal shape can change; treat it as display content rather than parsing fixed fields out of it.

The analysis is written back by the AI service itself through an ingestion callback; a user-facing caller normally only reads it or triggers it, and the reading side reflects whatever the service last wrote.

build_group.title: Build group (run group)
build_group.description: A named grouping of builds within a project, used to collect the builds of one release or test cycle.
build_group.id_convention: Plain integer build-group id, discovered from the group listing. Note: the project id in these paths is the TestHub project id, not the observability project id.

relations.via: builds are linked into a group (a build belongs to at most one group)

key_facts: Groups live in TestHub; this service is a pass-through that mirrors what TestHub returns, so writes here take effect in TestHub and are not undoable from this API.
A group has a name (required, up to 255 chars) and an optional description (up to 1000 chars); the name 'Ungrouped' is reserved and rejected.
A group's state is derived: it reads ACTIVE until it is closed, then CLOSED. Closing freezes the group's builds and test runs (they become non-editable / locked) but deletes no data.
Deleting a group removes the group and its build associations but never the underlying builds; the builds are detached asynchronously afterwards, so they may still show the group for a short window.

Bulk actions across many builds and the group delete both flip to asynchronous background work above a size threshold, returning an acknowledgement rather than a finished result — re-read to confirm the outcome.
Only one bulk action can run per project at a time: while one is in flight a second is refused, and the caller should retry rather than treat it as bad input.

The permission to add builds to a run group governs creating, editing, deleting and closing a group; the bulk-action operations are gated per action instead (linking needs that same run-group permission, while assigning a test plan or an assignee needs the automated-run edit permission).

accessibility.title: Accessibility (a11y) data
accessibility.description: Accessibility scan results for a build's and a test run's tests, plus the group's a11y plan and free-trial entitlement.
accessibility.id_convention: No id of its own: build-level a11y is addressed by the build UUID; test-run-level a11y is addressed by the TestHub build-test-case-execution-result (btcer) id, a plain integer. Plan/trial reads take no id and use the session's group/user.

relations.via: a11y test-run listing scoped by build UUID
per-test a11y detail by btcer id

key_facts: For groups on the App-Accessibility feature, an accessibility read whose build/test source is the App-Accessibility automation source is proxied to a separate Accessibility service and comes back in that service's shape, not the shape assembled here — the same route can therefore return two different bodies depending on the group flag and the source.

Several a11y reads are thin pass-throughs to a separate Accessibility service; on an upstream parse failure they return a plain text error body with a 500 status instead of the usual structured error envelope.
Severity of accessibility issues is always broken down into the four buckets critical, serious, moderate and minor.
Starting the accessibility free trial is a state change on the Accessibility product's entitlement even though it reads like a details fetch; checking trial status is a plain read.
The build must have finished (or timed out) and actually carry accessibility data, otherwise the a11y test-run listing returns a typed 4xx rather than an empty list.
Tests with no accessibility summary are silently dropped from the build's a11y listing, so its rows can be fewer than the build's total tests.
